 Read `median_us` (each replay is already the max over ranks).
 
+## Kernel breakdown
+
+Add `--profile-dir DIR` to see where the time goes. After timing, each case is
+replayed 3 more times under `torch.profiler`; every rank writes
+`DIR/<case>.rank<r>.kernels.json` (GPU time per kernel per forward, sorted)
+and `DIR/<case>.rank<r>.trace.json.gz` (open in Perfetto). Rank 0's top
+kernels are printed and included in `--output-json`.
+
+```bash
+python -m vllm.benchmarks.forward.profile DIR/decode.rank0.kernels.json
+# Before/after a change, same case: per-kernel deltas, largest first.
+python -m vllm.benchmarks.forward.profile base/decode.rank0.kernels.json new/decode.rank0.kernels.json
+```
+
+- Kernels are grouped by name without template or function arguments; the
+  JSON keeps one full name per group in `example`.
+- Only the timed forward is included: the in-graph KV restore and rank
+  rendezvous are excluded (`pre_forward_us`). `span_us` (first to last
+  forward kernel) should be close to `median_us`, a bit higher from profiler
+  overhead; `busy_us` can exceed it when streams overlap.
+- Compare the same rank across runs: under EP, ranks differ (e.g. collective
+  wait time shows up inside communication kernels).
+
+For Nsight Systems (NVTX, NCCL, CPU side, GPU metrics), skip `--profile-dir`:
+the two can't share CUPTI. Each case's 3 profiled replays run between
+`cudaProfilerStart`/`Stop` in an NVTX range `forward/<case>`, so a capture range
+records only them, one report per case (and rank):
+
+```bash
+nsys profile --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --capture-range-end=repeat \
+  --cuda-graph-trace=node -o prof vllm bench forward ...       # prof.1, prof.2, ...
+torchrun --nproc-per-node=4 --no-python nsys profile ... -o prof_rank%q{RANK} \
+  python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench forward ...
+nsys stats --report cuda_gpu_kern_sum --format csv -o kern prof.1.nsys-rep
+```
+
+Keep `--capture-range-end=repeat`: nsys's default stops after the first case
+and leaves the bench hanging. `nsys stats` also counts the KV restore copies
+that the JSON summary excludes.
+

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""GPU kernel profiles of `vllm bench forward` cases.
+
+With `--profile-dir`, each case's graph is replayed a few more times under
+`torch.profiler` after timing. Each rank writes a Perfetto trace and a kernel
+summary (`<case>.rank<r>.kernels.json`): per-kernel time per forward, sorted.
+
+Summarize one file or compare two (e.g. before/after a change):
+`python -m vllm.benchmarks.forward.profile A.kernels.json [B.kernels.json]`.
+
+The same replays run between `cudaProfilerStart`/`Stop` in an NVTX range per
+case (with or without `--profile-dir`), so Nsight Systems can record just them:
+`nsys profile --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --capture-range-end=repeat
+--cuda-graph-trace=node vllm bench forward ...`.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import gzip
+import json
+import statistics
+from collections import defaultdict
+from typing import Any
+
+import regex as re
+import torch
+
+_GPU_CATEGORIES = ("kernel", "gpu_memcpy", "gpu_memset")
+# Kernels named after a generic launcher are identified by their first
+# template argument instead.
+_GENERIC = re.compile(r"(^|::)(device_kernel|Kernel|kernel|KernelWrapper)$")
+# CuTe DSL kernel names embed per-shape layouts after these markers.
+_CUTE_DSL_SUFFIX = re.compile(r"_object_at_|_tensorptr")
+
+
+def _match_back(text: str, end: int, open_ch: str, close_ch: str) -> int:
+    """Index of the bracket opening the one closing at `end`, skipping
+    brackets of the other kind nested inside parentheses."""
+    depth, parens = 0, 0
+    for i in range(end, -1, -1):
+        ch = text[i]
+        if open_ch == "<" and ch in "()":
+            parens += 1 if ch == ")" else -1
+            continue
+        if parens:
+            continue
+        if ch == close_ch:
+            depth += 1
+        elif ch == open_ch:
+            depth -= 1
+            if depth == 0:
+                return i
+    return -1
+
+
+def short_name(name: str) -> str:
+    """`void ns::foo<T, 4>(args)` -> `ns::foo`: return type, template and
+    function arguments dropped. Generic launchers (e.g.
+    `cutlass::device_kernel<Op<...>>`) keep their first template argument."""
+    if name.startswith("kernel_cutlass_"):
+        return _CUTE_DSL_SUFFIX.split(name, maxsplit=1)[0]
+    head = name.strip()
+    if head.endswith(")"):
+        head = head[: max(_match_back(head, len(head) - 1, "(", ")"), 0)].rstrip()
+    template = ""
+    if head.endswith(">"):
+        start = _match_back(head, len(head) - 1, "<", ">")
+        if start > 0:
+            head, template = head[:start], head[start + 1 : -1]
+    base = head.split()[-1] if head.split() else name
+    if _GENERIC.search(base) and template:
+        arg = re.split(r"[<>(,]", template, maxsplit=1)[0].strip()
+        if arg:
+            return f"{base}<{arg.removeprefix('void ')}>"
+    return base
+
+
+def summarize(events: list[dict], replays: int, skip: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Per-forward kernel times from the GPU activities of `replays` replays.
+
+    Each replay first runs `skip` activities that aren't part of the timed
+    forward (the KV state restore and the rank rendezvous); they are reported
+    separately as `pre_forward_us`.
+    """
+    acts = sorted(
+        (e for e in events if e.get("cat") in _GPU_CATEGORIES and "dur" in e),
+        key=lambda e: e["ts"],
+    )
+    if not acts:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "No GPU activity recorded. Another profiler (e.g. nsys) may hold "
+            "CUPTI; don't combine --profile-dir with it."
+        )
+    if len(acts) % replays:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{len(acts)} GPU activities don't split into {replays} replays"
+        )
+    per_replay = len(acts) // replays
+    if per_replay <= skip:
+        raise ValueError(f"{per_replay} activities per replay, {skip} to skip")
+    kernels: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = defaultdict(
+        lambda: {"total_us": 0.0, "calls": 0, "example": ""}
+    )
+    spans, busy, pre = [], [], []
+    for r in range(replays):
+        chunk = acts[r * per_replay : (r + 1) * per_replay]
+        pre.append(sum(e["dur"] for e in chunk[:skip]))
+        forward = chunk[skip:]
+        spans.append(
+            max(e["ts"] + e["dur"] for e in forward) - min(e["ts"] for e in forward)
+        )
+        busy.append(sum(e["dur"] for e in forward))
+        for e in forward:
+            name = short_name(e["name"]) if e["cat"] == "kernel" else e["name"]
+            k = kernels[name]
+            k["total_us"] += e["dur"]
+            k["calls"] += 1
+            k["example"] = k["example"] or e["name"][:300]
+    total = sum(k["total_us"] for k in kernels.values())
+    rows = [
+        {
+            "name": name,
+            "us": round(k["total_us"] / replays, 2),
+            "pct": round(100 * k["total_us"] / total, 2),
+            "calls": k["calls"] // replays,
+            "example": k["example"],
+        }
+        for name, k in kernels.items()
+    ]
+    rows.sort(key=lambda row: -row["us"])
+    return {
+        "replays": replays,
+        # First to last forward activity; busy can exceed it when streams overlap.
+        "span_us": round(statistics.median(spans), 2),
+        "busy_us": round(statistics.median(busy), 2),
+        "pre_forward_us": round(statistics.median(pre), 2),
+        "activities": per_replay - skip,
+        "kernels": rows,
+    }
+
+
+def profile_graph(
+    graph: torch.cuda.CUDAGraph,
+    name: str,
+    prefix: str | None,
+    skip: int,
+    replays: int = 3,
+) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
+    """Replay `replays` times between `cudaProfilerStart`/`Stop`, in an NVTX
+    range named after the case, for `nsys --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi`.
+
+    With `prefix`, also trace them with `torch.profiler` and write
+    `prefix.trace.json.gz` and `prefix.kernels.json`. Every rank must call
+    this (replays may contain collectives).
+    """
+
+    def run() -> None:
+        torch.cuda.profiler.start()
+        with torch.cuda.nvtx.range(f"forward/{name}"):
+            for _ in range(replays):
+                graph.replay()
+                torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+        torch.cuda.profiler.stop()
+
+    if prefix is None:
+        run()
+        return None
+    activities = [torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity.CUDA]
+    with torch.profiler.profile(activities=activities) as prof:
+        run()
+    trace = f"{prefix}.trace.json.gz"
+    prof.export_chrome_trace(trace)
+    with gzip.open(trace, "rt") as f:
+        events = json.load(f)["traceEvents"]
+    summary = {"trace": trace, **summarize(events, replays, skip)}
+    with open(f"{prefix}.kernels.json", "w") as f:
+        json.dump(summary, f, indent=1)
+    return summary
+
+
+def format_summary(summary: dict[str, Any], top: int = 20) -> str:
+    lines = [
+        f"span {summary['span_us']:.1f} us, busy {summary['busy_us']:.1f} us, "
+        f"{summary['activities']} activities/forward",
+        f"{'us':>10} {'%':>6} {'calls':>6}  kernel",
+    ]
+    for row in summary["kernels"][:top]:
+        lines.append(
+            f"{row['us']:10.1f} {row['pct']:6.2f} {row['calls']:6d}  {row['name']}"
+        )
+    return "\n".join(lines)
+
+
+def format_diff(a: dict[str, Any], b: dict[str, Any], top: int = 20) -> str:
+    rows_a = {row["name"]: row for row in a["kernels"]}
+    rows_b = {row["name"]: row for row in b["kernels"]}
+    deltas = []
+    for name in rows_a.keys() | rows_b.keys():
+        ra, rb = rows_a.get(name), rows_b.get(name)
+        us_a, us_b = ra["us"] if ra else 0.0, rb["us"] if rb else 0.0
+        calls_a, calls_b = ra["calls"] if ra else 0, rb["calls"] if rb else 0
+        deltas.append((us_b - us_a, us_a, us_b, calls_a, calls_b, name))
+    deltas.sort(key=lambda d: -abs(d[0]))
+    lines = [
+        f"span {a['span_us']:.1f} -> {b['span_us']:.1f} us "
+        f"({b['span_us'] - a['span_us']:+.1f}), busy {a['busy_us']:.1f} -> "
+        f"{b['busy_us']:.1f} us ({b['busy_us'] - a['busy_us']:+.1f})",
+        f"{'delta us':>10} {'A us':>10} {'B us':>10} {'A n':>5} {'B n':>5}  kernel",
+    ]
+    for delta, us_a, us_b, calls_a, calls_b, name in deltas[:top]:
+        lines.append(
+            f"{delta:+10.1f} {us_a:10.1f} {us_b:10.1f} {calls_a:5d} {calls_b:5d}  "
+            f"{name}"
+        )
+    return "\n".join(lines)
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
+    parser.add_argument("summaries", nargs="+", help="One or two *.kernels.json.")
+    parser.add_argument("--top", type=int, default=20)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    if len(args.summaries) > 2:
+        parser.error("Pass one summary, or two to compare.")
+    loaded = []
+    for path in args.summaries:
+        with open(path) as f:
+            loaded.append(json.load(f))
+    if len(loaded) == 1:
+        print(format_summary(loaded[0], args.top))
+    else:
+        print(format_diff(loaded[0], loaded[1], args.top))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

-# Train-inference consistency skill
-
-Make the training side and the inference side in RL produce bitwise identical logprobs for the same token (diff = 0), and, while keeping 0 diff, bring performance back close to the high-performance baseline.

-# Backward: reuse and validation
-
-## Reusing backward: when you actually need to write your own
-
-When to reuse backward and when to write glue.
-
-### Conclusion
-
-Backward is determined by the **math formula**, not by the forward kernel. The backward of `y = f(x, W)` needs only the formula and the saved inputs: `dX = dY·W`, `dW = dYᵀ·x`. A vLLM forward kernel does not by itself require a new backward. "No backward operator at the same precision" is not a reason to rewrite: under the high_precision contract the backward runs in BF16/FP32 anyway.
-
-### How to wire it: forward once, backward uses what the forward saved
-
-The training forward is the inference forward. Each module is an autograd Function: its forward calls the inference kernel to produce the visible output and saves what its own backward needs (inputs, visible output, LSE, fixed routing IDs, quantized values and scales); its backward uses only those, through a reused library backward or a closed-form VJP. If the inference kernel does not output something the backward needs, change the kernel to output it.
-
-Delivery requires 0 diff and a training step within budget on the main topologies fixed at C1; C6 checks both together. Nemotron audited this against DS4: attention saves q/k/v, out and LSE; routed MoE saves x, the visible FC1 output and the visible output; linear and norms save their inputs; the router saves logits and fixed IDs. Its open gap is Mamba SSD, because vLLM's visible SSD does not output the chunk state.
-
-### Three cases
-
-| Case | Characteristics | Examples | What to do |
-| --- | --- | --- | --- |
-| A only rounding differs | Same math; summation order/chunking differs; difference in the last BF16 bit | RMSNorm, Mamba SSD scan, attention, conv1d, unquantized linear | Reuse the training framework's backward (MCore/TE/mamba_ssm); write no code |
-| B forward has rounding | FP8/NVFP4 quantization rounds; the true derivative is 0 almost everywhere | Quantized linear, FP8 Q/K/V | First fix the STE proxy (rounding passes through as 1; dX uses dequantized values by default; DS4 and Nemotron currently approximate with TE high_precision master values, and the deviation must be quantified per [layer 2](#layer-2-gradient-contract-comparison)), then reuse the ordinary BF16 GEMM backward |
-| C no ready-made backward for the whole segment | Composite of several operators with no library backward for the whole segment | Routed experts: sort -> grouped GEMM -> relu² -> restore -> top-k weighted sum | Write glue that chains ready-made operators; GEMM still uses TE grouped GEMM; compare gradients against an independent reference |
-
-Decision flow: (1) does the forward have rounding/quantization (top-k ID selection does not count; IDs are fixed and not differentiated)? No -> A. Yes -> (2) fix the STE contract -> (3) is there a packaged training backward for the whole segment (TE Linear/GroupedLinear, MCore MoE)? Yes -> B, reuse it and feed master values; no -> C, glue. If A has no same-math training implementation, also write only glue. Look first in mLite `primitive/modules` and `ops`, then in MCore/TE/mamba_ssm.
-
-### How DS4 did it
-
-DS4's only hand-written kernel is the small FP8 quantization Triton kernel in the forward. The backward has no hand-written kernel, only PyTorch closed-form formulas and glue, all in FP32.
-
-| Operator | Case | Backward source | What we wrote |
-| --- | --- | --- | --- |
-| FP8 dense linear (qkv, shared expert, o-proj) | B | TE `general_gemm`, BF16 master | Nothing |
-| Routed experts (grouped) | B+C | TE `general_grouped_gemm`; reuses gate_up, the output of the forward vLLM FC1, without recomputing | Glue: sort, activation derivative, summation |
-| Sparse attention | A | cuDNN sparse attention backward, consuming the forward's saved out and LSE | Nothing |
-| SwiGLU (with clamp), RMSNorm, q/kv norm, mHC | A | Hand-written closed-form derivative, FP32, `torch.compile` | PyTorch formula |
-| Routing score | A (IDs fixed) | FP32 replay of `sqrt(softplus)` + normalization, handed to autograd | PyTorch formula |
-| Others | A | Generic bridge: forward via vLLM, backward recomputes the PyTorch graph then `autograd.grad` | One utility function |
-
-DS4 wrote its own for four reasons, none of them a missing same-precision backward kernel: (1) library backwards need intermediates from the library's own forward (TE RMSNorm needs rstd, MCore MoE the token permutation; the vLLM forward has neither); (2) model-specific math is not in the library (`sqrt(softplus)` scoring, SwiGLU with clamp, mHC Sinkhorn); (3) discrete selection must copy the forward (recomputed top-k may pick a different expert on ties, so store the IDs and differentiate only the continuous score); (4) the generic bridge costs too much memory and time (autograd stores all 20 mHC iterations; use a closed-form derivative fused with compile). A custom backward function has no autograd graph inside, so its activation derivative must be closed-form (`dynamic_clamped_swiglu_vjp`; likewise relu² in Nemotron `routed_vjp`).
-
-### Three rules when reusing
-
-1. Intermediate definitions must match: attention backward uses the forward's out and LSE, so LSE base (ln or log2), softmax scale and memory layout must line up. If they do not, recompute the forward with the training kernel inside the backward.
-2. Backward need not be bitwise identical: recomputed intermediates differ from the vLLM forward in the last BF16 bit and gradients differ by the same amount, which is allowed. The requirement is that the gradient contract holds and the error is near the noise floor.
-3. Reused code must be verified too, per [layer 1](#layer-1-module-level-vjp-comparison): compare dX and dW against an FP32 reference that does not call the backward under test, with the same dY, in multiples of the noise floor.
-
-### Two test-infrastructure false negatives
-
-- A unit test that instantiated QuantFP8 directly lacked production training's vLLM config context (`CompilationConfig(custom_ops=['none','+quant_fp8'])`, Humming, PP4), and the first long-sequence test failed before computing anything. Fix: the test wrapper uses the production config; production operators and tolerances are unchanged.
-- An import check without GPU visibility makes vLLM select a non-CUDA platform, which cannot import `reshape_and_cache_flash` (exported only on CUDA). Dependency checks need real device visibility.
-- Both are test errors, not train-inference differences.
-
-## Backward validation: is the implementation right, is the approximation reasonable, is training biased
-
-Forward 0 diff shows the logprobs match, not that gradients are right. Validate the backward in three layers:
-
-| Layer | Question answered | Method | Cannot replace |
-| --- | --- | --- | --- |
-| 1. Module-level VJP comparison | Does the implementation match the agreed gradient contract (missing scale, wrong transpose, broken gradient chain) | compare dX, dW and a one-step update of every module against an independent reference that does not call the backward under test | layers 2 and 3 |
-| 2. Gradient contract comparison | Is the contract reasonable: does an approximation (e.g. dX from the master value) bias training | same batch, compare gradients under the two conventions per class and per layer | layer 1 |
-| 3. Proxy SFT three-arm comparison | Does the whole training chain have a systematic bias | three SFT paths (under test, gradient reference, native baseline) with the same data and hyperparameters | layers 1 and 2 |
-
-Run 1 → 2 → 3. If layer 1 fails, fix the implementation before any SFT. If layer 3 is abnormal, go back to layers 1 and 2. Passing all three clears the backward; none proves long-term RL stability.
-
-### Write down the gradient contract first
-
-#### The three tiers of a weight
-
-In quantized training one parameter has three values, and the gradient must end up at the one the optimizer manages:
-
-| Tier | Precision | What it is |
-| --- | --- | --- |
-| main | FP32 | optimizer state; updates accumulate here |
-| master | BF16 | the model parameter, converted from main every step; non-quantized layers compute with it directly |
-| deployed value | NVFP4 / FP8 etc. | master quantized per the deployment rule; both the training forward and inference use these bytes |
-
-Keep the optimizer's parameter identity: when replacing the forward, do not create parameters the optimizer does not know about. The deployed value is not a trainable parameter.
-
-#### Contract table
-
-A kernel without autograd does not need a surrogate gradient: non-quantized GEMM, norm and attention reuse the existing backward when the math matches; STE is needed only through discrete operations such as quantization rounding. Before implementing, decide per module class:
-
-| Item | What must be decided |
-| --- | --- |
-| Visible forward | the inference implementation; input/output dtype, layout; quantize/dequantize positions, scale granularity, rounding, clamp, accumulation precision |
-| Trainable variables | input, master weight, bias, norm, router; whether scale is fixed, stop-gradient or trainable |
-| Surrogate function | whether dX uses the master or dequantized value (see below); identity or clipped STE, and the value at the threshold |
-| Discrete state | fixed expert IDs, sparse indices, ordering; continuous score/combine weights that still need gradients |
-| backward | reused implementation or custom VJP; cast, accumulation/reduction precision, communication and normalization |
-| Save/recompute | quantized values, scale, norm/attention intermediates, routing, RNG; memory cost and recompute rules |
-| Reference and acceptance | independent reference implementation, target shape/execution path, metrics and tolerances agreed in advance |
-
-Identity STE sets the surrogate derivative of Q(x) to 1; clipped STE sets 1 inside the range and 0 outside, with the threshold value stated and never switched silently. Declare weight and activation quantization separately; frozen weights do not mean nothing upstream of the activations needs gradients.
-
-#### Linear: which weight dX uses
-
-For `Y = X · Wᵀ + b` with upstream gradient `G`:
-
-```text
-dW = Gᵀ · X_ref        # returns to master via STE, then the optimizer updates main
-db = sum_over_tokens(G)
-dX = G · W_ref
-```
-
-Two choices for `W_ref`:
-
-- **Dequantized value**: `W_ref = dequant(quant(W_master))`, the value the forward actually used. This is the true derivative of `Y = X · Wqᵀ` with respect to X, and what fake-quant QAT gets from autograd. **Use this by default.**
-- **Master value**: `W_ref = W_master` (BF16). Reuses the plain BF16 GEMM backward without dequantizing; the cheapest hookup when the inference kernel takes only packed bytes and has no backward. Cost: dX is no longer the exact forward derivative and ignores the quantization error's effect on the input gradient.
-
-The two give different gradients and must not be swapped silently. With the master value, the layer-2 comparison is mandatory: quantify and record the bias. Likewise for activation quantization, state whether `X_ref` is the quantized or original activation.
-
-Before reusing a linear or grouped GEMM backward, check flatten/transpose, padding and valid tokens, bias reduction, saved inputs, scaling and the accumulation/backprop dtype. Matching output shape does not prove reusability.
-
-### Layer 1: module-level VJP comparison
-
-#### How to build the reference implementation
-
-The reference may use PyTorch ops and autograd but **must not call the backward under test**, or both paths share the error. For discrete operations implement the agreed surrogate backward explicitly; the zero gradient of bare rounding is not a reference.
-
-This bridge takes the output value from the inference implementation and the gradient from an independent surrogate. Use it to build the reference path:
-
-```python
-import torch
-
-
-class VisibleWithSurrogate(torch.autograd.Function):
-    @staticmethod
-    def forward(ctx, visible, surrogate):
-        assert visible.shape == surrogate.shape
-        assert visible.device == surrogate.device
-        assert visible.dtype == surrogate.dtype
-        return visible
-
-    @staticmethod
-    def backward(ctx, grad_output):
-        return None, grad_output
-
-
-with torch.no_grad():
-    visible = inference_linear(x, deployment_weight, scales)
-w_ref = dequantize(deployment_weight, scales)  # default contract; use master_weight for the master-value contract
-surrogate = torch.nn.functional.linear(x, w_ref, bias)
-y = VisibleWithSurrogate.apply(visible.detach(), surrogate)
-```
-
-- Build the surrogate graph in normal grad mode, outside the custom Function's forward.
-- With the dequantized surrogate, `w_ref`'s gradient must reach master via STE: bridge a tensor valued as the dequantized weight whose gradient passes straight to master, then feed it to a plain linear.
-- Do not use `visible + surrogate - surrogate.detach()`: floating-point add/subtract and compiler transforms change the result. Do not modify the bridge output in place downstream.
-- This bridge is the independent validation reference, not the production wiring; production wiring is in [How to wire it](#how-to-wire-it-forward-once-backward-uses-what-the-forward-saved).
-- `visible_forward(visible, native, *inputs)` is another way to write the same bridge: `visible` saves inputs without building a graph, `native` is the training framework's implementation of the same math and reruns the forward on those inputs in backward; precision and speed depend on which `native` is chosen.
-
-#### Comparison steps
-
-1. **Fix the state.** Fix inputs, weights, quantization config, mask/routing. Reference and candidate get independent copies; clear accumulated gradients. Check that the visible forward matches inference, then the saved state the backward needs; at integration, confirm the real forward produces that state.
-2. **Same upstream gradient.** Both sides use the same external dY, dtype and values. Cover fixed random, zero, and sparse (non-zero at selected positions) gradients, then samples from real training. `y.sum().backward()` alone misses transpose, permutation and broadcast errors.
-3. **Compare item by item.** Compare dX, dW and every bias/norm/router/scale gradient separately: missing, shape, finiteness, non-zero where expected. Do not ignore unused differentiable inputs by default; list parameters the branch genuinely does not use. Report max absolute error, relative L2 `‖g − g_ref‖₂ / max(‖g_ref‖₂, eps)`, norm ratio and cosine; direction alone is not enough. With a zero norm the cosine is undefined; use absolute error.
-4. **Set tolerances in advance.** Derive atol/rtol and the relative L2 threshold from dtype, reduction length and reference precision; record the reasoning. No single threshold for all modules, no relaxing after a failure, and no relaxing a same-semantics kernel optimization because "STE is an approximation anyway". Cross-framework bitwise identity is not required.
-5. **Coverage.** Small M (decode), large M (training/prefill), different context lengths, unaligned tails, padding/packing/mask, zeros and extreme values; both sides of the quantization threshold, the saturation region, different scales. For MoE cover empty experts, repeated routing, shared experts, top-k ties; for shared parameters check gradient accumulation across use sites. Test under the target dtype/layout, recompute, autocast, CUDA Graph, gradient accumulation and the actual parallel reduction; local first, then integrated.
-6. **One-step update.** From the same parameters and optimizer state, run one update each and compare the change in master. If gradients are close but updates differ, check scaling, clipping, optimizer state and parameter binding.
-
-Cross-check smooth non-quantized modules with small, high-precision [gradcheck](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.autograd.gradcheck.html) or finite differences: fix the discrete branch, avoid non-smooth boundaries, and perturb the weights the forward actually sees. **Do not validate STE with finite differences of the real quantized forward**: that measures the discrete forward, which the STE surrogate derivative deliberately differs from.
-
-#### What to check per module
-
-| Module | Reuse first | Semantics to check |
-| --- | --- | --- |
-| Dense/QKV/LM head | training linear/grouped VJP, gradient returns to master | dX value convention, cast, bias, gradient accumulation of shared parameters |
-| Norm/RoPE | existing training VJP, FP32 statistics if needed | epsilon, RMS or LayerNorm, position offset, rotation layout |
-| Activation + quantization | the actual composition of activation derivative and STE | saturation region, whether scale is detached, fusion order |
-| Attention/sparse attention | training backward with the same mask/index semantics | causal boundary, softmax scale, LSE definition, GQA, order of selected KV; do not mix auxiliary quantities from different forwards |
-| MoE | expert linear/grouped VJP and a differentiable combine | inverse dispatch permutation, gradient accumulation of repeated tokens, empty experts, shared experts, top-k weight normalization |
-| Router/sparse selection | fix the discrete selection, keep the continuous score's derivative | no continuous gradient for IDs/indices; do not detach the whole router output |
-| Linear attention/SSM | training backward with the same chunked arithmetic | chunk boundary, initial state, state precision, conv state |
-| Selected logprob | log-softmax/gather VJP matching the definition | vocab-shard reduction, temperature, token mask, loss normalization |
-
-Recompute must save or deterministically rebuild the scale, routing/indices, RNG and necessary intermediates, and must not switch the surrogate function.
-
-### Layer 2: gradient contract comparison
-
-Layer 1 answers "does the implementation equal the contract", not "is the contract reasonable". When the contract contains an approximation (most often dX from the master instead of the dequantized value), quantify its distance from the exact derivative:
-
-1. On a fixed checkpoint and batch, compute dX (and gradients related to activation quantization) for every quantized layer under both conventions.
-2. Report cosine and norm ratio per module class and per layer; inspect outlier layers.
-3. Measure each target precision combination separately: changing weight or activation precision changes the bias.
-
-On Nemotron-H (NVFP4 routed experts, FP8 Mamba projections), master-value and dequantized-value dX have cosine ≈0.99 and norm ratio ≈1.00 per class and layer, with both BF16 and FP8 activations, so this approximation does not cause the training score gap. Remeasure for other precisions, a larger learning rate or longer training.
-
-### Layer 3: Proxy SFT three-arm comparison
-
-After the first two layers pass, run a controlled SFT over the whole training chain:
-
-| Path | Visible forward | backward | Purpose |
-| --- | --- | --- | --- |
-| Under test | aligned inference numerics | production backward | the scheme to deliver |
-| Gradient reference | same as under test at the same parameter snapshot | independent surrogate reference (the bridge above works) | isolate backward implementation errors |
-| Native baseline | original training numerical path | verified original training backward | measure the recipe's overall quality change |
-
-- First compare gradients and one-step update of under-test vs gradient-reference on a fixed checkpoint and batch, then run curves; once trajectories diverge, visible values differ too. The under-test vs native-baseline gap includes quantization and forward-path differences, not only backward. If the gradient reference's full curve is unaffordable, compare on representative batches and state the missing range.
-- Controlled variables: initial weights and optimizer state, data and order, labels/mask, packing, loss normalization, global batch and gradient accumulation, learning rate and schedule, clipping, precision and loss scaling, seed, recompute policy.
-- Record train loss, fixed-validation-set NLL, gradient norm, update RMS, clipping ratio, non-finite values, throughput, against optimizer step or cumulative effective tokens. Fix the comparison window and acceptable deviation before the run; a short run is only a smoke test.
-- Localization: loss differs at the initial weights -> check forward, data, mask; initial loss matches but one-step update differs -> backward, reduction, scale, clipping, optimizer; diverges only after several steps -> save the first abnormal checkpoint, check recompute, quantization refresh, learning rate, RNG, then replay at the same weights.
-- Mark unexplained or unbudgeted differences inconclusive; do not cover them with forward 0 diff.
-
-On Nemotron-H the three paths (aligned trainer with BF16 activations, Megatron QAT, Megatron BF16) ran 40 steps on gsm8k with the same data in the same order: loss 0.3388 / 0.3383 / 0.3374, gradient norm 0.685 / 0.674 / 0.728, curves overlapping. The training loop itself is fine; the RL score gap comes from RL-specific factors.
-
-### Common false differences
-
-Each of these made gradients look mismatched when the comparison method was the problem:
-
-- **Upstream gradient precision differs.** FP32 dY on one side and BF16-rounded dY on the other creates a difference unrelated to the backward. Use the same external dY.
-- **Dump timing.** Expert gradients are multiplied by the expert-DP to DP scaling ratio only inside the optimizer step; dumping earlier shows a false multiplicative difference.
-- **Unsharded copy under FSDP2.** After forward-only the root module is not resharded, so the parameter fetched by name is the unsharded compute copy, not the real master. Perturbing it or reading its gradient both mislead.
-- **"Frozen" is not frozen.** Zeroing the gradient still lets AdamW weight decay change the parameter; a real freeze needs grad None or removal from the optimizer.
-- **Test environment differs from production.** A unit test missing production config context, or an import without GPU visibility, selects the wrong implementation or fails to import (see [Two test-infrastructure false negatives](#two-test-infrastructure-false-negatives)).
-
-### What to write in the report
-
-Per module class: gradient contract (dX value choice, STE type, scale handling), reference implementation, upstream gradient construction, shapes/paths covered, metrics and tolerances with reasoning. Layer 2: per-class per-layer cosine/norm ratio and outlier layers. Layer 3: config diff table of the three paths, curves, conclusion within the window. List missing coverage explicitly, not as "the rest is analogous".
-
-For the basic definition of STE see [Bengio et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.3432); it does not decide the surrogate gradient rule for a specific model.

-# Checkpoint, resume and memory budget
-
-Use this guide to get checkpoint save, load and resume right in long RL runs, and to budget host (CPU) memory peaks and growth. For per-phase GPU memory peaks see [Locating GPU OOM and staging peaks by lifecycle](#locating-gpu-oom-and-staging-peaks-by-lifecycle).
-
-## Find by symptom
-
-| Symptom | Where to go |
-| --- | --- |
-| OOM while loading a checkpoint | [Load](#4-load-enough-capacity-does-not-mean-enough-for-the-transient-peak) |
-| Train-inference mismatch on the first step after restore | [13](#13-stale-quantization-scale-on-the-first-step-after-restore) |
-| Resume is set but training starts from step 0 | [14](#14-resume_modeauto-starts-from-step-0) |
-| Host RSS grows every step | [3.3](#33-locating-slowly-grows-every-step) |

-
-## Terms
-
-- **pinned memory:** page-locked host memory for direct GPU DMA (`cudaHostAlloc` / `cudaHostRegister`), cached by PyTorch's caching host allocator.
-- **cgroup:** limit `memory.max`, usage `memory.current`, split in `memory.stat` into anon, file (page cache) and shmem.
-- **RSS and PSS:** RSS counts shared pages fully in every process; PSS splits them, so only summed PSS approximates the physical total.
-- **DCP / Megatron dist_ckpt:** PyTorch and Megatron distributed checkpoint formats; each rank writes its shard, `.metadata` last.
-- **staging / D2H:** the host buffer GPU tensors are copied into before writing to disk.
-- **Ray object store (plasma):** Ray's shared memory for passing objects, mapped into each worker and charged via PSS.
-- **old-logprob:** the logprob training recomputes for rollout tokens with the pre-update policy.
-- **Ray OOM threshold:** `RAY_memory_usage_threshold`, the usage fraction at which Ray kills workers. Default 0.95.
-
-## Key rules
-
-- Check file, memory and derived state separately; complete files can still mismatch on the first step after restore.
-- Capture the first exception (errno, rank, file, offset), not the last message.
-- Completion marker last; clear the old directory before overwriting; all ranks check and fail together; a missing file raises instead of falling back to a fresh optimizer.
-- Under EP4 + FSDP2, ranks' expert shards in DCP share key and offset, so restore reads another rank's experts. Put the EP rank in the key (port the reference fix), add a 4-GPU bitwise read-back unit test, and raise on EP size mismatch.
-- Rotation deletes only tracked, complete, idle directories; in long runs keep one checkpoint every 20 steps outside rotation.
-- Set rollout `gpu_memory_utilization` per training mode ([5](#5-gpu-memory-set-gpu_memory_utilization-per-mode-when-training-and-rollout-are-colocated)).
-- Save fixes pass [the acceptance in 3.2](#32-reproduce-and-discriminate). Before a long run on a new save path or layout, run to the first save and do one kill→resume.
-- Resume is proven by matching per-rank digests in a new process, a byte-identical first export, an aligned first old-logprob and one non-zero update; `resume_mode=auto` alone proves nothing.
-- Read host memory as anon/file/shmem; `memory.current` includes page cache, and Ray kills on it.
-- Pinned buffers round up to a power of 2 (Nemotron: 146.9 GiB pinned for 88.2 GiB of optimizer state, +67%); allocate large long-lived pinned blocks at exact size.
-- The save step is the peak; a higher Ray threshold or smaller microbatch does not fix headroom.
-- For per-step growth, use the per-process PSS floor and a small CPU-only repro before changing code.
-- Verify per save path that the host cache is released after save.

-## Checkpoint and resume
-
-### 1. Three independent contracts
-
-Classify the problem before calling it "the checkpoint is broken":
-
-| Contract | Typical failure |
-| --- | --- |
-| File: serialization and publish | Disk write error; an incomplete directory treated as complete |
-| Memory: transient peaks of save and load | Killed by Ray after the write finishes; cgroup OOM during load |
-| Derived state: the first export after restore | Files complete, but the first step after restore mismatches ([stale quantization scale](#13-stale-quantization-scale-on-the-first-step-after-restore)) |
-
-The third class is a derived-state lifecycle bug, not file corruption.
-
-### 2. Which state exact resume needs

-| State | Requirement |
-| --- | --- |
-| Model parameters or LoRA adapter shards | Saved per rank; strict load that rejects missing/unexpected keys ([training forward](training-forward.md)) |
-| Optimizer state, including the CPU-offloaded part | Same step as the model. Nemotron chunked optimizer offload: 88.2 GiB per rank, 94.7 GB per rank on disk; DS4.1 saves LoRA parameters and Adam `exp_avg` / `exp_avg_sq` in FP32 |
-| LR scheduler | Check the saved value, not the source default (DS4.1 checks its constant, no-warmup schedule per rank) |
-| RNG | Four streams: CPU, CUDA, Python, NumPy |
-| Counters and data position | global step, optimizer step, data cursor; DS4.1 also saves the cumulative count of effective-signal steps |
-| Run contract | Hashes of code, data and recipe, compared item by item on restore; reject a change in total steps or data by default. To extend training, declare a new phase explicitly; do not edit the old contract file or add a generic ignore switch |

-

-- **Records outside training:** the metrics jsonl is overwritten on resume.

-### 3. Save

-

-

-
-A fast repro keeps the real tensors, serializer and concurrency, skips rollout/backward and repeats only save, for a bounded number of rounds sized to the failure probability; stop at the first failure and keep the scene. -## Memory budget: host and GPU
-
-Host memory fails in two ways in long RL runs: phase **peaks** (save / load / sleep) hitting the limit, and slow per-step **growth**; they are measured differently (1-4). GPU memory is a third class: with training and rollout colocated, rollout `gpu_memory_utilization` is set per training mode (5).
-
-### 1. Who holds host memory
-
-| Source | Mechanism |
-| --- | --- |
-| Pinned buffer of optimizer offload | The caching host allocator rounds up to a power of 2, so the footprint is tens of percent above the nominal state; summed across ranks it pushes residency before save close to the limit |
-| Parameter shards of FSDP CPU offload | Each rank's shard stays resident on CPU; doubles if load creates a second pinned copy |
-| D2H staging during save | Stays in the pinned cache pool; whether `torch.accelerator.empty_host_cache()` releases it must be verified per save path |
-| CPU backup of serving sleep | L1 sleep keeps one full backup per rank; the pinned cache is not returned after wake |
-| Ray object store | plasma mappings count into each process's PSS as shared pages; node shmem does not grow with it (3) |
-
-`param_offload` trades CPU pressure for GPU memory; optimizer offload is separate. Change one offload switch at a time and measure the phase peak before and after.
-
-### 2. Limits and who does the killing
-
-- **cgroup.** The job limit `memory.max` is usually below physical memory; budget against it. A cgroup OOM shows an `oom_kill` event and process SIGKILL, with no Python stack.
-- **Ray memory monitor.** Kills workers at `RAY_memory_usage_threshold`=0.95 by default; log line `exceeded threshold of <bytes>B (95.0% ...)`. Its usage figure includes page cache. Raising the threshold does not fix headroom: Nemotron at 0.985 was still killed during save.
-- Distinguish GPU allocation exception, host cgroup OOM and Ray kill. A CUDA allocator allocation-failure / retry warning is not a terminal OOM and the step may complete, but it does show memory pressure.
-
-### 3. How to measure
-
-#### 3.1 One record per phase
-
-Log one line at load, save, sleep, wakeup, reset KV cache and generation start / end, with monotonic time, node / rank / PID and policy version. -
-`generate_sequences` includes wake/init. An error inside it does not prove token generation started, let alone a backward/optimizer OOM.
-
-#### 3.2 Pitfalls in the readings
-
-| Reading | Problem |
-| --- | --- |
-| `memory.current` | Includes page cache, which masks per-step growth; but it is what Ray and the save peak see |
-| `free`, `psutil.virtual_memory().used` | System-visible memory, not process RSS or job cgroup usage |
-| `scontrol` FreeMem | Excludes reclaimable cache |
-| `ru_maxrss`, Slurm MaxRSS | Cumulative peak, not current RSS |
-| VmPin/VmLck | Cannot alone infer CUDA pinned |
-| Sum of per-process RSS | Counts shared mappings repeatedly; use PSS |
-
-Pinned memory from cudaHostAlloc shows up as shmem in cgroup `memory.stat` (measured on Nemotron).
-
-#### 3.3 Locating "slowly grows every step"

-1. Use node `MemTotal−MemAvailable` and cgroup anon/file/shmem to find which class grows.

-

-
-Budget the save-step peak as the sum of what is alive at the same time, against cgroup limit × Ray threshold:
-
-```text
-peak  ≈ resident pinned optimizer offload (actual footprint after allocator rounding)
-      + save D2H staging (and the part of it left in the cache pool)
-      + page cache of the newly written checkpoint files
-      + CPU backup of serving sleep and unreleased pinned cache
-      + resident amount of the other processes (rollout, driver, Ray workers, etc.; take the floor per 3.3)
-limit = cgroup memory.max × RAY_memory_usage_threshold
-```

-| --- | --- | --- |

-4. **Find the earliest divergence.** Look first at the embedding, block outputs, and logits at the last valid prompt position. -| Class | Evidence | Handling |
-| --- | --- | --- |

-10. Check that deployed bytes = `requantize(master)`.
-11. Start the master from the real BF16 release, not a dequantized checkpoint, whose values sit on grid points so NVFP4 deployed values only change after thousands of steps at small lr. θ0 bytes then differ from the official checkpoint (Nemotron-H: NVFP4 99.776% identical, FP8 24/46 tensors differ); quantify the cost with proxy SFT and have a human confirm it ([QAT §6.2](#62-fix)).
-
-## Terms
-
-- **NVFP4**: FP4 E2M1 values, one FP8 E4M3 block scale per 16 elements, plus one FP32 global scale.
-- **block scale / global scale**: per-block scale (`weight_scale`, `scale`) / per-tensor or per-fusion-group scale (`weight_scale_2`, `weight_global_scale`, `scale2`).
-- **amax**: maximum absolute value of a tensor (or block), used to compute scale.
-- **4over6 / MSE**: TE NVFP4 block scale selection settings; the Nemotron-H checkpoint uses them.
-- **E4M3 / E2M1 / UE8M0**: FP8 (4 exponent, 3 mantissa bits) / FP4 (2 exponent, 1 mantissa bit) / unsigned 8-bit exponent (power-of-2 scale).
-- **W4A16 / W4A4 / W8A8**: weight bit width / activation bit width.
-- **QDQ**: quantize then immediately dequantize, giving a high-precision value on the grid.
-- **fake-quant / fake-QAT**: the training forward uses the QDQ value while GEMM stays high precision; not low-precision training.
-- **STE**: straight-through estimator; treats the derivative of rounding as 1 (or with a clipping mask).
-- **master**: high-precision parameters managed by the optimizer.
-- **conversion owner**: the single party that converts a tensor family to the inference format.
-- **fusion group**: tensors fused in serving (QKV, gate/up) that must share scale.
-- **R3**: MoE route replay; training uses the expert selection recorded by rollout.
-- **BI=1 / BI=0**: the `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` switch; 1 is the true on-policy arm where training calls the inference kernels, 0 is the regular baseline.
-- **probs_diff**: verl's `training/rollout_probs_diff_*`, the token probability difference between rollout and the training forward.
-- **TIS / `rollout_is`**: rollout importance sampling correction.
-- **θ0**: policy weights before the first update.
-- **oracle**: the reference implementation or value that decides pass or fail.
-- **VJP**: the backward function that computes input and parameter gradients from the upstream gradient.
-
-## Conversion chain: from master weights to the bytes the vLLM kernel uses
-
-### 1. Four stages
-
-```text
-A. master weights     FP32/BF16 optimizer master (plus the FP32 exceptions the model declares)
-   ↓ forward materialization
-B. weights the training forward actually sees
-                      BF16; under QAT it is DQ(Q(W)), the dequantized value on the deployment grid
-   ↓ export (gather → HF mapping → quantize/pack)
-C. inference-format bytes
-                      packed NVFP4 + block scale + global scale / FP8 + scale /
-                      INT4 packed + scale / layers still BF16 in mixed precision
-   ↓ loader → post-load
-D. tensors loaded by vLLM and used by the kernel (including post-load reordering and derived scales)
-```
-
-| Stage | Invariant | How to verify |
-| --- | --- | --- |
-| A | Record dtype separately for parameters and buffers; an FP32 master does not mean forward uses FP32 | Read optimizer parameter identity and dtype; see [§6](#6-dtype-contract-six-boundaries) |
-| B | Under QAT, `Q` is the same function on the same grid as the export in C | Unit test: weights of B = dequantize(bytes of C), bitwise |
-| C | Scale computed on the full logical tensor; fusion group shares the global scale; excluded layers keep their dtype; recomputing on the same master is idempotent | Compare packed bytes, block scale, global scale per tensor; see [§2](#2-inventory-the-checkpoints-full-quantization-rules-first) |
-| D | Each family quantized once; post-load only reorders, does not recompute scale; calibration values arrive unchanged | Per tensor, compare exported bytes with the bytes vLLM uses after loading |
-
-Record the real format and scale of weights, activations and KV (packed UE8M0, FP32 scale, MXFP4/FP8 scope); activation and packing rounding may differ between SM90 and SM100. Before measuring quantization error, confirm the scale comes from the current weights, not an old tensor.
-
-### 2. Inventory the checkpoint's full quantization rules first
-
-1. From `hf_quant_config.json` and the `quantization_config` in `config.json`, list each layer's format, which layers carry `input_scale`, and whether the KV cache carries k/v scale. Read layer by layer; do not infer from the model name ([P12](#p12-inferring-a-layers-precision-from-the-models-overall-name)). Nemotron-H Lightning 30B-A3B: `MIXED_PRECISION`; 46 FP8 layers (`mixer.in_proj`/`out_proj` of 23 Mamba layers); 5935 `W4A16_NVFP4` layers (routed/shared experts, lm_head); FP8 KV cache; 46 fp32 scalar `input_scale`, FP8 layers only.
-2. Encode the BF16 release with the checkpoint's own scales; 100% identical packed bytes confirm the release matches the checkpoint.
-3. From the **real BF16 release**, requantize with the candidate rule and report per tensor the match ratio of packed bytes, block scale and global scale. Dequantized weights already sit on the grid and pass under any rule ([P2](#p2-verifying-a-rule-with-dequantized-weights-gives-a-false-positive)). Measured match rates: [P1](#p1-scale-rule-differs-from-the-checkpoint-requantization-flips-codes), [P3](#p3-fp8-per-tensor-scale-convention-is-not-amax448).
-
-Decisions:
-
-- Call the rules of a mainstream implementation (TE, ModelOpt, NeMo-RL) directly; do not invent a scale policy. Deviate, and report it, only when the mainstream implementation cannot do it. Nemotron's self-invented "enlarge scale only on overflow" was replaced by an existing TE rule.
-- θ0 deployed bytes = the real BF16 release requantized by the rule, which differs from the official checkpoint: on Nemotron-H, NVFP4 bytes are 99.776% identical and FP8 24/46 tensors differ; the proxy SFT cost is about 0.03 nat ([QAT §6.2](#62-fix)). This policy needs human confirmation.
-- The BI=1 training forward, BI=0 QAT and the exporter call the same `requantize`; θ0 bytes of the two arms are identical. `input_scale`, `k_scale`, `v_scale` are calibration values passed through from the checkpoint.
-- When a single FP8 checkpoint is the source of truth, the training base is a deterministic dequantized derivative, and requantizing need not restore the checkpoint byte for byte. Measure separately: (1) with zero updates, re-exported bytes equal θ0; (2) the precision difference from the original checkpoint.
-
-### 3. What each format outputs
-
-| Format | Artifacts | Must check |
-| --- | --- | --- |
-| block FP8 | FP8 weight + `weight_scale_inv`, scale per block | Commonly 128×128; FP32/UE8M0 branch, backend, exclusion scope |
-| per-tensor FP8 | FP8 weight + `weight_scale` | Scale from the amax of the full weight, not of a shard; convention may not be amax/448 |
-| MXFP8 | E4M3 weight + UE8M0 `weight_scale_inv` | 1×32 block direction, scale encoding, pad and high-precision exceptions |
-| NVFP4 W4A16 (compressed-tensors, existing `fp4` sender) | `.weight_packed` + `.weight_scale` + `.weight_global_scale` | 1×16, two-level scale, shared outer scale for gate/up, activation contract |
-| NVFP4 W4A4 (ModelOpt, Inkling) | packed `uint8` under the original parameter name + FP8 `scale` + FP32 `scale2` + BF16 `input_amax` + `original_shape` | Naming not interchangeable with compressed-tensors; needs a separate adapter |
-| INT4 compressed-tensors | `weight_packed` + `weight_scale` + `weight_shape` | group_size, symmetric quantization, pack layout, list of tensors actually quantized |
-| DeepSeek V4.1 attention FP8 | F8_E4M3 weight + F8_E8M0 `.scale`, 32×32 block | Not rowwise 32-element MXFP8 |
-
-`weight_scale_inv` is only a loader protocol name; interpret the value per implementation.
-
-### 4. Who converts: conversion owner
-
-A tensor family has one conversion owner. Once the sender has packed, the receiver must not quantize again. dtype reinterpret, layout staging and post-load repack are not quantization.
-
-| Path | Training | Export | Rollout load | owner |
-| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
-| FP8 rollout-only | BF16 | Full BF16 | `quant_weights()` converts to block-FP8 | rollout receiver |
-| VERL FSDP QAT NVFP4 | BF16 + fake quant | After gathering the full tensor, `QATQuantizer` outputs packed NVFP4/scale | compressed-tensors | FSDP sender |
-| VERL Megatron QAT NVFP4 | BF16 + ModelOpt fake quant | `QATWeightExporter` | ModelOpt | Megatron sender |
-| Megatron FP8 E2E | TE FP8 | Bridge-specific FP8 export planning | vLLM FP8 | Bridge / rollout, per the pinned recipe |
-| Nemotron-H BI=0 (verl Megatron) | BF16 + ModelOpt weight STE | Requantized by the checkpoint's rules into ModelOpt `MIXED_PRECISION` | ModelOpt | sender (`mixed_precision_export=True`) |
-| Pre-quantized checkpoint passthrough | No requantization | Original tensor/scale | Per the checkpoint layout | checkpoint producer |
-
-- Full merge: convert logically complete HF tensors one at a time by their owner; no whole-model all-gather or per-step disk write.
-- QAT: the training forward simulates quantization; export generates the actual packed weights and scales.
-
-#### 4.1 FSDP path (VERL)
-
-- With `actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.qat.enable=true`, quantizable `nn.Linear` modules become `QATLinear` after the PEFT wrapper and before the FSDP wrap. Forward does NVFP4 W4A16/W4A4 fake quant and ends in `F.linear`; after the optimizer step, `invalidate_all_scales` clears the weight scale cache. [Implementation][qat-linear]
-- Export: `FSDPEngine.get_per_tensor_param()` calls `full_tensor()` on each `DTensor`, then `QATQuantizer.quantize_with_fusion()`:
-
-```text
-FSDP local shards → full_tensor() all-gather → full HF weight
-→ full-weight amax / global_scale → QKV or gate/up fused_global_scale
-→ per-row, per-group block scale → packed NVFP4 weight + scales
-```
-
-  The cost is the all-gather and GPU staging. The quantizer caches to CPU per decoder layer and moves back to GPU, so peak GPU memory is not necessarily one tensor. [Export][qat-export]
-
-- `get_per_tensor_param_shard()` outputs only the local BF16 shard, with no quantizer and no scale. Shard-local block quantization is an unsupported new protocol and must at least solve:
-  1. aligning shard and block boundaries, or handling cross-shard blocks;
-  2. a collective for the full-weight amax/global scale;
-  3. a consistent fused global scale for QKV and gate/up;
-  4. W4A4 explicitly carrying the activation-derived `input_global_scale`, which cannot be rebuilt from weight shards.
-
-  Until these contracts and the oracle exist, quantizing each shard and concatenating is forbidden.
-- Non-QAT: export BF16 in HF coordinates; BF16 rollout does not quantize, and `rollout.quantization=fp8` is quantized by the receiver. LoRA merge exception: [P6](#p6-lora-mergetrue-bypasses-the-fsdp-qat-export).
-
-#### 4.2 Megatron path
-
-- VERL: ModelOpt installs fake-quant modules; `MegatronEngine.get_per_tensor_param()` exports HF weights through Megatron-Bridge, and `QATWeightExporter` reads the module quantizer's amax/block metadata to produce NVFP4 and scales. [ModelOpt exporter][modelopt-source]
-- VERL FP8 E2E: TE handles FP8 forward/backward in training; when the Bridge declares `export_weight_dtype=fp8`, VERL does not cache generic conversion tasks. The rollout format is decided by `rollout.quantization` and the serving checkpoint contract; FP8 training does not mean exported tensors are in vLLM layout.
-- Megatron capability cannot be inferred as FSDP capability.
-- Distinct artifacts: the offline converter prepares the initial checkpoint (may write to disk); the online exporter streams in memory; post-load reorders without recomputing scale; a training checkpoint is not a servable quantized HF checkpoint.
-
-#### 4.3 Receiver quantization (rollout-only)
-
-`rollout.quantization=fp8`: the trainer exports BF16; `load_quanted_weights()` in the vLLM worker calls `quant_weights()`, which uses `scaled_fp8_blockwise()` to produce the FP8 weight and `weight_scale_inv`, then replays the quant method's post-load. There are also a DeepSeek V4-specific entry and an Ascend MXFP8 branch with different scale naming. [receiver][receiver-source] When the checkpoint is already FP8/MXFP4, confirm whether it is requantization or passthrough. vLLM cannot quantize BF16 online into ModelOpt `MIXED_PRECISION`.
-
-### 5. Minimal adaptation for a new quantization format
-
-1. From the checkpoint config and the actual loader, list key, shape, dtype, block size, packing and fusion group of weight/scale, and the unquantized tensor families.
-2. Trace export -> loader -> post-load and mark the single owner of each family.
-3. If a converter is missing, add the minimal conversion at the existing owner's entry; verify on one tensor / fusion group, then cold-load a small model. Changing the dtype is not a conversion.
-4. Test zero merge and a non-zero update; get quantize-after-full-gather right before shard optimizations.
-
-One evidence table is enough: tensor family -> source -> export format -> serving format -> owner -> unit/small-model verification.
-
-#### Minimal acceptance
-
-- [ ] Record training dtype, export dtype/layout, rollout dtype/layout and owner.
-- [ ] Fixed-token logprob of the zero-adapter path and the base are within the noise baseline of the same backend.
-- [ ] After a non-zero update, tokenwise logprob/KL between trainer and rollout stays within bounds.
-- [ ] name/shape/dtype/count/bytes of packed weight, scale and ignored families all close.
-- [ ] Deployed bytes = `requantize(master)`.
-- [ ] FSDP QAT proves scale is computed after `full_tensor()`; with shard export, prove it is not quantized, or provide the four shard-local contracts of §4.1 and a cross-rank oracle.
-- [ ] Each family is quantized exactly once.
-
-### 6. dtype contract: six boundaries
-
-For each model, record `checkpoint → load/bridge → wrapper/sharding → forward → backward/optimizer → export/serving` separately.
-
-| Boundary | Megatron | VERL/FSDP | Must check |
-| --- | --- | --- | --- |
-| Source weights and conversion | Bridge may reorder, split, cast; model may override default conversion | HF loader, dequantized derived checkpoint, init dtype | Same revision; logical value/scale/layout match, not only target dtype |
-| Parameter storage | `params_dtype` plus model exceptions; FP32 master/optimizer | HF keep-precision list, PEFT master, FSDP shard | An FP32 master does not mean forward uses FP32 |
-| forward parameters | Float16Module converts selectively | FSDP2 `MixedPrecisionPolicy.param_dtype` | Measure inside forward, not only before the wrap |
-| Operator computation and output | TE/FLA/TileLang/fused each define product, accumulation and output precision | HF/PEFT kernel and autocast | FP32 output does not prove FP32 product; BF16 output does not prove BF16 accumulation |
-| Gradient and optimizer | TP/EP/SP/CP collective, DDP | FSDP reduce dtype, gradient accumulation | FP32 reduction does not restore values rounded in forward |
-| Export and serving | Undo the parallel layout, convert adapter/quantization format | gather/export HF adapter | Compare values on the same logical layout |
-
-FP32 protection takes several forms: mark-to-skip before conversion, reset after declaration (which does not restore values already lost), bypassing the default BF16 downcast, and operator-level selection. It is not "all special parameters are raised in precision".
-
-FSDP: HF `_keep_in_fp32_modules_strict` is a load contract and does not become a per-parameter cast exception in FSDP ([P16](#p16-fsdp-bf16-policy-overrides-the-fp32-parameter-contract)). Respect the model's existing contract first, and verify any change of computation precision against a same-model reference and actual serving. `param_dtype=None`, `param_dtype=fp32` and FP32 autocast are different things.

-## QAT, low-precision training and STE
-
-### 1. Choose the precision route first
-
-Rule out input, weight, adapter, layout and operator correctness errors first, then choose precision:
-
-1. When GPU memory allows and rollout can use BF16, use BF16 for both training and inference; check FP32 exception parameters one by one.
-2. When rollout must be low precision (such as NVFP4), use weight QAT or a BF16 actor for training. On Nemotron-H the weight QAT arm is stable. Whether `rollout_is=token` stabilizes the BF16 actor is **not tested**.
-3. Consider real low-precision training last: backward/kernel support and maintenance cost more.
-
-Same dtype is not same computation, and QAT is not bit-exact. QAT and low-precision training shrink the **weight value** gap; the kernel and reduction-order gap goes only when the training forward calls the inference kernels (the BI=1 arm of the [BI switch recipe](recipe-and-acceptance.md)). A natively low-precision model does not necessarily run with `dtype=bf16`; do a capacity pre-check first.
-
-### 2. What the four kinds of path are
-
-| Path | Training forward | backward / optimizer | Is it QAT |
-| --- | --- | --- | --- |
-| High-precision training + low-precision rollout | BF16 weights | High precision | No; quantized only at export |
-| fake-QAT | `DQ(Q(W))`, GEMM is still BF16 | STE sends the gradient back to the high-precision master | Yes |
-| Real low-precision GEMM (FP8/MXFP8/NVFP4) | TE changes the compute kernel | High-precision master/exception tensors remain | Different from fake-QAT |
-| Frozen quantized base + high-precision LoRA | Dequantized base + adapter | Only the adapter is trained | No |
-
-- Neither fake-QAT nor real low-precision training makes the optimizer/gradients low precision. W4A16 quantizes only weights; W4A4 also quantizes inputs.
-- Real low precision: NVFP4 forward is not FP4 backward; configurations include high-precision backward and backward on the dequantized operand.
-- Only weight-only formats can compute scale from the full weight; formats with activation quantization also need activation scale/calibration state, which weights cannot provide. QAT simulation and export follow the same format rules, but scales are not necessarily constant during training.
-- When LoRA is applied separately, do not fake-quant the merged base+adapter yourself.
-- Open-source frameworks (verl [#6992](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/6992), [#7971](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7971), NeMo-RL) essentially only do W4A16; activation inconsistency only appears at W4A8.
-
-### 3. Implementing fake-QAT
-
-Forward form (Nemotron-H):
-
-```text
-w_visible = w + (dequant(requantize(w)) - w).detach()
-```
-
-- `requantize` is the same function as the exporter; replace the library's built-in quantizer when its rules differ.
-- Requantization runs on every forward, and again under full recompute; Nemotron-H step time is about +60%.
-- A temporary `QuantModuleRegistry` replacement and the old class-attribute patch give the same probs_diff mean on the same quick workload (0.0095/0.0091/0.0100 vs 0.0096/0.0092/0.0101); module hit check: [P7](#p7-qat-switch-is-on-target-modules-were-not-replaced).
-
-### 4. How much mismatch QAT can remove
-
-Nemotron-H (`rollout_probs_diff` mean, NVFP4 mixed-precision deployment, single node 4×GB200):
-
-| Approach | Training forward | probs_diff mean |
-| --- | --- | --- |
-| BF16 training + quantized rollout | BF16 weights | About 0.025; no rollout correction |
-| Weight QAT (STE) | Dequantized deployed weights, BF16 GEMM | About 0.010 (pearson 0.986→0.997); three 3-step smoke runs of one recipe, 0.0091-0.0102 |
-| Weight QAT + activation fake-quant | Same, plus static FP8 activations | About 0.0107, about 10% worse than weights only |
-| true on-policy (BI=1) | Deployed bytes + the same kernels as vLLM | max = mean = 0 at every step for 100 steps |
-
-The QAT arm's probs_diff max is still 0.73-1.0; a small mean does not rule out large per-token deviations. Other models (different metrics, not thresholds): DeepSeek-V4 BF16 train + FP8 rollout has a first-step logprob drift of about 0.023 and still reports rising reward/eval ([DeepSeek][dsblog]); Kimi K3 frozen quantized base + LoRA has a train/rollout KL noise floor of about 0.002, a Schulman KL estimate, not a mean absolute logprob diff ([K3][k3blog]).
-
-#### 4.1 Activation fake-quant: aligned per layer, worse end to end
-
-Adding vLLM's static FP8 activation fake-quant to training aligns single-layer output to the BF16 noise floor, but end-to-end probs_diff gets about 10% worse: FP8 rounding is discontinuous, so any element-wise upstream mismatch flips codes and amplifies the difference. To judge, add relative noise δ only to the training-side input and sweep the output error; the crossover was about δ≈1%, and activation quantization hurts when upstream mismatch exceeds it. This is one measurement on one model, not a threshold; for a new model, measure upstream mismatch and repeat the sweep. Nemotron-H did not merge it.
-
-Rule: the weight-side range/axis/scale/rounding must match serving ([rule 3](#key-rules)); matching the activation side depends on upstream mismatch and is not unconditional. Mainstream frameworks (verl, NeMo-RL, slime) use the same **dynamic** activation rule on both sides and do not reuse an external checkpoint's static activation scales; the NeMo-RL Nemotron recipe quantizes only routed experts and leaves Mamba projections, attention and lm_head in BF16. On DeepSeek V4.1, KV quantization simulation adds only about 1.93% improvement on top of R3. Training-side simulation of the FP8 KV cache is not covered.
-
-#### 4.3 When QAT is worth it
-
-Evaluate unified FP8/QAT only when evidence shows the train-inference quantization difference is the main limit; "no score gain" is not a reason to switch precision first. For DSv4.1 rank2 LoRA, the post-merge quantized delta is only 5.1-7.7% of the pre-quantization delta (a norm ratio, not information retention), which only supports treating step size/quantization as controlled variables. The long-running Qwen Flash-Next experiment is same-source BF16/BF16 and does not validate the FP8 rollout route.
-
-### 5. STE contract
-
-The STE surrogate (identity or clipped), whether dX uses the master or dequantized value, scale handling and verification are in [Backward validation](backward-validation.md#write-down-the-gradient-contract-first). By default dX uses the dequantized value; when using the master value, quantify the bias.
-
-### 6. Why QAT does not train
-
-Train-inference consistency is the strictest QAT: forward uses quantized weights, the high-precision master accumulates updates, STE passes the gradient back. Whether it trains depends only on the master's distance to the nearest decision boundary. In W4A16 (the FP4 code is decoded to BF16 in a register and goes through the BF16 tensor core; the gain is 1/4 the weight bandwidth), W4A4 and W8A8 alike, the computed values are "code × scale".
-
-#### 6.1 Dead zone
-
-- Each NVFP4 element has only 8 values, 0/0.5/1/1.5/2/3/4/6 × scale, with RNE rounding. From a dequantized checkpoint the master sits on grid points, half a spacing from every decision boundary, and must travel that half spacing before the code changes.
-- At lr 1e-6 one step moves the master about 0.01%; a few hundred steps move it far less than half a spacing, so deployed values stay byte-for-byte unchanged. RL gradients are more random than SFT, closer to a random walk, and need more steps.
-- Result: NVFP4-covered parameters (on Nemotron-H, routed/shared experts and lm_head, the bulk) have zero deployed change, and validation NLL is clearly worse than the native BF16 baseline; freezing these weights explains about half the gap.
-- Recomputing block scale does not flip codes earlier: from grid points requant is idempotent, the E4M3 scale only changes code after block amax moves 3-6%, and a tiny global scale change only rescales the whole tensor.
-- Mainstream QAT (NeMo-RL QARL, slime/Kimi INT4, Jet-RL) starts from the original BF16 weights, which lie between grid points, so any small drift flips a proportional share of codes and there is no dead zone. INT4 with 1×32 groups from a dequantized checkpoint stalls the same way.
-- FP8 is barely affected: floating-point relative spacing is 6-12%, small elements have small absolute spacing, and some elements are always near a boundary. DS4 also starts from dequantized FP8 and is affected only mildly.
-
-#### 6.2 Fix
-
-Preferred: use the original BF16 weights (the real BF16 release) as the master and requantize every step by the same rule (Nemotron-H: TE 4over6, E4M3 upper bound 256). State two points:
-
-- **θ0 is not equal to the official checkpoint bytes.** Requantizing from the real BF16 release, 99.776% of Nemotron-H's NVFP4 bytes are identical and 24 of 46 FP8 tensors (ModelOpt calibrated scale) differ. "The official checkpoint was generated by this rule" holds only on dequantized weights, where MSE and MAE cannot tell rules apart on grid points ([P2](#p2-verifying-a-rule-with-dequantized-weights-gives-a-false-positive)). Proxy SFT gives the cost: 300-step val NLL A-bf16 3.4685 vs C-dequant 3.4641 / C-bf16 3.4373, about 0.03 nat, present at θ0 and not growing during training. This policy needs human confirmation.
-- **Three acceptance items** (all pass on Nemotron-H): (1) with zero updates, re-exported bytes equal θ0 (not the official checkpoint); (2) fast-tier RL θ0/θ1/θ2 is 0 diff and deployed bytes start changing; (3) proxy SFT gap to the native BF16 baseline is within budget.
-
-Alternative, keeping θ0 bytes: add a fixed small jitter to move the master off grid points (toward the neighboring cell, at most half a step; after requant check per block that bytes are unchanged, and roll back changed blocks). Whichever you choose, state that from a dequantized checkpoint at lr 1e-6, NVFP4 deployed values do not change for roughly the first 10³-10⁴ steps. See [P24](#p24-master-starts-on-the-quantization-grid).
