+# Backward: reuse and validation
+
+## Reusing backward: when you actually need to write your own
+
+When to reuse backward and when to write glue.
+
+### Conclusion
+
+Backward is determined by the **math formula**, not by the forward kernel. The backward of `y = f(x, W)` needs only the formula and the saved inputs: `dX = dY·W`, `dW = dYᵀ·x`. A vLLM forward kernel does not by itself require a new backward. "No backward operator at the same precision" is not a reason to rewrite: under the high_precision contract the backward runs in BF16/FP32 anyway.
+
+### How to wire it: forward once, backward uses what the forward saved
+
+The training forward is the inference forward. Each module is an autograd Function: its forward calls the inference kernel to produce the visible output and saves what its own backward needs (inputs, visible output, LSE, fixed routing IDs, quantized values and scales); its backward uses only those, through a reused library backward or a closed-form VJP. If the inference kernel does not output something the backward needs, change the kernel to output it.
+
+Delivery requires 0 diff and a training step within budget on the main topologies fixed at C1; C6 checks both together. Nemotron audited this against DS4: attention saves q/k/v, out and LSE; routed MoE saves x, the visible FC1 output and the visible output; linear and norms save their inputs; the router saves logits and fixed IDs. Its open gap is Mamba SSD, because vLLM's visible SSD does not output the chunk state.
+
+### Three cases
+
+| Case | Characteristics | Examples | What to do |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| A only rounding differs | Same math; summation order/chunking differs; difference in the last BF16 bit | RMSNorm, Mamba SSD scan, attention, conv1d, unquantized linear | Reuse the training framework's backward (MCore/TE/mamba_ssm); write no code |
+| B forward has rounding | FP8/NVFP4 quantization rounds; the true derivative is 0 almost everywhere | Quantized linear, FP8 Q/K/V | First fix the STE proxy (rounding passes through as 1; dX uses dequantized values by default; DS4 and Nemotron currently approximate with TE high_precision master values, and the deviation must be quantified per [layer 2](#layer-2-gradient-contract-comparison)), then reuse the ordinary BF16 GEMM backward |
+| C no ready-made backward for the whole segment | Composite of several operators with no library backward for the whole segment | Routed experts: sort -> grouped GEMM -> relu² -> restore -> top-k weighted sum | Write glue that chains ready-made operators; GEMM still uses TE grouped GEMM; compare gradients against an independent reference |
+
+Decision flow: (1) does the forward have rounding/quantization (top-k ID selection does not count; IDs are fixed and not differentiated)? No -> A. Yes -> (2) fix the STE contract -> (3) is there a packaged training backward for the whole segment (TE Linear/GroupedLinear, MCore MoE)? Yes -> B, reuse it and feed master values; no -> C, glue. If A has no same-math training implementation, also write only glue. Look first in mLite `primitive/modules` and `ops`, then in MCore/TE/mamba_ssm.
+
+### How DS4 did it
+
+DS4's only hand-written kernel is the small FP8 quantization Triton kernel in the forward. The backward has no hand-written kernel, only PyTorch closed-form formulas and glue, all in FP32.
+
+| Operator | Case | Backward source | What we wrote |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| FP8 dense linear (qkv, shared expert, o-proj) | B | TE `general_gemm`, BF16 master | Nothing |
+| Routed experts (grouped) | B+C | TE `general_grouped_gemm`; reuses gate_up, the output of the forward vLLM FC1, without recomputing | Glue: sort, activation derivative, summation |
+| Sparse attention | A | cuDNN sparse attention backward, consuming the forward's saved out and LSE | Nothing |
+| SwiGLU (with clamp), RMSNorm, q/kv norm, mHC | A | Hand-written closed-form derivative, FP32, `torch.compile` | PyTorch formula |
+| Routing score | A (IDs fixed) | FP32 replay of `sqrt(softplus)` + normalization, handed to autograd | PyTorch formula |
+| Others | A | Generic bridge: forward via vLLM, backward recomputes the PyTorch graph then `autograd.grad` | One utility function |
+
+DS4 wrote its own for four reasons, none of them a missing same-precision backward kernel: (1) library backwards need intermediates from the library's own forward (TE RMSNorm needs rstd, MCore MoE the token permutation; the vLLM forward has neither); (2) model-specific math is not in the library (`sqrt(softplus)` scoring, SwiGLU with clamp, mHC Sinkhorn); (3) discrete selection must copy the forward (recomputed top-k may pick a different expert on ties, so store the IDs and differentiate only the continuous score); (4) the generic bridge costs too much memory and time (autograd stores all 20 mHC iterations; use a closed-form derivative fused with compile). A custom backward function has no autograd graph inside, so its activation derivative must be closed-form (`dynamic_clamped_swiglu_vjp`; likewise relu² in Nemotron `routed_vjp`).
+
+### Three rules when reusing
+
+1. Intermediate definitions must match: attention backward uses the forward's out and LSE, so LSE base (ln or log2), softmax scale and memory layout must line up. If they do not, recompute the forward with the training kernel inside the backward.
+2. Backward need not be bitwise identical: recomputed intermediates differ from the vLLM forward in the last BF16 bit and gradients differ by the same amount, which is allowed. The requirement is that the gradient contract holds and the error is near the noise floor.
+3. Reused code must be verified too, per [layer 1](#layer-1-module-level-vjp-comparison): compare dX and dW against an FP32 reference that does not call the backward under test, with the same dY, in multiples of the noise floor.
+
+### Two test-infrastructure false negatives
+
+- A unit test that instantiated QuantFP8 directly lacked production training's vLLM config context (`CompilationConfig(custom_ops=['none','+quant_fp8'])`, Humming, PP4), and the first long-sequence test failed before computing anything. Fix: the test wrapper uses the production config; production operators and tolerances are unchanged.
+- An import check without GPU visibility makes vLLM select a non-CUDA platform, which cannot import `reshape_and_cache_flash` (exported only on CUDA). Dependency checks need real device visibility.
+- Both are test errors, not train-inference differences.
+
+## Backward validation: is the implementation right, is the approximation reasonable, is training biased
+
+Forward 0 diff shows the logprobs match, not that gradients are right. Validate the backward in three layers:
+
+| Layer | Question answered | Method | Cannot replace |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| 1. Module-level VJP comparison | Does the implementation match the agreed gradient contract (missing scale, wrong transpose, broken gradient chain) | compare dX, dW and a one-step update of every module against an independent reference that does not call the backward under test | layers 2 and 3 |
+| 2. Gradient contract comparison | Is the contract reasonable: does an approximation (e.g. dX from the master value) bias training | same batch, compare gradients under the two conventions per class and per layer | layer 1 |
+| 3. Proxy SFT three-arm comparison | Does the whole training chain have a systematic bias | three SFT paths (under test, gradient reference, native baseline) with the same data and hyperparameters | layers 1 and 2 |
+
+Run 1 → 2 → 3. If layer 1 fails, fix the implementation before any SFT. If layer 3 is abnormal, go back to layers 1 and 2. Passing all three clears the backward; none proves long-term RL stability.
+
+### Write down the gradient contract first
+
+#### The three tiers of a weight
+
+In quantized training one parameter has three values, and the gradient must end up at the one the optimizer manages:
+
+| Tier | Precision | What it is |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| main | FP32 | optimizer state; updates accumulate here |
+| master | BF16 | the model parameter, converted from main every step; non-quantized layers compute with it directly |
+| deployed value | NVFP4 / FP8 etc. | master quantized per the deployment rule; both the training forward and inference use these bytes |
+
+Keep the optimizer's parameter identity: when replacing the forward, do not create parameters the optimizer does not know about. The deployed value is not a trainable parameter.
+
+#### Contract table
+
+A kernel without autograd does not need a surrogate gradient: non-quantized GEMM, norm and attention reuse the existing backward when the math matches; STE is needed only through discrete operations such as quantization rounding. Before implementing, decide per module class:
+
+| Item | What must be decided |
+| --- | --- |
+| Visible forward | the inference implementation; input/output dtype, layout; quantize/dequantize positions, scale granularity, rounding, clamp, accumulation precision |
+| Trainable variables | input, master weight, bias, norm, router; whether scale is fixed, stop-gradient or trainable |
+| Surrogate function | whether dX uses the master or dequantized value (see below); identity or clipped STE, and the value at the threshold |
+| Discrete state | fixed expert IDs, sparse indices, ordering; continuous score/combine weights that still need gradients |
+| backward | reused implementation or custom VJP; cast, accumulation/reduction precision, communication and normalization |
+| Save/recompute | quantized values, scale, norm/attention intermediates, routing, RNG; memory cost and recompute rules |
+| Reference and acceptance | independent reference implementation, target shape/execution path, metrics and tolerances agreed in advance |
+
+Identity STE sets the surrogate derivative of Q(x) to 1; clipped STE sets 1 inside the range and 0 outside, with the threshold value stated and never switched silently. Declare weight and activation quantization separately; frozen weights do not mean nothing upstream of the activations needs gradients.
+
+#### Linear: which weight dX uses
+
+For `Y = X · Wᵀ + b` with upstream gradient `G`:
+
+```text
+dW = Gᵀ · X_ref        # returns to master via STE, then the optimizer updates main
+db = sum_over_tokens(G)
+dX = G · W_ref
+```
+
+Two choices for `W_ref`:
+
+- **Dequantized value**: `W_ref = dequant(quant(W_master))`, the value the forward actually used. This is the true derivative of `Y = X · Wqᵀ` with respect to X, and what fake-quant QAT gets from autograd. **Use this by default.**
+- **Master value**: `W_ref = W_master` (BF16). Reuses the plain BF16 GEMM backward without dequantizing; the cheapest hookup when the inference kernel takes only packed bytes and has no backward. Cost: dX is no longer the exact forward derivative and ignores the quantization error's effect on the input gradient.
+
+The two give different gradients and must not be swapped silently. With the master value, the layer-2 comparison is mandatory: quantify and record the bias. Likewise for activation quantization, state whether `X_ref` is the quantized or original activation.
+
+Before reusing a linear or grouped GEMM backward, check flatten/transpose, padding and valid tokens, bias reduction, saved inputs, scaling and the accumulation/backprop dtype. Matching output shape does not prove reusability.
+
+### Layer 1: module-level VJP comparison
+
+#### How to build the reference implementation
+
+The reference may use PyTorch ops and autograd but **must not call the backward under test**, or both paths share the error. For discrete operations implement the agreed surrogate backward explicitly; the zero gradient of bare rounding is not a reference.
+
+This bridge takes the output value from the inference implementation and the gradient from an independent surrogate. Use it to build the reference path:
+
+```python
+import torch
+
+
+class VisibleWithSurrogate(torch.autograd.Function):
+    @staticmethod
+    def forward(ctx, visible, surrogate):
+        assert visible.shape == surrogate.shape
+        assert visible.device == surrogate.device
+        assert visible.dtype == surrogate.dtype
+        return visible
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def backward(ctx, grad_output):
+        return None, grad_output
+
+
+with torch.no_grad():
+    visible = inference_linear(x, deployment_weight, scales)
+w_ref = dequantize(deployment_weight, scales)  # default contract; use master_weight for the master-value contract
+surrogate = torch.nn.functional.linear(x, w_ref, bias)
+y = VisibleWithSurrogate.apply(visible.detach(), surrogate)
+```
+
+- Build the surrogate graph in normal grad mode, outside the custom Function's forward.
+- With the dequantized surrogate, `w_ref`'s gradient must reach master via STE: bridge a tensor valued as the dequantized weight whose gradient passes straight to master, then feed it to a plain linear.
+- Do not use `visible + surrogate - surrogate.detach()`: floating-point add/subtract and compiler transforms change the result. Do not modify the bridge output in place downstream.
+- This bridge is the independent validation reference, not the production wiring; production wiring is in [How to wire it](#how-to-wire-it-forward-once-backward-uses-what-the-forward-saved).
+- `visible_forward(visible, native, *inputs)` is another way to write the same bridge: `visible` saves inputs without building a graph, `native` is the training framework's implementation of the same math and reruns the forward on those inputs in backward; precision and speed depend on which `native` is chosen.
+
+#### Comparison steps
+
+1. **Fix the state.** Fix inputs, weights, quantization config, mask/routing. Reference and candidate get independent copies; clear accumulated gradients. Check that the visible forward matches inference, then the saved state the backward needs; at integration, confirm the real forward produces that state.
+2. **Same upstream gradient.** Both sides use the same external dY, dtype and values. Cover fixed random, zero, and sparse (non-zero at selected positions) gradients, then samples from real training. `y.sum().backward()` alone misses transpose, permutation and broadcast errors.
+3. **Compare item by item.** Compare dX, dW and every bias/norm/router/scale gradient separately: missing, shape, finiteness, non-zero where expected. Do not ignore unused differentiable inputs by default; list parameters the branch genuinely does not use. Report max absolute error, relative L2 `‖g − g_ref‖₂ / max(‖g_ref‖₂, eps)`, norm ratio and cosine; direction alone is not enough. With a zero norm the cosine is undefined; use absolute error.
+4. **Set tolerances in advance.** Derive atol/rtol and the relative L2 threshold from dtype, reduction length and reference precision; record the reasoning. No single threshold for all modules, no relaxing after a failure, and no relaxing a same-semantics kernel optimization because "STE is an approximation anyway". Cross-framework bitwise identity is not required.
+5. **Coverage.** Small M (decode), large M (training/prefill), different context lengths, unaligned tails, padding/packing/mask, zeros and extreme values; both sides of the quantization threshold, the saturation region, different scales. For MoE cover empty experts, repeated routing, shared experts, top-k ties; for shared parameters check gradient accumulation across use sites. Test under the target dtype/layout, recompute, autocast, CUDA Graph, gradient accumulation and the actual parallel reduction; local first, then integrated.
+6. **One-step update.** From the same parameters and optimizer state, run one update each and compare the change in master. If gradients are close but updates differ, check scaling, clipping, optimizer state and parameter binding.
+
+Cross-check smooth non-quantized modules with small, high-precision [gradcheck](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.autograd.gradcheck.html) or finite differences: fix the discrete branch, avoid non-smooth boundaries, and perturb the weights the forward actually sees. **Do not validate STE with finite differences of the real quantized forward**: that measures the discrete forward, which the STE surrogate derivative deliberately differs from.
+
+#### What to check per module
+
+| Module | Reuse first | Semantics to check |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Dense/QKV/LM head | training linear/grouped VJP, gradient returns to master | dX value convention, cast, bias, gradient accumulation of shared parameters |
+| Norm/RoPE | existing training VJP, FP32 statistics if needed | epsilon, RMS or LayerNorm, position offset, rotation layout |
+| Activation + quantization | the actual composition of activation derivative and STE | saturation region, whether scale is detached, fusion order |
+| Attention/sparse attention | training backward with the same mask/index semantics | causal boundary, softmax scale, LSE definition, GQA, order of selected KV; do not mix auxiliary quantities from different forwards |
+| MoE | expert linear/grouped VJP and a differentiable combine | inverse dispatch permutation, gradient accumulation of repeated tokens, empty experts, shared experts, top-k weight normalization |
+| Router/sparse selection | fix the discrete selection, keep the continuous score's derivative | no continuous gradient for IDs/indices; do not detach the whole router output |
+| Linear attention/SSM | training backward with the same chunked arithmetic | chunk boundary, initial state, state precision, conv state |
+| Selected logprob | log-softmax/gather VJP matching the definition | vocab-shard reduction, temperature, token mask, loss normalization |
+
+Recompute must save or deterministically rebuild the scale, routing/indices, RNG and necessary intermediates, and must not switch the surrogate function.
+
+### Layer 2: gradient contract comparison
+
+Layer 1 answers "does the implementation equal the contract", not "is the contract reasonable". When the contract contains an approximation (most often dX from the master instead of the dequantized value), quantify its distance from the exact derivative:
+
+1. On a fixed checkpoint and batch, compute dX (and gradients related to activation quantization) for every quantized layer under both conventions.
+2. Report cosine and norm ratio per module class and per layer; inspect outlier layers.
+3. Measure each target precision combination separately: changing weight or activation precision changes the bias.
+
+On Nemotron-H (NVFP4 routed experts, FP8 Mamba projections), master-value and dequantized-value dX have cosine ≈0.99 and norm ratio ≈1.00 per class and layer, with both BF16 and FP8 activations, so this approximation does not cause the training score gap. Remeasure for other precisions, a larger learning rate or longer training.
+
+### Layer 3: Proxy SFT three-arm comparison
+
+After the first two layers pass, run a controlled SFT over the whole training chain:
+
+| Path | Visible forward | backward | Purpose |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Under test | aligned inference numerics | production backward | the scheme to deliver |
+| Gradient reference | same as under test at the same parameter snapshot | independent surrogate reference (the bridge above works) | isolate backward implementation errors |
+| Native baseline | original training numerical path | verified original training backward | measure the recipe's overall quality change |
+
+- First compare gradients and one-step update of under-test vs gradient-reference on a fixed checkpoint and batch, then run curves; once trajectories diverge, visible values differ too. The under-test vs native-baseline gap includes quantization and forward-path differences, not only backward. If the gradient reference's full curve is unaffordable, compare on representative batches and state the missing range.
+- Controlled variables: initial weights and optimizer state, data and order, labels/mask, packing, loss normalization, global batch and gradient accumulation, learning rate and schedule, clipping, precision and loss scaling, seed, recompute policy.
+- Record train loss, fixed-validation-set NLL, gradient norm, update RMS, clipping ratio, non-finite values, throughput, against optimizer step or cumulative effective tokens. Fix the comparison window and acceptable deviation before the run; a short run is only a smoke test.
+- Localization: loss differs at the initial weights -> check forward, data, mask; initial loss matches but one-step update differs -> backward, reduction, scale, clipping, optimizer; diverges only after several steps -> save the first abnormal checkpoint, check recompute, quantization refresh, learning rate, RNG, then replay at the same weights.
+- Mark unexplained or unbudgeted differences inconclusive; do not cover them with forward 0 diff.
+
+On Nemotron-H the three paths (aligned trainer with BF16 activations, Megatron QAT, Megatron BF16) ran 40 steps on gsm8k with the same data in the same order: loss 0.3388 / 0.3383 / 0.3374, gradient norm 0.685 / 0.674 / 0.728, curves overlapping. The training loop itself is fine; the RL score gap comes from RL-specific factors.
+
+### Common false differences
+
+Each of these made gradients look mismatched when the comparison method was the problem:
+
+- **Upstream gradient precision differs.** FP32 dY on one side and BF16-rounded dY on the other creates a difference unrelated to the backward. Use the same external dY.
+- **Dump timing.** Expert gradients are multiplied by the expert-DP to DP scaling ratio only inside the optimizer step; dumping earlier shows a false multiplicative difference.
+- **Unsharded copy under FSDP2.** After forward-only the root module is not resharded, so the parameter fetched by name is the unsharded compute copy, not the real master. Perturbing it or reading its gradient both mislead.
+- **"Frozen" is not frozen.** Zeroing the gradient still lets AdamW weight decay change the parameter; a real freeze needs grad None or removal from the optimizer.
+- **Test environment differs from production.** A unit test missing production config context, or an import without GPU visibility, selects the wrong implementation or fails to import (see [Two test-infrastructure false negatives](#two-test-infrastructure-false-negatives)).
+
+### What to write in the report
+
+Per module class: gradient contract (dX value choice, STE type, scale handling), reference implementation, upstream gradient construction, shapes/paths covered, metrics and tolerances with reasoning. Layer 2: per-class per-layer cosine/norm ratio and outlier layers. Layer 3: config diff table of the three paths, curves, conclusion within the window. List missing coverage explicitly, not as "the rest is analogous".
+
+For the basic definition of STE see [Bengio et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.3432); it does not decide the surrogate gradient rule for a specific model.

+# Checkpoint, resume and memory budget
+
+Use this guide to get checkpoint save, load and resume right in long RL runs, and to budget host (CPU) memory peaks and growth. For per-phase GPU memory peaks see [Locating GPU OOM and staging peaks by lifecycle](#locating-gpu-oom-and-staging-peaks-by-lifecycle).
+
+## Find by symptom
+
+| Symptom | Where to go |
+| --- | --- |
+| OOM while loading a checkpoint | [Load](#4-load-enough-capacity-does-not-mean-enough-for-the-transient-peak) |
+| Train-inference mismatch on the first step after restore | [13](#13-stale-quantization-scale-on-the-first-step-after-restore) |
+| Resume is set but training starts from step 0 | [14](#14-resume_modeauto-starts-from-step-0) |
+| Host RSS grows every step | [3.3](#33-locating-slowly-grows-every-step) |
+| Planning host memory for a checkpoint in the hundreds of GB | [4](#4-capacity-planning) |
+| vLLM fails to start when colocated with training (KV budget too small) | [5](#5-gpu-memory-set-gpu_memory_utilization-per-mode-when-training-and-rollout-are-colocated) |
+| GPU OOM during init / export / wake | [Locating GPU OOM](#locating-gpu-oom-and-staging-peaks-by-lifecycle) |
+
+## Terms
+
+- **pinned memory:** page-locked host memory for direct GPU DMA (`cudaHostAlloc` / `cudaHostRegister`), cached by PyTorch's caching host allocator.
+- **cgroup:** limit `memory.max`, usage `memory.current`, split in `memory.stat` into anon, file (page cache) and shmem.
+- **RSS and PSS:** RSS counts shared pages fully in every process; PSS splits them, so only summed PSS approximates the physical total.
+- **DCP / Megatron dist_ckpt:** PyTorch and Megatron distributed checkpoint formats; each rank writes its shard, `.metadata` last.
+- **staging / D2H:** the host buffer GPU tensors are copied into before writing to disk.
+- **Ray object store (plasma):** Ray's shared memory for passing objects, mapped into each worker and charged via PSS.
+- **old-logprob:** the logprob training recomputes for rollout tokens with the pre-update policy.
+- **Ray OOM threshold:** `RAY_memory_usage_threshold`, the usage fraction at which Ray kills workers. Default 0.95.
+
+## Key rules
+
+- Check file, memory and derived state separately; complete files can still mismatch on the first step after restore.
+- Capture the first exception (errno, rank, file, offset), not the last message.
+- Completion marker last; clear the old directory before overwriting; all ranks check and fail together; a missing file raises instead of falling back to a fresh optimizer.
+- Under EP4 + FSDP2, ranks' expert shards in DCP share key and offset, so restore reads another rank's experts. Put the EP rank in the key (port the reference fix), add a 4-GPU bitwise read-back unit test, and raise on EP size mismatch.
+- Rotation deletes only tracked, complete, idle directories; in long runs keep one checkpoint every 20 steps outside rotation.
+- Set rollout `gpu_memory_utilization` per training mode ([5](#5-gpu-memory-set-gpu_memory_utilization-per-mode-when-training-and-rollout-are-colocated)).
+- Save fixes pass [the acceptance in 3.2](#32-reproduce-and-discriminate). Before a long run on a new save path or layout, run to the first save and do one kill→resume.
+- Resume is proven by matching per-rank digests in a new process, a byte-identical first export, an aligned first old-logprob and one non-zero update; `resume_mode=auto` alone proves nothing.
+- Read host memory as anon/file/shmem; `memory.current` includes page cache, and Ray kills on it.
+- Pinned buffers round up to a power of 2 (Nemotron: 146.9 GiB pinned for 88.2 GiB of optimizer state, +67%); allocate large long-lived pinned blocks at exact size.
+- The save step is the peak; a higher Ray threshold or smaller microbatch does not fix headroom.
+- For per-step growth, use the per-process PSS floor and a small CPU-only repro before changing code.
+- Verify per save path that the host cache is released after save.
+
+## Checkpoint and resume
+
+### 1. Three independent contracts
+
+Classify the problem before calling it "the checkpoint is broken":
+
+| Contract | Typical failure |
+| --- | --- |
+| File: serialization and publish | Disk write error; an incomplete directory treated as complete |
+| Memory: transient peaks of save and load | Killed by Ray after the write finishes; cgroup OOM during load |
+| Derived state: the first export after restore | Files complete, but the first step after restore mismatches ([stale quantization scale](#13-stale-quantization-scale-on-the-first-step-after-restore)) |
+
+The third class is a derived-state lifecycle bug, not file corruption.
+
+### 2. Which state exact resume needs
+
+| State | Requirement |
+| --- | --- |
+| Model parameters or LoRA adapter shards | Saved per rank; strict load that rejects missing/unexpected keys ([training forward](training-forward.md)) |
+| Optimizer state, including the CPU-offloaded part | Same step as the model. Nemotron chunked optimizer offload: 88.2 GiB per rank, 94.7 GB per rank on disk; DS4.1 saves LoRA parameters and Adam `exp_avg` / `exp_avg_sq` in FP32 |
+| LR scheduler | Check the saved value, not the source default (DS4.1 checks its constant, no-warmup schedule per rank) |
+| RNG | Four streams: CPU, CUDA, Python, NumPy |
+| Counters and data position | global step, optimizer step, data cursor; DS4.1 also saves the cumulative count of effective-signal steps |
+| Run contract | Hashes of code, data and recipe, compared item by item on restore; reject a change in total steps or data by default. To extend training, declare a new phase explicitly; do not edit the old contract file or add a generic ignore switch |
+| Completion marker | `.metadata` / tracker (e.g. `latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt`), written last, see 3.4 |
+
+Not in the checkpoint, rebuilt after restore:
+
+- **Parameter-derived caches:** quantization scale, packed/transposed/fused weight, version markers (see 5).
+- **Records outside training:** the metrics jsonl is overwritten on resume.
+
+### 3. Save
+
+#### 3.1 Capture the first error, do not fix the last error message
+
+Keep the writer callback's original exception / errno, rank, path, offset, requested / returned bytes and exception chain, which DCP and Ray wrappers may drop; also filesystem/mount, free space, quota and cgroup OOM events, not just the final `ActorDiedError`. `unexpected pos` can come from disk space, quota, permissions or I/O failure; the first exception tells them apart.
+
+#### 3.2 Reproduce and discriminate
+
+A fast repro keeps the real tensors, serializer and concurrency, skips rollout/backward and repeats only save, for a bounded number of rounds sized to the failure probability; stop at the first failure and keep the scene. DS4 model-only save failed on the 3rd attempt on one path and the 6th on another; Nemotron with host cache release failed on the 2nd-4th save.
+
+**Acceptance for a save fix: N consecutive saves + kill→resume→save again.** Also run it before the first long run of a new save path, parallel layout or node count; running to the first save point is enough.
+
+Order of discrimination:
+
+1. Same buffer/serializer, target filesystem versus node-local disk as the control; read the errno of the first failure.
+2. Control concurrency, pinned/pageable and memory peak; if the serializer changed along with the filesystem, the result cannot be attributed to one factor.
+3. Check growth of threads, processes and file handles, separately from the write error.
+4. Only then read kernel / filesystem client code; a matching historical issue is supporting evidence, not proof of a fix.
+
+#### 3.3 Reliable publish
+
+Serialize on node-local disk and close the file; copy to a **temporary name on the target filesystem**, handle short copies, flush/fsync as durability requires, verify integrity, then rename within the same filesystem. Publish metadata/tracker/completion marker only after all ranks finish. A move across filesystems is not an atomic rename.
+
+#### 3.4 Commit protocol: write the completion marker last
+
+| Rule | If you do not |
+| --- | --- |
+| Write `.metadata` / tracker last, after every rank's shards and auxiliary files (optimizer, RNG, scheduler) succeed and are confirmed collectively | A rank fails, the marker already exists, and restore reads incomplete state |
+| Before overwriting a step directory, delete all old files first (uncommit) | Old optimizer / RNG silently pair with the new model |
+| Before restore, all ranks check file completeness together and fail together | The rank missing a file exits; the others hang until the NCCL timeout |
+| Ranks with no shard to write still join the same collective | Collective order diverges across ranks and hangs |
+| A requested load with a missing file raises an error, not just a log line | Training silently continues with a fresh optimizer |

+Acceptance: a save failing midway (Nemotron hit a real ENOSPC) makes all ranks exit together without advancing the tracker, and training resumes directly; new code loads an old-code checkpoint. Never kill a job mid-write; verify the checkpoint is complete first.

+Check the expected shard set, non-empty sizes, leftover temporary files, checksums where needed, and do one real full restore. A correct save digest is not a restore test (DS4.1 checkpoints 20/24 had correct save digests but were never restored in a new process, and the report says so).

+
+Load may copy the full optimizer into anonymous memory, and FSDP CPU offload may create a second set of pinned storage. Accept by loading model + optimizer + RNG/extra at real scale, not one small shard.

+Read a checkpoint with the image that wrote it: DS4.1 host PyTorch 2.11 cannot deserialize the DTensor `_FlatLayout` written by the image's 2.13; it reads only inside the image with `torch.load(weights_only=True, mmap=True, map_location="cpu")`. +### 5. Derived state after restore
+
+DS4 chain: initial HF load saves FP8 source scales → DCP restores the trained BF16 parameters → the first export still uses the old registry → the actor re-quantizes by parameter version, but rollout uses the old scales. The first resumed step mismatches; once the next optimizer hook clears the cache it matches. The prediction "it recovers on the next step" plus a before/after-fix comparison on the same checkpoint locates the cause.

+Fix it in the lifecycle that owns the state: after load/update, invalidate or rebuild parameter-derived caches (scale, packed/transposed/fused weight, version markers), reusing an existing hook without side effects such as a real optimizer update. DS4's minimal patch calls the existing post-update hook ([Megatron-LM #197](https://github.com/ISEEKYAN/Megatron-LM/pull/197)). List every parameter-derived cache and its invalidation code, add the missing calls and one regression test.

+4. **One non-zero update.** A zero-advantage step only exercises the flow (two DS4.1 resume segments had zero gradient on all ranks at step 2, proving nothing about restored adapter values).

+
+| Item | Record |
+| --- | --- |
+| Size per checkpoint and save time | DS4 full32: 99 files, about 3.2 TiB, save about 269 s. Nemotron-H 30B-A3B, 4×GB200: 353 GB (EP4 + FSDP2) or 429 GB (PP4 dist_opt), save 72-152 s, about 2-3% of step time when saving every 5 steps. Layout-specific; state these for your model in the plan |
+| Rotation | The mLite engine ignores `max_actor_ckpt_to_keep` |
+| Checkpoint used for eval | Rotation may have deleted the step to evaluate; a checkpoint from another chain cannot substitute |
+| Resume on a different node after node failure | Copy checkpoint, dequantization cache, pinned image and dependency cache to the new node before launch; disable automatic requeue; change only the node selection; write a transfer record |
+| Paths for two-arm experiments | BI=0 / BI=1 output and checkpoint paths are separate; renaming the run breaks a resume chain in progress ([recipe and acceptance](recipe-and-acceptance.md#rules)) |

+## Memory budget: host and GPU
+
+Host memory fails in two ways in long RL runs: phase **peaks** (save / load / sleep) hitting the limit, and slow per-step **growth**; they are measured differently (1-4). GPU memory is a third class: with training and rollout colocated, rollout `gpu_memory_utilization` is set per training mode (5).
+
+### 1. Who holds host memory
+
+| Source | Mechanism |
+| --- | --- |
+| Pinned buffer of optimizer offload | The caching host allocator rounds up to a power of 2, so the footprint is tens of percent above the nominal state; summed across ranks it pushes residency before save close to the limit |
+| Parameter shards of FSDP CPU offload | Each rank's shard stays resident on CPU; doubles if load creates a second pinned copy |
+| D2H staging during save | Stays in the pinned cache pool; whether `torch.accelerator.empty_host_cache()` releases it must be verified per save path |
+| CPU backup of serving sleep | L1 sleep keeps one full backup per rank; the pinned cache is not returned after wake |
+| Ray object store | plasma mappings count into each process's PSS as shared pages; node shmem does not grow with it (3) |

+`param_offload` trades CPU pressure for GPU memory; optimizer offload is separate. Change one offload switch at a time and measure the phase peak before and after.
+
+### 2. Limits and who does the killing
+
+- **cgroup.** The job limit `memory.max` is usually below physical memory; budget against it. A cgroup OOM shows an `oom_kill` event and process SIGKILL, with no Python stack.
+- **Ray memory monitor.** Kills workers at `RAY_memory_usage_threshold`=0.95 by default; log line `exceeded threshold of <bytes>B (95.0% ...)`. Its usage figure includes page cache. Raising the threshold does not fix headroom: Nemotron at 0.985 was still killed during save.
+- Distinguish GPU allocation exception, host cgroup OOM and Ray kill. A CUDA allocator allocation-failure / retry warning is not a terminal OOM and the step may complete, but it does show memory pressure.
+
+### 3. How to measure
+
+#### 3.1 One record per phase
+
+Log one line at load, save, sleep, wakeup, reset KV cache and generation start / end, with monotonic time, node / rank / PID and policy version. +
+`generate_sequences` includes wake/init. An error inside it does not prove token generation started, let alone a backward/optimizer OOM.
+
+#### 3.2 Pitfalls in the readings
+
+| Reading | Problem |
+| --- | --- |
+| `memory.current` | Includes page cache, which masks per-step growth; but it is what Ray and the save peak see |
+| `free`, `psutil.virtual_memory().used` | System-visible memory, not process RSS or job cgroup usage |
+| `scontrol` FreeMem | Excludes reclaimable cache |
+| `ru_maxrss`, Slurm MaxRSS | Cumulative peak, not current RSS |
+| VmPin/VmLck | Cannot alone infer CUDA pinned |
+| Sum of per-process RSS | Counts shared mappings repeatedly; use PSS |

+Pinned memory from cudaHostAlloc shows up as shmem in cgroup `memory.stat` (measured on Nemotron).

+#### 3.3 Locating "slowly grows every step"

+1. Use node `MemTotal−MemAvailable` and cgroup anon/file/shmem to find which class grows.

+### 4. Capacity planning
+
+Budget the save-step peak as the sum of what is alive at the same time, against cgroup limit × Ray threshold:
+
+```text
+peak  ≈ resident pinned optimizer offload (actual footprint after allocator rounding)
+      + save D2H staging (and the part of it left in the cache pool)
+      + page cache of the newly written checkpoint files
+      + CPU backup of serving sleep and unreleased pinned cache
+      + resident amount of the other processes (rollout, driver, Ray workers, etc.; take the floor per 3.3)

+```

+| --- | --- | --- |
+| EP4 + FSDP2 (mLite; BI=1 arm default `ACTOR_OPTIMIZER=fsdp2`) | Not measured separately | 0.65 (verified) |
+| dist_opt (BI=1 arm optional `ACTOR_OPTIMIZER=dist_opt`; numbers from PP4 dist_opt measurements) | 54-64 GiB (FP32 quantization master resident on GPU) | 0.7, 0.6 and 0.65 fail to start; measured 0.55 |

+host RSS / container or Ray limit

+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Init / FSDP wrap | Full materialization before sharding; largest single parameter; CPU-resident/tied parameters | Whether meta → shard → load takes effect; per-rank peak |
+| forward / backward | Full module from all-gather, activation, workspace | Measure logprob and actor update separately; frozen parameters may be gathered too |
+| Export / merge / quantize | A single full tensor, fused groups, lazy generator references | The actual export set; release timing after yield/exception |
+| compile / graph capture | autotune workspace and graph pool | Find the allocation in the log; eager only isolates, recheck the production graph separately |
+| KV planning / wake | KV budget, trainer residency, allocator free cache | Resolved GMU/TP and allocator metrics, not the configured value |
+| checkpoint / host | Full CPU copy, optimizer gather, shared mappings, Ray guard | Per-process and node usage; RSS does not sum to the physical total |

+A small model with the same special layers, attention period and scale layout verifies the mechanism; only the full model verifies capacity, such as the all-gather peak of a huge single parameter.

+After update's temporaries are freed, PyTorch keeps the blocks as reserved-but-unallocated. Another allocator such as CuMem cannot use them.

+`empty_cache()` releases free cache only, not live tensors, and not reserved memory held by active blocks or a graph's private pool. `gc.collect()` helps only when collecting a reference cycle drops a tensor's last owner; high reserved alone does not prove GC is needed.

+### 4. How to tell a fix from a config downgrade

+
+- A configured path is not an executed path: record a marker/count and treat zero hits as an invalid verification.
+- Before comparing tensors, align request, token position, rank/owner and valid region; equal byte hashes alone do not prove the same objects.

+
+### 13. Stale quantization scale on the first step after restore

+- **Cause and Fix:** See [5](#5-derived-state-after-restore).

+# Fault localization and mismatch bisect
+
+Use this when training and rollout do not match, or a stage of a multi-node run died. It finds the first divergence with the fewest observations and produces a reviewable root cause, without dumping the whole model and without changing precision first. Performance attribution is in [Performance](performance.md); OOM and staging peaks are in [Checkpoint, resume and memory budget](checkpoint-resume.md).
+
+## Symptom → first step
+
+| Symptom | Do first |
+| --- | --- |
+| Not bitwise identical already at θ0 | [01 Isolate the side first](#isolate-the-side-first): four control groups; whichever two are equal rule out that side |
+| Only some sequences are wrong | 01 same-prefix sibling: two samples of the same prompt must be bitwise identical over the shared prefix, otherwise it is the engine side |
+| Wrong starting from some token position | [02 Bisect](#bisect-and-first-divergence): single-request prefill, bisect along one axis of layer/module/position |
+| The difference grows slowly with training (θ0 is basically right) | [01 Isolate the side first](#isolate-the-side-first): save a small batch of prompt/response, score repeatedly at the same version to get each side's noise floor, then compare early and late adapters |
+| Same operator input, still different | [Numerical contracts](../workflow/README.md), [BI kernel appendix table](bi-kernels.md) |
+| Multi-node will not start / NCCL errors | [05 Communication fault ladder](#gb200-first-tell-apart-topology-implementation-mode-and-build) |
+| Not sure what to save to be able to reproduce | [06 Save and compare protocol](#save-and-compare-protocol) |

+## Key rules
+
+1. Find the earliest divergence, not the largest layer; all later differences propagate from earlier ones.
+2. Isolate the side before bisecting; classify before changing precision: input mismatch → weight mismatch → discrete path mismatch → kernel numerics → precision contract. Precision comes last.
+3. Align probes by semantics (LSE in ln or log2, before or after norm, before or after the residual add). Misaligned probes produce false divergences.
+4. Stop bisecting at a discrete decision (top-k, index); fix the routing, then continue.
+5. A single round does not count; hidden coupling (one switch also changed scheduling) cannot be attributed to the switch; the target path must actually be exercised, otherwise the result is VACUOUS.
+6. A two-node test must prove cross-node transfer happened; successful initialization does not mean bandwidth is reasonable; one `max_abs=0` does not prove consistency for arbitrary batches.

+6. **Return to the original failing path.** After the fix, re-verify with the real adapter, input and run config. Passing with reduced layers/eager does not replace verifying the full model, decode, or CUDA Graph/MTP.
+
+### Per-module dump: find the earliest divergence, not the largest layer
+
+1. Build a semantic mapping table: layer, function, input/output role, module path on both sides, logical shape. FSDP wrapper names and fused vs separate Q/K/V need not match; combine before comparing.
+2. Capture block boundaries and final logits first, on a few tokens/samples; refine the earliest significantly divergent block into norm, projection, router, expert, residual etc.
+3. Align valid tokens, position, mask, TP/FSDP shards, expert ID, dimension order and padding. Never compare a physical shard with the full tensor.
+4. A hook takes a snapshot, not an overwritable reference, and never changes the computation. +
+Build a cross-stack boundary table: embedding, residual stream, norm input/output, Q/K/V, compressed rows/index, attention output, router logits/indices, expert input/output, combine, lm_head and scorer. EP dispatch may reorder, duplicate or pad tokens; align expert tensors by semantic token/expert/shard key, not local offset. Give adjacent or fused GEMMs separate boundaries by default.
+
+### Minimal but credible observations
+
+- Copy tensors before buffer reuse; save only necessary boundaries and tokens, with a byte cap. Model-specific mappings and artifacts stay in the model working directory.
+- The manifest records code/image version, checkpoint and adapter identity, input digest, position/mask, dtype/quantization, score semantics, graph/MTP, rank/layout and intervention options. Same config does not mean same weights.
+- One directory per call; write the manifest after completion. Refuse comparison on missing boundaries, repeated calls, or incompatible version/shape; do not silently take the intersection or truncate. Non-finite values fail explicitly; metrics on zero norm are marked undefined.
+- Compare max abs, MAE, relative L2, cosine; for final full-vocab logits also log-softmax, probability total variation and argmax.
+
+### Recommended logs: identity + metric measurement basis + evidence boundary
+
+Reuse existing logs and JSON artifacts; no extra logging framework. One manifest per run, one detailed report per comparison. The terminal prints summaries, not full tensors. Mark unknown fields unknown; do not backfill them as verified.
+
+```text
+[mismatch] run=<id> step=<n> policy=<digest> input=<sha> phase=<prefill|decode> rank=<n> repeat=<n>
+  scope=<fixed-input|independent-rollout> intervention=<none|name>
+  metric=<name> value=<number> reference=<run/repeat/boundary>
+  self_repeat=<noise> report=<relative-path> classification=<defect|numerical|quantization|unknown>
+```
+
+`metric` uses the names in [Metric measurement basis](#metric-measurement-basis) (`logprob_mae`, `probability_mae`, KL diagnostic statistic, tensor relative L2, vocab TV), never interchangeably.
+
+Time load, rollout, score and update separately so cold start is not counted as training. A distributed job's outer console log is only a forwarded copy: when updates stop, check TaskRunner/worker raw logs, checkpoint times and completed steps first. One forward/backward stack does not prove a hang; do not restart a healthy job because log forwarding stopped.
+
+### Limits of bisect
+
+A floating-point difference may vanish in later rounding, masking or routing, so "this layer differs" is not monotonic in depth and O(log L) does not always find the first difference. Coarse-scan for a suspect interval, then bisect/fine-scan, verify the boundaries before it, and confirm responsibility with the same operator input.
+
+A cut point must carry the complete state: residual, MHC mix, SSM/conv state, KV, positions, routing and necessary metadata. A fused upper-layer post and this layer's pre have no natural independent cut point. Prefix replacement that drops hidden state creates new differences.
+
+Only a same-input operator A/B separates upstream propagation from this operator's error. Injecting reference activations, fixing the routing or replacing the kernel can confirm causality, but they are diagnostic interventions; accept the production fix only after restoring the original path.
+
+### Form a reviewable root cause
+
+The result must contain: the minimal input, the last identical/earliest different boundary, the same-input control, the source mechanism, the trigger condition, and the minimal change that makes the failure disappear. A config difference is only a lead: in Nemotron, running both reduction block sizes with the same kernel gave consistent results for both, which overturned the guess that the block size difference was the cause.
+
+If after three rounds only the final score is known to differ, add observation points or re-check the sample mapping instead of rerunning in full. Keep the failing samples and the ruled-out hypotheses so the next round does not repeat them.
+
+### Conclusion and stop conditions
+
+The report answers only: what was observed, what the controls proved, what is not yet proven, and one minimal next step. Correctness errors must be fixed. Normal numerical differences are judged by noise and task impact. Quantization error needs same-input evidence; low-precision inference alone is not grounds to blame it. When improvement is needed, evaluate in order: supported high-precision rollout, QAT matching serving, real low-precision training. Do not cover wrong weights or adapters by changing precision.
+
+**Replacing with the reference output is diagnosis, not a fix. Lower local error does not mean lower training mismatch; per-operator ablation gains do not add up.** Stop once this round's evidence goal is reached; do not change the training config or start new experiments along the way.
+
+## Classification and handling order
+
+After isolating the side ([01](#isolate-the-side-first)) and bisecting ([02](#bisect-and-first-divergence)), classify the difference, then decide what to touch. Precision comes last. Model-specific probes, runtime patches and measurements stay in the model working directory.
+
+### Classification table
+
+| Class | Evidence | Handling |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Correctness error | Missing weights, wrong mask/position/layout, wrong scale/block, wrong quantization range, operator semantics violate the contract | Must be fixed and the original failing path re-verified; for a diagnostic task, deliver the reproducer and evidence first, without widening modify permission |
+| Normal floating-point difference | Explained by same-version repeatability/reduction/kernel noise, no contract error found | Report the noise floor and task impact; bit-exact is not the only pass condition |
+| Error from correct quantization | Mapping and quantization rules are correct, and a same-input control localizes the divergence to the quantization path | Precision ablation in the order below |
+| Unlocalized | Insufficient evidence or confounded variables | Keep unknown, continue with minimal probes, do not declare "it is just quantization" |
+
+Precision ablation order: supported and affordable high-precision rollout → QAT matching the serving rules → real low-precision training (most backend requirements, last). A natively quantized model does not support BF16 just by changing the dtype. Fake quant must match the serving weight/activation rules but does not reproduce its GEMM. QAT is not a workaround for a wrong scale. QAT contract and route selection: [precision guide](precision-quant.md#1-choose-the-precision-route-first).
+
+Keep a single checkpoint source; open a separate high-precision adapter branch when needed.
+
+### Handling order
+
+Input mismatch → weight mismatch → discrete path mismatch (top-k, index) → kernel numerics → precision contract. Rule out each item before moving to the next.
+
+Acceptance: after the fix, the same failing probe passes, the original path is not broken, and error growth on fixed samples is explained/controlled; then look at training process metrics and the fixed task evaluation. Set tolerances from the model and the baseline; do not copy another model's 0.002. Statistics on a fixed old trajectory are diagnostics, not a KL estimate of the current policy.
+
+This procedure does not authorize stopping jobs, switching dtype, adding GPUs or changing the production recipe. When the next diagnostic gate needs new permissions/resources, report the smallest next probe and its cost.
+
+### Delivery
+
+Follow [06 Save and compare protocol](#save-and-compare-protocol): manifest, bounded dump, comparison table, semantic boundary of the earliest divergence, classification and confidence, one next step; state which paths were actually tested. No separate framework, no cross-model universal threshold.
+
+A case that looks like precision but is a switch-scope correctness error: [determinism takes effect only on the main thread](bi-kernels.md#determinism-takes-effect-only-on-the-main-thread).
+

+| What to ask | Example record |
+| --- | --- |
+| Which implementation | AllToAll, some version of DeepEP, HybridEP; note the fork/revision |
+| Which path of that implementation | The actual class, API and kernel behind high-throughput / low-latency / v2 |
+| How it communicates | NVLink within a node; RDMA across nodes; or the MNNVL path actually enabled |
+| What it was compiled into | 4-peer/8-peer macro, target GPU, NVSHMEM dynamic dependency |

+MNNVL being off does not rule out cross-node EP: the verified path may be NVLink within a node and RDMA NICs across nodes. Nor does that path work on every GB200; devices, network, peer build, underlying libraries and the called API all need verification.

+### Same-fabric fairness
+
+Before any communication-bound A/B, prove both arms use the same transport. In one GB200 NVL case the BI=0 arm's NCCL AllGather/ReduceScatter went `via P2P/MNNVL` (same clique, cliqueSize 8) while the BI=1 arm's DeepEP low-latency a2a was pinned to RoCE (`VLLM_DEEPEP_LOW_LATENCY_USE_MNNVL=0`, `NVSHMEM_HCA_PREFIX=rocep`); a gap blamed on non-overlappable communication latency was mostly the wrong NIC, fixed by two environment variables.

+
+Large tensors and checkpoints stay in `results/<run-id>/`; source and small summaries go into version control. +### Archive experiment material by step

+```text
+<workspace>/
+  steps/

Large files go to persistent storage with size and hash, never only a node-local path.

+- **A candidate is not a reviewed baseline.** The index marks the recommended candidate and the human-confirmed baseline ID separately; the baseline links to exact config/image/code, result set and review record, or reads "pending review". Later comparisons reference that ID; do not swap the denominator for a same-named script's new content or another backend's old result.
+- **Reruns keep history.** A new run gets a new ID and overwrites nothing. Mark an invalidated conclusion with the reason and the replacing run. Continuing an experiment keeps separate attempt/segment and exit records. Reuse evidence across steps by reference, not by copy.

+### Replayable raw data
+
+Keep the real framework batch: prompt/response IDs, attention/response masks, positions, lengths, UID/group/sibling, rollout logprobs, necessary reward and routing records, plus the packing mapping, parallel config and how to restore that step's rollout weights. The raw batch is the replay input; exported per-token logprobs are for comparison only.
+
+Step N's rollout usually comes from the policy before update N, so the post-update checkpoint may not reproduce it. Under partial rollout or async staleness, segments of one sequence may come from different policies (re-prefill after interruption continues under the new policy); record the policy version per segment, or a single-checkpoint replay turns expected policy difference into false inconsistency. +### Compare per-token logprobs
+
+Each side (rollout and training old-logprob, or two replays) exports `{request_id: (logprobs, response_mask)}` as original-dtype tensors with `torch.save`. Do not convert to JSON or rebuild from printed logs. Key points:
+
+- **Align by logical request, not physical row.** Remove padding and restore the pre-packing UID order. Both request sets must match; a missing request raises an error rather than comparing the intersection.
+- **Compare only valid response tokens.** Positions outside the mask are excluded. Every sequence needs at least one valid token; an empty batch is an invalid experiment.
+- **Bitwise comparison looks at bytes, not values.** Value comparison treats `+0.0` and `-0.0` as equal and two NaNs as unequal. Compare integer views: `a.view(torch.int32)` (float32) or `a.view(torch.int16)` (bf16). Do not cast first and then claim bitwise identity in the original dtype.
+- **Same contract on both sides.** Same policy version, same raw/processed basis (for processed, record temperature, truncation, penalty), same input. Compare input token hashes before scores; differences from different inputs are not numerical differences.

+```python
+def compare_logprobs(a, b):
+    assert a.keys() == b.keys(), "request sets differ"
+    n = bad = 0; first = None; max_err = 0.0
+    for uid in sorted(a):
+        (x, mx), (y, my) = a[uid], b[uid]
+        assert torch.equal(mx, my), f"{uid}: masks differ"
+        x, y = x[mx], y[my]
+        ix = x.view(torch.int16 if x.dtype == torch.bfloat16 else torch.int32)
+        iy = y.view(torch.int16 if y.dtype == torch.bfloat16 else torch.int32)
+        diff = (ix != iy).nonzero()
+        if len(diff) and first is None:
+            first = (uid, int(diff[0]))
+        n += len(x); bad += len(diff)
+        max_err = max(max_err, (x.double() - y.double()).abs().max().item())

+
+### Per-layer trace: find the boundary of the first divergence
+
+When logprobs mismatch, record tensors with forward hooks at the same semantic boundaries on both sides (for example each layer's attention output, MoE routing, residual), find the first differing boundary in execution order, then do a bounded dump there. Key points:
+
+- **Key by semantics, not rank.** Each record's key is `(request_id, boundary name, logical slice)`, for example `("step7-p2-s3", "layer2.attn.out", "tokens=0:128")`. Stitch TP/CP/EP shards back by global coordinates and remove padding before recording. Naming and order must match on both sides. A missing probe invalidates the whole experiment; it cannot be skipped.
+- **Hashes first, tensors on demand.** Take SHA256 of the contiguous tensor's original-dtype bytes (`hashlib.sha256(t.contiguous().view(torch.uint8).cpu().numpy()).hexdigest()`), with shape, dtype and semantic execution sequence number. A hash shows where it differs, not by how much; save raw tensors only at the first differing boundary.
+- **Clone before the buffer is reused.** Inference-side workspace and CUDA Graph output buffers are overwritten by the next call; `clone()` in the hook before hashing or saving.
+- **The first difference is not the root cause.** To blame an operator, also prove its input is identical on both sides (record its input hash too).
+
+### Replay controls
+
+With fixed rollout and fixed weights, change one variable (packing order, batch composition, parallel layout, kernel switch), replay old-logprob, and use the comparison above to judge whether that variable affects the result. Key points:
+
+- **One process per variant**, with a synchronous entry point that blocks until the replay finishes. Do not use background submission such as `sbatch`: on timeout or failure the job cannot be reclaimed. Variants that change compilation, libraries or initialization environment need a new process.
+- **Each variant writes to a new directory** without overwriting old results; record the actual command, environment, exit code and elapsed time. Preview the command and budget before executing; on failure, stop at that variant.
+- **Prove the replay is frozen**: record the weight fingerprint, confirm no generation and no optimizer update, and confirm the packing actually in effect, not just the command-line arguments.

+# Environment, image and runtime version provenance
+
+Once the environment is set up (the image pins the native runtime, uv manages training dependencies, source arrives as a traceable snapshot or a minimal overlay), prove that it is what is actually running. Code existing does not mean it is executing.
+
+## Find by symptom
+
+| Symptom / question | Where to go |
+| --- | --- |
+| Not sure which version of source / wheel / .so / image is actually running | [Run manifest](#use-one-run-manifest-to-answer-what-exactly-is-it-right-now) |
+| How many commits "latest" actually differs from the target branch | ["Latest" must come with a target branch](#latest-must-come-with-a-target-branch) |
+| Overlay, or change the source and rebuild | [Boundary between overlay and native wheel](#boundary-between-overlay-and-native-wheel) |
+| Recompiles on every start / not sure where the cache should go | [Compile cache](#compile-cache-where-it-lives-decides-whether-it-can-load) |
+| Not sure which path DeepEP actually runs / how it was built | [Four things about the communication implementation](#communication-implementation-do-not-use-one-name-for-four-things) |
+
+## Key rules
+
+1. Pin the image digest, CPU architecture and Python version first, then resolve training dependencies. Image tag, PyPI version and upstream PR merge status do not replace one minimal inference run in the image.
+2. `--system-site-packages` does not stop uv from installing a same-named package that then imports first; check the install plan, the actual import path and the GPU operators together.
+3. Each of the six manifest layers (source, installed packages, native libraries, JIT kernels, container, run) has evidence nothing else replaces: `latest` is not the digest, `pip show` in another venv is not the actual import path, the Python source HEAD is not the loaded .so.
+4. Audit inside the worker, interpreter and mount namespace that actually run; the login container shell and the Ray worker may differ.
+5. One image tag may point to different digests on different dates/nodes; ARM64 and AMD64 tags may be independent builds.
+6. Modify in the host worktree, execute in the container: same-commit worktree plus per-file hash check, never an overlay stack detached from the formal source.
+7. Write version pins such as "the Megatron fork is only compatible with Megatron-Bridge v0.6.2" into the run manifest.
+8. How the image was produced (container commit exported to sqsh, or Dockerfile rebuild), where it was pushed, and the three-repo SHAs in the tag are part of the run identity.

+## Environment identity: code existing does not mean it is executing
+
+### Use one run manifest to answer "what exactly is it right now"

+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Source | remote, target branch, HEAD, dirty patch hash, submodule gitlink/actual HEAD | `latest`, the repo directory name |
+| Installed package | Actual interpreter, import path, package version, wheel/build revision | `pip show` of another venv |
+| Native library | Path/hash of the `.so` actually loaded, build inputs, target architecture, dynamic dependencies | Python source HEAD, extension file name |
+| JIT kernel | DSL/source hash, compiler version, specialization/config, cache origin | `.so` unchanged |
+| Container | OCI manifest/platform digest or `.sqsh` SHA256, parent image, build record | A mutable Docker tag, image creation time |

+See [debugging mismatch](debugging-mismatch.md#do-not-use-one-name-for-four-things).

+### "Latest" must come with a target branch

+Pin each repo's target branch per the [delivery target](../practices/code-and-delivery.md#8-three-repo-delivery-from-experimental-implementation-to-three-prs-and-one-image). The reference implementation's PR is a design reference, not automatically the PR base. If the user names another fork/branch, record the override. fetch is not checkout; submodule update follows the parent repo's gitlink, not each submodule's own remote.

+```bash

+git -C /explicit/repo remote -v
+git -C /explicit/repo fetch origin

+git -C /explicit/repo log --left-right --oneline A...B

+### Boundary between overlay and native wheel

+3. In a container not yet running the workload, sync each changed in-package Python file individually: before copying, check the original file's hash against `HEAD`; after copying, check the hash of the file under test; save the sync manifest. For new files, check no original exists on either side. Never overwrite the whole package or modify a running container.
+4. Keep the image's version, generated files and unchanged extensions. Recompile native/binding changes and verify the artifacts; for JIT changes check compile inputs and cache; if the ABI/toolchain changes, rebuild the image.
+5. After startup, re-check import/library paths in the actual worker and test. Finally build the unified image from the formal PR's clean commit and rerun acceptance; the user does not redo the development sync. Details: [Implementation and delivery](../practices/code-and-delivery.md#8-three-repo-delivery-from-experimental-implementation-to-three-prs-and-one-image).
+
+Overlays are for development/diagnosis only, not the delivery format.
+
+- An overlay covers specific files in the container with external copies; a wheel is an installed package that may carry compiled machine code.
+- Cover only the necessary files at their exact target paths; do not mount the whole repo over the installed package and shadow its extensions. Verify the target's original hash first, apply once at startup, stop on failure, and save the overlay manifest, final hashes and import paths.
+- A Python-only change can still change the binding/JIT/shape contract; it is not automatically exempt from recompiling or testing.
+- Changes to CUDA/C++, bindings, compile macros, submodule kernels or the CUDA/Torch ABI need checking and recompiling. Before acting on a "missing extension", rule out the wrong venv, shadowing by a whole-repo mount, search paths and dynamic dependencies.
+- If the image already has the correct artifact, verify it and use it. Do not recompile a DeepEP already proven to work, and do not change only the source pin in the recipe expecting the old `.so` to change.
+- Do not fix a FlashAttention extension load failure by `unset`ting a variable. Accept a config fix only once it is shown the variable selected an unneeded/incompatible path and the run passes with the user's target path restored.

+

+
+1. Commit production changes to their PRs; freeze the clean source commit and all native/JIT build inputs and dependencies; record the base image digest, not just the tag. A dirty patch may identify a diagnostic candidate but cannot be an uncommitted dependency of the final run.
+2. Build the final image and check import/dependencies/hashes in a fresh container **with no development source mounts and no inherited JIT cache**, keeping the device, model and data mounts production needs.
+3. Run the agreed correctness, Graph/cache and performance gates in that image; if observability was on, accept again with the formal config and no probes.
+4. Publish exactly the accepted artifact and verify the registry digest/architecture; if conversion or repackaging changes the content, verify the equivalent closure and run a final smoke.
+5. Sync recipe, PR description and image receipt; "image push succeeded" does not cover items that failed. Follow this order when the user asks to push after testing.
+
+The receipt states how the image was produced: Dockerfile rebuild from a clean commit, or changes installed in a container then committed and exported as `.sqsh` (the only option when the coordinator has no docker permission; fine for development, but formal delivery returns to the Dockerfile); which registry it went to (Nemotron: public Docker Hub); a tag carrying the vLLM/Megatron/verl SHAs, not just the date. Record both the `.sqsh` SHA256 and the registry digest under the same tag.
+
+Adding a new project source layer to an old OCI base does not bring in another experiment image's vLLM/FA4 changes. A deleted file missing from the top-level tar may still exist in lower layers; deleting a base file needs a correct whiteout or a check in the final rootfs.
+
+Upgrading FlashInfer/NVSHMEM must not silently upgrade Torch/CUDA. Pin the target interpreter and constraints, compare packages/dynamic dependencies before and after, and confirm the APIs used and build compatibility. A version number is not evidence of an HCA fix or of model correctness.
+
+## Compile cache: where it lives decides whether it can load
+
+Put the Triton/Inductor/vLLM compile caches on node-local disk mounted explicitly into the container; a `noexec` mount (such as `/dev/shm` in some containers) cannot load the compiled `.so`, and a per-container tmpfs recompiles on every start. Isolate caches by image, source commit and GPU architecture, and give each rank on a node its own copy, since an existing cache directory does not mean a cache hit.
