+# Training-side model support
+
+How to build a training implementation cheaply and prove it computes the same math as inference. Where training weights come from (master -> training forward weights) is in [Precision, quantization and QAT](precision-quant.md).
+
+## Three routes
+
+The routes differ in where parallelism and kernels come from. In all three we write the model.
+
+| | MCore (Megatron-Bridge) | FSDP2 (VERL's HF interface path) | mLite |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Positioning | Mature TP/PP/EP/CP, main production RL path | Cheapest: write only the model, no parallelism | Built for consistency: forward calls vLLM kernels, backward reuses the training implementation |
+| Forward source | MCore kernels (TE, grouped GEMM) | Our PyTorch model to vLLM semantics, in the Transformers `PreTrainedModel` interface for the VERL loader and PEFT | vLLM kernels (`visible_forward(visible, native, ...)`) |
+| Achievable consistency | BI=0, via R3 + importance sampling | BI=0 | BI=1, logprob raw bytes identical |
+| What to write for a new model | Bridge weight mapping + modules MCore lacks (Mamba/SSM, special norms) | Whole model: config class, checkpoint loading (with dequantization), per-layer forward, per-operator precision contract; autograd backward, filled in where missing | One `model/<name>/`: config, checkpoint mapping, assembly, protocol; modules from `primitive/modules` |
+| Typical pitfalls | Mapping checks values, not semantics; MCore and vLLM math differ (MoE activation clamp) | bf16 autocast around the VERL forward rewrites module precision; `--system-site-packages` ABI; PyTorch reference (Mamba scan) too slow; loading a third-party implementation from the image by mistake | Private modules inside the model directory, bypassing the shared skeleton |
+
+Choose after the [module inventory](#module-inventory-and-placement-rules), by: is BI=1 needed, how many backwards are missing, what parallelism is needed. Nemotron looked cheap by name; FA4, Mamba scan and W4A16 MoE all lacked a backward.
+
+## Find by symptom
+
+| Symptom / question | Where to go |
+| --- | --- |
+| New model loads and config parses, but unclear whether it can train | [Module inventory](#module-inventory-and-placement-rules) |
+| Want to reuse vLLM forward code, but tangled in paged KV / cudagraph / scheduling | [Call kernels only](#reproducing-the-forward-call-kernels-only-do-not-port-the-scheduler) |
+| Weight mapping shapes are right, output silently degrades | [Mapping checks values and semantics](#43-mapping-checks-cover-values-and-semantics-not-only-shape) |
+| Inference kernel has no backward; should we write one | [Three-case decision](backward-validation.md#three-cases) |
+| Wrote a VJP; how to prove it is right | [Module-level comparison steps](backward-validation.md#comparison-steps) |
+| Unit tests pass but real training fails / step 0 occasionally not bitwise | [Two test-infrastructure false negatives](backward-validation.md#two-test-infrastructure-false-negatives); [BI kernels](bi-kernels.md) |
+| Changes after modifying packing or CP/TP/EP; wrong only on long sequences | [Layout and length](#distributed-layout-length-boundaries-and-training-side-acceptance) |
+| `ppo_kl` non-zero after rollout switches parallel layout (e.g. DP+EP to TP1 per GPU) | [Bitwise identity after changing the parallel layout](#bitwise-identity-after-changing-the-parallel-layout) |
+| `modified by an inplace operation` after no longer recomputing old-logprob | [Entropy when old-logprob is not recomputed](#entropy-when-old-logprob-is-not-recomputed-bypass) |
+| How to hook into VERL / Megatron | [Framework integration](#verl--megatron-integration) |
+| Which kernel an operator uses in BI mode and its cost | [BI kernels](bi-kernels.md) |
+
+## Key rules
+
+1. Semantics follow the vLLM implementation and the checkpoint.
+2. Before starting, list for every module whether its inference kernel has a backward.
+3. Call kernels only; do not port the scheduler. mLite (BI=1): FP32 logprob raw bytes vs vLLM-captured trajectories, target 0 diff. FSDP2 / MCore (BI=0): no 0-diff target; judge each side against an independent reference, then look at precision.
+4. Mapping checks cover values and semantics, not only shape; fused parameters are overwritten whole.
+5. The precision contract lives in the model. Where vLLM computes in FP32 (position-encoding angles, router logits and bias, norm statistics, etc.), the training module sets the dtype and disables the outer autocast. Under VERL's bf16 autocast, casting only the inputs of matmul-type operators (including `F.linear` and `einsum` decomposed into bmm) does not stop the downgrade. Measure output dtype and values under the real autocast.
+6. Backward follows the formula, not the forward kernel. Only rounding differs -> reuse. Quantization rounding -> fix the STE contract, reuse BF16 GEMM. No whole-segment backward -> write glue, GEMM still TE. "No backward kernel at the same precision" is not a reason to rewrite.
+7. Reuse model-agnostic operators: mLite `primitive/modules` and `ops` first, then MCore/TE/mamba_ssm; only then is it new code.
+8. Backward need not be bitwise; report bitwise and tolerance separately; the reference builds its graph independently with ATen autograd; tolerances are fixed before seeing results; synthetic inputs are labeled as not real activations.
+9. Do not recompute activations; use the forward's saved intermediates (DS4: gate_up / LSE).
+10. The model directory holds only config / checkpoint / model / protocol; reusable parts go into `primitive/`; no same-named `primitive/` under the model directory; impl name `lite`.
+11. Long-sequence boundary points (KV page, packing prepend, the 7000/9216 tiers) need dedicated tests.
+12. MTP block, EPLB redundant experts and draft are explicitly skipped in mapping and sync.
+
+## Module inventory and placement rules
+
+List per module: inference kernel, same-math training implementation, quantization rounding, discrete selection, backward. Then pick the route and each module's place in the code tree. This catches missing backwards before they cost weeks.
+
+Training support means an implementation we maintain that backpropagates correctly. Config registration, same-family fallback, the vLLM inference implementation and third-party implementations in the image (newer Transformers modeling, NeMo AutoModel) do not count. Write it per [Reproducing the forward](#reproducing-the-forward-call-kernels-only-do-not-port-the-scheduler) into real source files and verify by loading through the actual loader in a new process. A REPL-only implementation or runtime monkeypatch is not evidence.
+
+### 1. How to build the inventory
+
+One row per module, every column filled; write unknown, not "should exist".
+
+| Column | Question to answer |
+| --- | --- |
+| Inference kernel | The function vLLM actually calls (not the model-file class name), with quantization variants, attention backend, cudagraph branch |
+| Same-math implementation in the training framework | mLite `primitive/modules`, `ops`; MCore / TE; mamba_ssm, causal_conv1d. Rounding-only differences count as same math; a different activation clamp does not. Third-party same-model implementations are not entered |
+| Quantization rounding | FP8/NVFP4 rounding in the forward; weights and activations separately |
+| Discrete selection | top-k expert IDs, sparse indices; IDs fixed and not differentiated, the continuous score needs a derivative |
+| backward | Does the library have one; do its intermediates (LSE, rstd, token permutation) match what our forward saves |
+| Conclusion | Reuse / glue / new code ([decision rules](backward-validation.md#three-cases)) |
+
+Nemotron-H:
+
+| Module | Inference kernel | Same-math training implementation | Rounding | Discrete | backward | Conclusion |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Mamba SSD scan | `mamba_chunk_scan_combined_varlen` | mamba_ssm | None | None | mamba_ssm `_mamba_chunk_scan_combined_bwd` | Reuse |
+| conv1d | `causal_conv1d_fn` | causal_conv1d | None | None | Yes; dW needs fixed-order FP32 | Reuse + small glue |
+| Attention (FP8 KV) | FA4 fixed split + FP8 Q/K/V | FA4 BF16 | Yes | None | FA4 BF16 backward only | Dequantize, recompute BF16 O/LSE, reuse |
+| Mamba in/out_proj (FP8), shared expert (NVFP4) | FlashInfer / NVFP4 GEMM | TE `general_gemm` | Yes | None | TE | Fix STE, reuse |
+| Routed experts (NVFP4 W4A16) | CuTe-DSL / Humming MoE | TE grouped GEMM | Yes | Yes | No whole-segment backward | Glue `routed_vjp` |
+| RMSNorm / gated RMSNorm, routing score | BI kernel / grouped top-k | PyTorch formula | None | None for the score | autograd | Reuse |
+| MTP block, draft | Not part of training | - | - | - | - | See §4 |
+
+### 3. Placement rules
+
+#### 3.1 mLite (Megatron `experimental/lite/megatron/lite`)
+
+Read `experimental/lite/docs/porting.md` and `architecture.md` first. Three layers: `runtime` (lifecycle, training-step orchestration), `model` (registration + model-specific build/load/export protocol), `primitive` (reusable: parallel state, TP layers, checkpoint conversion, MoE utilities, optimizer wrappers). The runtime knows no model details: it gets the protocol from the registry, builds a typed config, and lets the protocol build the model.
+
+| Rule | Content |
+| --- | --- |
+| The model directory holds only four things | `model/<name>/`: config, checkpoint mapping (WeightSpec), assembly, protocol. Impl name `lite` (`<name>/lite/`) |
+| Modules go into primitive | norm / linear / router / experts / dispatcher / attention -> `primitive/modules`; generic VJP bridge -> `primitive/ops`; quantization encoding -> `primitive/quantization`; PP splitting, thd, CP -> `primitive/parallel`; HF read/write via `primitive/ckpt/hf_weights` (`SafeTensorReader`, `load_hf_weights`, `export_hf_weights`) |
+| Model-specific math still goes into primitive and is registered | e.g. Mamba2 bridge, FP8-KV attention -> `primitive/modules/<x>.py`; no same-named `primitive/` under the model directory |
+| No file for reused backward | Reusing TE / mamba_ssm backward means no `backward.py`; glue goes in the module file |
+| Dependencies are one-directional | `model/` imports `primitive/`, never the reverse; top-level checkpoint/quantization does not import the impl subtree |
+| Layering guards must be registered | Add the model to `tests/unit/runtime/test_layering_contracts.py` or the guard does not apply |
+| No hybrid architecture packages | porting.md: "Keep these out of the first PR: Hybrid model implementation packages"; hybrid (Mamba + attention + MoE) modules are split into primitive |
+| State third-party kernel dependencies | Document hard dependencies on vllm, flashinfer private APIs, mamba_ssm, causal_conv1d, and the `init_batch_invariance()` call in build_model |
+
+DS4 is the positive example: `model.py` (650 lines) assembles te.RMSNorm, CSA, HCA/mHC, thd and the fp8 recipe with three model-specific deviations; `moe.py` (102 lines) = SigmoidTopKRouter + Experts + TokenDispatcher + SwiGLUMLP, hash-route the only model-specific code; `checkpoint.py` is one WeightSpec using shared load/export.
+
+#### 3.2 MCore / Megatron-Bridge
+
+- Bridge `models/<name>/`: provider + HF<->MCore mapping; modules MCore lacks (Mamba/SSM variants, special norms, HC) go into `megatron/core`, not Bridge.
+- Mapping checks values, not only shape ([§4.3](#43-mapping-checks-cover-values-and-semantics-not-only-shape)).
+- MCore and vLLM may use different formulas (MoE activation clamp); BI=0 cannot align those either, so list them first.
+- The Megatron fork works only with Megatron-Bridge v0.6.2, pinned in the image.
+
+#### 3.3 FSDP2 (VERL's HF interface path)
+
+- Write a PyTorch model to vLLM semantics in the Transformers `PreTrainedModel` / config interface so the VERL loader, PEFT and HF save/load use it directly. "HF" is only the interface and weight format.
+- Delivery: the model goes into the verl trunk, registered to the Auto classes (`AutoConfig` / `AutoModelForCausalLM`, etc.), and ships with the recipe as one verl PR ([Code and delivery §8](../practices/code-and-delivery.md#verl-a-thin-recipe-not-a-second-training-framework)). The verl FSDP extension guide's advice against copying modeling into `verl/models` targets models already in transformers. Register at the current checkout's FSDP load chain (`get_hf_auto_model_class` -> `from_pretrained`).
+- Develop and deliver from the same verl source and registration entry. Do not modify the checkpoint's `config.json` / `auto_map` (the low-precision checkpoint is the single source of truth) or enable `trust_remote_code`. The load log must show our registered class was used.
+- VERL's automodel engine (`automodel_actor`) uses NeMo AutoModel and is not this route; routes are distinguished by forward source, not by FSDP2 sharding.
+- Under bf16 autocast, FP32 computations (position-encoding angles, router logits and bias, norm statistics, following vLLM) disable autocast inside the module and set the dtype.

+## Reproducing the forward: call kernels only, do not port the scheduler
+
+The first deliverable after the inventory is a training forward with vLLM's math. Logprob measurement basis and R3 route replay: [workflow](../workflow/README.md), [rollout engine](rollout-engine.md).
+
+### 1. First separate the responsibilities of the model implementation and the training framework
+
+A training framework (FSDP2, MCore, mLite runtime) shards a trainable model; it does not make an inference-only kernel differentiable or write the model. Write a minimal PyTorch model for the current loader interface covering the config, checkpoint loading, forward, gradients and save interface actually used; full Transformers integration, generation and all parallelism are not needed first. The semantic basis is vLLM and the checkpoint, not a third-party implementation in the image.
+
+| Capability | What the training route still has to do | What in inference / Megatron is not copied |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Model math | Real semantics of attention/SSM, norm, position encoding, routing, residuals, special embeddings | vLLM paged KV, decode scheduling, cudagraph management; MCore provider/ModuleSpec wiring |
+| Backpropagation | Input gradients of every training-path operator; trained-parameter gradients; recompute correctness ([Backward validation](backward-validation.md)) | TP/SP/CP-specific collectives and gradient reduction |
+| Weights | Names, axes, fused order, expert IDs, sharing, derived state | HF<->Megatron shard layout, PP export protocol |
+| LoRA | Target coverage, A/B direction and scaling, non-zero adapter taking effect | Parallel linear wrapper, TP adapter aggregation |
+| Memory | Initialization peak, large frozen table residency, save/export peak | Megatron memory saver, PP scheduling |
+
+dtype, dequantization, QAT and update format: [precision guide](precision-quant.md). Here each module states its input/output precision and differentiable boundary.
+
+### 2. How to wire kernel-only calls
+
+Each layer's forward runs once: call the vLLM kernel for the visible output, bitwise identical to inference, and save what the backward needs; see [backward wiring](backward-validation.md#how-to-wire-it-forward-once-backward-uses-what-the-forward-saved). Borrow only the kernel, no vLLM runtime object:
+
+- No KV paging, decode scheduling or CUDA Graph management. Training runs a full-sequence teacher-forced forward; packing passes boundaries via thd/cu_seqlens.
+- Reuse order: model-agnostic differentiable operators -> concise PyTorch reference to vLLM semantics -> ready-made operators with backward -> custom autograd/kernel only if necessary. This order only says where to look first; the training-step cost of each choice is checked at C6 against the C1 budget, not deferred to C10.
+- Handle discrete top-k / index selection apart from the selected differentiable tensors. What is trained, frozen or given an auxiliary loss follows the model definition; do not detach to get it running or add router/indexer objectives.
+- vLLM layer modules used directly (FusedMoE, ModelOpt linear) need `get_tp/ep_group`, so the training process creates vLLM process groups (Nemotron does; DS4's own modules do not).
+- Take the same branch as inference: reproduce the quantization config, attention backend and BI-switch kernel selection, or the comparison is against a different path. Tests use the production `CompilationConfig(custom_ops=...)` ([the two false negatives](backward-validation.md#two-test-infrastructure-false-negatives)).
+
+"The same kernel" still has pitfalls (Nemotron 7-layer localization):
+
+1. Direct and compiled paths of the same gated RMS kernel differ; calling it through an opaque custom-op boundary removed the difference.
+2. A differing reduction block was wrongly blamed alone; the same captured kernel showed both blocks match.
+3. The last 4.768e-7 logprob difference came from the HF forward calling `.float()` after lm_head; keeping the real BF16 head output and sharing the scoring fixed it. This is not truncating an FP32 projection to BF16 to manufacture equality.
+
+### 3. Read the inference implementation along the full support chain
+
+Order: model file (layer types and order, residual and norm positions, position encoding, attention visibility, router/indexer, special embeddings) -> each layer's actual kernel and quantization variant -> attention backend and KV dtype -> weight loader (name mapping, fused order, derived scale) -> BI-switch branches. Confirm the parameter/buffer list from the same checkpoint/config.
+
+Sizes sharing one implementation need no separate port. For ordinary dense models, look for a reusable generic skeleton first; we still write the model. Multimodal is validated per task; diffusion is out of scope.
+
+### 4. The minimal implementation that really has to be filled in
+
+#### 4.1 Reproduce the math
+
+Confirm from the checkpoint/config and inference code: layer types and order, parameters/buffers, residual and norm positions, position encoding, attention visibility, router/indexer, special embeddings. Model-specific math (`sqrt(softplus)` scoring, SwiGLU with clamp, mHC Sinkhorn, ReLU² experts) is in no library; write it from the inference source, not the paper.
+
+#### 4.2 A frozen base still has to propagate input gradients
+
+```python
+W.requires_grad_(False)
+y = linear(x, W) + scale * B(A(x))  # no gradient for W, but still propagate to x
+loss(y).backward()
+```
+
+Wrapping a frozen block in `no_grad()` cuts LoRA gradients of earlier layers; only a frozen table lookup needing no input/parameter derivative is exempt. With initial B=0 a zero gradient for A can be normal; test with a non-zero adapter or a real step. A finite loss does not prove backward.
+
+<a id="33-shape"></a>
+
+#### 4.3 Mapping checks cover values and semantics, not only shape
+
+Per weight class: source name -> training name -> serving name, axis transforms, sharing. Focus on fused QKV, gate/up order, expert numbering, extra norm/bias, tie weights, non-persistent buffers, derived state (FP8 KV scale, NVFP4 alpha). Every missing/extra item needs a reason; quantization-derived items follow the precision guide and need not be byte-identical to the low-precision source. FSDP needs no HF<->Megatron bridge but may need checkpoint->training and export mappings.
+
+#### 4.4 Packing boundaries for Mamba / stateful modules
+
+Every stateful operator (conv1d, SSM scan, recurrence, PLE shift) must consume sequence boundaries; a correct attention mask proves nothing about them. Incidents:
+
+- verl via Megatron-Bridge did not pass boundaries to Mamba; sequence states mixed and logprob was silently wrong, visible only as a larger mismatch.
+- Qwen3.8 Flash-Next's PLE shift made the second sample reference the first sample's last token.
+
+Check: unequal-length A/B run separately and merged; sentinel-initialized outputs to catch missed writes. In mLite, derive boundary metadata from `PackedSeqParams`/`ThdPackMeta`, not a separate `SSMMeta`. See also [Long-sequence boundary points](#long-sequence-boundary-points).
+
+#### 4.5 Recompute and small-model trimming
+
+With activation checkpointing on, verify recompute reads the same state and gives reasonable gradients. Trim to the smallest layer set covering every non-equivalent path and its dependencies, usually 4-6 layers; keep mixed attention, cross-layer sharing and layer-specific table lookups. Record kept layer indices and the config transform; a slice proves only covered paths, not full-model mismatch or score gain.
+
+### 5. How to prove it computes the same math
+
+Feed the training forward vLLM-captured trajectories (fixed tokens, weight version, position, mask, routing); never compare probability summaries or argmax. mLite (BI=1): FP32 logprob raw bytes, target 0 diff. FSDP2 / MCore (BI=0): judge each side against an independent reference, then check the remaining difference comes only from precision rules.
+
+- Same policy weights. Differing dtypes are a contract mismatch; do not convert to fake bitwise.
+- Reference artifact (Nemotron): frozen trainer image, full actor, 2048 tokens, FP32 0 diff; five real updates, 883,998 tokens of identical FP32 logprob.
+- Old-logprob recomputation and the grad-enabled forward are two paths; evidence for each ([dual-path contract](../workflow/validation.md#old-logprob-and-training-forward-dual-path-contract)).
+- Find the first divergence per [debugging](debugging-mismatch.md): per-module dump, single-request prefill, then the operator.
+
+### 6. Small tasks handed to agents and stop conditions
+
+Each outputs a short conclusion, source version, reproducible command and artifact.
+
+| Task | Minimal acceptance | If it fails |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Implementation inventory | Training model class, operator backward, checkpoint loader; gaps listed | Write the minimal model; stop cold-starting the large model |
+| Module comparison | Same weights/inputs; gradients vs a differentiable reference | Locate the earliest difference |
+| Few-layer training | Non-zero loss, finite gradients, intended adapter changes | Separate broken path, operator bug, gradient-less target |
+| Save and restore | Fresh-process restore: consistent forward and next step | Check state, adapter, optimizer, residency |
+
+Distribute only after the first two pass; scale up after the few-layer two-step loop passes.
+
+### 7. How to judge development cost
+
+Training implementation exists: wire loading, LoRA, sharding. Inference only with differentiable references: fill in assembly, mapping, interfaces. Key operator lacks backward or clear semantics: separate blocker; reference and gradient validation first; no uniform person-day figure.
+
+## Distributed layout, length boundaries and training-side acceptance
+
+Record trainer and rollout topologies separately. TP/CP/EP, padding, packing and collectives change data mapping and reduction paths; long sequences hit untested boundaries; forward 0 diff does not vouch for gradients or the optimizer.
+
+### Compute resources first, then request them
+
+Write trainer and rollout process groups separately. At four GPUs per node, an inference DP8/EP8 group spans two nodes; two DP4/EP4 replicas are not one EP8 group and skip cross-node EP communication. The runtime decides grouping.
+
+If dense DP excludes CP: `W = TP × PP × CP × DP`. Expert side: verify `W = ETP × EP × PP × EDP` and the CP mapping separately. **Do not multiply EP into the dense world again.** W=8, TP1/PP2/CP2 gives DP=2; a log calling DP×CP "DP" shows 4. Clarify naming and members; do not change GPU count to match a config string.
+
+GPU memory follows the layout. With PP1 each rank holds all layers' activations, linear in sequence length. Per-route EP backward state stored for other ranks' slots grows by the average ranks per token; store only own routes. Rollout `gpu_memory_utilization` is set from what training still holds during rollout, per training mode, in the recipe ([Memory budget 02 §5](checkpoint-resume.md#5-gpu-memory-set-gpu_memory_utilization-per-mode-when-training-and-rollout-are-colocated)).
+
+### Packing and CP
+
+For the target UID reconstruct global request `[seq_start, seq_end)`, rank range `[rank_start, rank_end)`, local rows, cu_seqlens, positions, all compression/reordering mappings.
+
+The intersection `[max(seq_start, rank_start), min(seq_end, rank_end))` contributes rows only when start < end. The overlap window must not give a disjoint request this rank's output. Host cumulative boundaries equal the rows the device compactor produces.
+
+Cover: before/after/at the boundary, empty intersection, cross-rank, compression-ratio and tile remainders. Window constant 8: check 1…7, not only multiples. Start from a hand-computable counterexample, then enumerate nearby legal configs.
+
+Passing `cu_seqlens` does not mean a fallback consumes it ([§4.4](#44-packing-boundaries-for-mamba--stateful-modules)).
+
+### EP and collectives
+
+Record expert mapping, tokens per rank, padding capacity, route order, shared/routed combine, quantization scales. Empty ranks may still join collectives; partially written reused buffers leave stale data. Use different sentinels per side; zero-filling both gives a false green.
+
+Pinning NCCL algorithm/channels may remove reduction differences on one stack and cut throughput significantly; verify it per topology, not as a universal env list, before relaxing config or building a deterministic collective.
+
+MCore dev's grad-ready assertion takes first-batch hook counts as golden and errors on a different count. Short-sequence micro-batches can make counts data-dependent (Nemotron r10 at step 2; r12 did not reproduce). With dp×cp=1 and expert_dp=1, `overlap_grad_reduce` off avoids it without changing values; root cause unknown. With EP4 + dist_opt and dp>1, multi-micro-batch reduction fires early (reported).
+
+### Bitwise identity after changing the parallel layout
+
+**Principle.** Floating-point addition is not associative. Layout sets reduction grouping, order and rounding: TP splits a matmul into per-rank partial sums; EP computes a token's top-k experts on different ranks and merges. Last-bit differences become different tokens after dozens of layers and sampling, so bitwise identity holds only for the verified layout; any TP/EP/DP change must be proven again.
+
+**Rules.**
+
+1. The reduction tree is part of the numerical contract: per level, accumulation dtype, order and rounding points. All legal rollout layouts and training walk the same tree.
+2. A degenerate layout (TP=1, EP=1) must simulate the tree: per-rank partial sums, same rounding, same merge order.
+3. After a layout change, compare per-token logprob raw bytes on fixed inputs before training. Non-zero `ppo_kl`/probs_diff is fixed, not avoided by reverting the layout.
+4. Locate: dump per layer, find the first differing layer, confirm its inputs (MoE: router logits too) are bitwise equal; the bug is that layer's reduction ([Fault localization](debugging-mismatch.md#bisect-and-first-divergence)).
+5. Measure the cost of simulating the order and report it apart from the layout gain.
+
+**Examples.**
+
+| Model | Layout change | Where the difference is | Fix and result |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Nemotron-H (W4A16 MoE, BI=1) | rollout from DP4EP4 per node to TP1 per GPU | EP4: per-rank FP32 sums rounded to BF16, merged in FP32 as `((s0+s1)+(s2+s3))+(s4+s5)`. EP1: six outputs summed sequentially in FP32, no intermediate rounding. Max logprob diff 0.4; greedy tokens diverge at positions 10–129 | Without EP, BI mode computes all experts in one launch and reduces in EP4 order (vLLM `661cde6833`, not in the image). Both layouts match training bitwise; `ppo_kl` 0 over 58 steps; multi-turn replay 404 s vs 485 s, reduction cost about 2.5% |
+| DeepSeek V4.1 | training TP=1, inference TP>1 | order of per-TP-rank partial sums | both sides use one fixed reduction tree, TP=1 included (`VLLM_TP_INVARIANT_LEAVES`) |
+
+### Asynchronous communication and lifetime
+
+Check streams, events, buffer owners and reuse timing. Passing with a global synchronize only proves a timing issue and is not the fix; find the missing dependency and accept on the same path.
+
+### Long-sequence boundary points
+
+Test at real lengths:
+
+| Boundary | Fact | How to test |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| KV page | training attention replicates vLLM's KV page size; page boundaries are numerical boundaries | sparse dY across the page boundary |
+| Fixed split attention | fixed split count and keys per split; the resulting `MAX_SEQ_LEN` is an invariance bound, not a performance knob | above: error, not silent truncation; below: two real lengths × random/zero/sparse dY |
+| Packing prepend | one prepended short sequence shifts every target row offset | two prepend controls vs none, bitwise |
+| Micro-batch fits the longest sequence | verl needs each micro-batch to fit the longest sequence (`ppo_max_token_len_per_gpu`, Nemotron 16384 vs DS4 4096; Nemotron training has no CP) | OOM probe at formal length; do not extrapolate from 8K |
+| Embedding backward | CUDA `embedding_dense_backward` accumulates at reduced precision with ≤3072 indices, e.g. a short sequence alone in a micro-batch | length-tiered tolerance |
+| CP compressed boundary | see [Packing and CP](#packing-and-cp) | before/after/at the boundary |

+### The D term in attention backward
+
+With P rounded to FP8, visible O = fp8(P)·V ≠ softmax(QKᵀ)·V. If `D = rowsum(dO⊙O)` uses visible O while dS uses recomputed P, `rowsum(dS_i) ≠ 0` and dQ gains a same-sign per-row bias (Nemotron: about 3% of dQ/dK, v2 FAIL at steps 150/250; fixed 0.006–0.009, PASS). Mainstream FP8 attention (TE fp8_dpa, SageBwd) uses visible O, so a human decides after being informed.
+
+Four checks:
+
+1. **FA4 interface signature**: `_flash_attn_bwd` derives D in preprocess from the `out` passed; D cannot be passed. The public interface errors under `requires_grad`; the actor calls `_flash_attn_fwd/_bwd`. Fix: recompute BF16 O and LSE from dequantized Q/K/V, pass to bwd (layer backward +4–15%, end to end <0.05%).
+2. **varlen LSE layout**: ln vs log2, per head vs per token, softmax scale folded or not. On mismatch, recompute with the training kernel.
+3. **GQA 32/2**: dK/dV summed within each Q head group; A/A needs fixed summation order.
+4. **When the saved Q/K/V are released under recompute=full**: if only dequantized Q/K/V are saved, recompute must read the same state; early release changes the values.
+
+### Microbatch split and gradient difference
+
+Different microbatch splits give about 2e-3 relative gradient difference (loss normalization, accumulation order, reduced-precision embedding backward at ≤3072 indices). Not a bug, but:
+
+- Criterion denominator = `max(B16 reference floor, noise floor of the implementation under test)`, never the FP32 ideal.
+- Both arms use the same split; if it changes, rerun A/A.
+- grad_norm is not comparable across different microbatch counts.
+
+### Control matrix
+
+With policy/tokens fixed, test original layout, reversed order, target first/last, changed micro-batch, CP-boundary sample, each reconstructed by UID/global token coordinates. Real TP/EP changes may legally change the reduction; the experiment contract decides whether cross-topology bitwise equality is required.
+
+Safe packing is not a fix for a metadata bug; it may only lower trigger probability. After the fix, the original layout and nearby boundaries must pass.
+

+### Training-side correctness acceptance: gradient comparison criterion v2 and optauth
+
+Two independent checks beyond forward 0 diff.
+
+#### Gradient comparison criterion v2
+
+- Freeze the criterion (tolerance, denominator, thresholds) before the run, record its sha, never change it after.
+- Planted-error check first: gradients ×1.25 and ×1.05 must both FAIL.
+- Accept on several snapshots (steps 0/50/150/250); the D-term problem appeared only at step 150.
+- On failure, inject reference gradients block by block to find the first module over the limit.
+- Extended to FSDP2: EP4 + FSDP2 all four snapshots PASS, worst-class median 1.08–1.39, all floors from B16.
+- Tool bug: with `overlap_grad_reduce=False` gradients were reduced again before the EP4 dump (fixed). The export path needs A/A too: ‖g‖ bitwise equal, local shards bitwise equal to the dump, replica diff 0/0.
+- Cross-process bitwise backward is not required. An occasional non-bitwise first step comes from the thread-local Inductor deterministic config (the autograd thread's first compile picks 512/1024 blocking by timing); fix in [BI kernels: determinism](bi-kernels.md#determinism-takes-effect-only-on-the-main-thread).
+
+#### Optimizer acceptance (optauth)
+
+Verify the optimizer consumes clipped `main_grad`, the update lands on master, and deployed bytes = requantize(master). Freeze the criterion first. Split failures into criterion modeling gaps (e.g. a check inapplicable without replicated parameters; the equal-magnitude first Adam step invalidating γ-type criteria while the per-coordinate bound holds), documented and accepted, and implementation errors, fixed. Cover all parameter group types: a first-step probe without an FP32 wd_mult=0 parameter misses weight decay applied to that group.
+
+#### Facts outside the two criteria
+
+- Frozen base with LoRA: base modules still propagate input gradients ([§4.2](#42-a-frozen-base-still-has-to-propagate-input-gradients)).
+- The two-step RL loop (θ0→θ1→θ2) accepts the forward; three-arm SFT accepts training effect; report all three separately ([validation](../workflow/validation.md)).

+## VERL / Megatron integration
+
+Upstream config keys may differ from what was used here. Find the actual call paths of rollout dump, old-logprob and skip/repeat in the current checkout and record the commit; local-patch options are not upstream API. Process content (recipe and PR contract, review material, two-step acceptance, E2E targets) is in [validation.md](../workflow/validation.md#recipe-review-materials-and-two-step-acceptance-agreement); PR ownership in [Code and delivery §8](../practices/code-and-delivery.md#8-three-repo-delivery-from-experimental-implementation-to-three-prs-and-one-image).
+
+### Where the integration layer is
+
+Megatron's `experimental/lite/examples/verl/verl_mlite/` provides the verl engine adapter (`model_engine=mlite`, `pkg://verl_mlite.config`), installable into the unified image without reimplementing the engine in verl. Check engine registration, model factory, batch conversion, loss normalization and optimizer path; list reusable interfaces and gaps. Consistency uses mLite; the training baseline uses the existing recipe's default MCore path; do not mix them.
+
+### Capture location
+
+Save the DataProto (or equivalent) after rollout returns and before the first old-logprob; append trainer scores after. Record policy version, UID, input/response IDs, mask, position IDs, reward, route replay data if needed, and the UID -> packed-row mapping if reordered. Keep a pre-update checkpoint bound to the batch by content fingerprint; after strict load compare structure and keys and reject missing/unexpected keys.
+
+### Historical DS4 entry point
+
+DS4 used patched VERL options (`skip.rollout.*`, `DS4_SKIP_UPDATE=1`); confirm in code and logs that any such switch takes effect.
+
+### Minimal adapter contract
+
+The synchronous entry point takes batch, checkpoint, variant and output directory, then:
+
+1. Records actual policy, effective config, libraries and parallel layout.
+2. Reads the same rollout, repacks per variant, keeps logical UIDs.
+3. Runs the real old-logprob forward and exports per-token logprobs in UID order ([Saving and comparing](debugging-mismatch.md#compare-per-token-logprobs)).
+4. Records no generation and no update, and mutable-buffer initialization.
+5. Waits for workers/collectives, closes its resources, returns an exit code.
+
+It keeps native `no_grad`/`forward_only` semantics and replaces neither the [grad-enabled forward comparison](../workflow/validation.md#old-logprob-and-training-forward-dual-path-contract) nor update acceptance. A/B/C may share one long-lived worker once weight and state isolation is verified. The runner does not take over Ray/Slurm; the launcher blocks on remote jobs and reclaims on timeout. +# Code, experiment snapshots and delivery
+
+Code ownership across three repos for cross-stack train-inference consistency delivery and "three PRs, one image" (§8), and PRs and cleanup (§9). Lifecycle, cold-start and model acceptance details are not repeated.
+
+## 8. Three-repo delivery: from experimental implementation to three PRs and one image
+
+Cross-stack RL delivery for a model is one vLLM PR, one Megatron PR, one verl PR, and one unified image built from the versions the three pin. Default targets are `vllm-project/vllm:main`, `NVIDIA/Megatron-LM:dev` and `verl-project/verl:main`; a fork may host the head but does not replace the main repo's target branch. This section covers change ownership and delivery checks; it does not replace the [ten-step flow](../workflow/README.md), the [numerical gates](../workflow/validation.md) or human recipe review.
+
+### Before changing code: give a change map first
+
+Fix the inference-side change locations in step 3 and the training side and integration interfaces in step 5; step 1 need not design every interface. Submit a short table of "feature → existing module/interface → proposed change location → reason for reuse or addition", covering at least model construction, forward/backward, quantization, parameter registration, checkpoint and the build entry.
+
+Read the implementation and callers in the selected checkout before choosing file names; the paths below are design references, not a requirement to copy DeepSeek's directories. Do not write a standalone engine first and discover at the end that the existing integration layer or the real trainer cannot use it.
+
+### vLLM: implement in the formal execution path, do not deliver a patch loader
+
+- Development environment and code sync follow [same-commit worktree, per-file sync and build verification](../guides/environment-provenance.md#boundary-between-overlay-and-native-wheel); development sync is not how the final image is installed and does not change the PR's target branch.
+- Model-specific selection goes in the model construction/execution entry; changes to shared kernels, backends and metadata go in the existing owning module, stating which models and callers are affected.
+- BI=0 keeps the reviewed native path; BI=1 explicitly selects the aligned implementation. Check the actual backend and fail early when a required BI capability is missing; never silently fall back while still claiming consistency.
+- Kernel numerics, binding and build registration ship together; CUDA/C++ changes enter the normal build, and JIT changes such as CuTe DSL record the compiler and specialization. Do not submit only the Python call while depending on an uncommitted `.so`, source file or build script inside the experiment container.
+- Verify the default path is unchanged and cover the modified shared interfaces; when only a certain model/runner/topology is supported, restrict it explicitly rather than implying other models support BI.
+
+Reference points in [vLLM #54955](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54955): the formal kernel integration in `csrc/batch_invariant/`, the DeepGEMM BI capability check, and the stable tie-break/prefill-decode semantics of sparse selection. These address operator numerics, backend authenticity and execution shape change respectively; they are more than a BI switch.
+
+### Megatron mLite: separate the model, the aligned operators and the runtime
+
+The train-inference consistency implementation uses mLite; the training baseline uses the default MCore path of the existing verl recipe, without the aligned implementation. Record the training baseline and the vLLM BI=0 inference performance baseline separately; they are not the same comparison. When target-model support has gaps, state them and get them reviewed; do not change the training scheme on your own.
+
+| Change | Preferred owner | Should not go in |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Model layer structure, parameters and checkpoint mapping | model/protocol/checkpoint modules of `experimental/lite/model/<model>/` | a temporary model implementation inside a verl recipe |
+| forward aligned with vLLM, autograd/STE, model-specific quantization | that model's aligned implementation and primitive modules | miscellaneous top-level mLite scripts, global monkeypatch |
+| Reusable training/communication/optimizer capabilities | existing shared primitive/runtime, changed only for a real interface gap | one model's recipe constants and diagnostic branches |
+| verl engine adaptation, batch/loss bridging | existing `experimental/lite/examples/verl/verl_mlite/` interface | another equivalent engine inside verl |
+
+- Select native vs aligned implementations through the existing protocol/factory/explicit config; do not scatter environment checks across low-level forwards or replace instance methods/global functions at runtime. Small-scope branches can stay; do not copy the whole model for a tidy directory; reuse shared math and backward, and implement independently only primitives whose numerical semantics really differ.
+- Do not assemble production operators with `inspect.getsource`, AST rewriting, or string replacement plus `exec`, and do not register models via `sitecustomize` or temporary `PYTHONPATH` hijacking. Import stable interfaces from the real dependency, and commit necessary changes to the owning module.
+- Keep the parameter registration, state_dict/checkpoint, distributed reduction and recomputation contracts; do not replace the training master parameters with an inference cache the optimizer does not manage just to align forward. Backward is accepted separately per the [gradient contract](../guides/backward-validation.md#write-down-the-gradient-contract-first); it need not be bitwise identical with inference, and a kernel without autograd does not automatically need STE.

+[Megatron #7050](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7050) separates DeepSeek-V4's `lite/` from `vllm/primitive/` and reuses the existing `verl_mlite`, illustrating these boundaries. `verl_mlite` exists in official Megatron dev, not only in a fork; still check the version this task pins and its actual capabilities.
+
+### verl: a thin recipe, not a second training framework
+
+What is delivered depends on the route:
+
+- **mLite route**: for non-observability changes, deliver ideally only one recipe script and one image build script, reusing the real trainer of the current version and the installed `verl_mlite`.
+- **FSDP2 Day-0 route**: verl lacks the model, so the deliverable is the self-written model implementation in verl mainline, its Auto class registration and the recipe, in one verl PR; the model implementation itself is the deliverable and needs no separate "generic interface gap" pre-review. +On both routes, when there is a real generic interface gap, first give call-chain evidence, the interface to change and the scope of impact, **get human review before implementing**, and make the minimal fix in the owning repo; do not hide code in scripts or move it to the wrong repo to make up the file count.

+The two-file form of [verl #7688](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7688) and the `verl.trainer.main_ppo`/`model_engine=mlite` chain are the reference; its development mounts and overlay are not how the final image is delivered. +
+### Step 10: from clean PRs to verifiable delivery
+
+1. **Three complete diffs.** For each repo, record the target owner/branch/base SHA agreed with the user and the PR head; check the merge-base, commit history and actual diff. Required model support must be in the PR or already merged into the target branch; another unmerged feature branch cannot be the base. Do not carry over a preview PR's history drift or unrelated deletions; pin cross-repo dependencies by commit. After changing the base or rebasing, re-review the diff; evidence from the old head does not transfer.
+2. **One rebuildable image.** Build from three clean checkouts, pinning the base image digest, dependencies and necessary native/JIT build inputs, and install all runtime packages normally, including external adapter packages. Training and inference workers use the same immutable platform digest and the same Python/Torch and runtime dependencies; different nodes/processes are fine, but not two independent environments inside the image to dodge compatibility. It must run without host source mounts, startup-time patches or uncommitted overlays.
+3. **Re-accept from a new container.** Check the actual worker's interpreter, imports, libraries and versions; verify the proxy, full-model zero-update and the real RL loop of the reviewed recipe per the existing gates; then record performance/quality. A successful build, offline disk replay and historical 0 diff do not replace verifying the final artifact; on a difference, shrink back to a fixed failing replay first instead of relaunching full training to locate it.
+4. **One mapping.** Use the [report template](../workflow/report-template.md) to list the three PRs, image digest, recipe review version and acceptance receipts, marking each item pass/fail/inconclusive/not run. Update it after code cleanup, build or dependency changes; an unverified clean implementation does not inherit the overlay prototype's pass.
+
+When slimming the implementation PR, non-essential diagnostic tools, docs and experiment artifacts stay in the private repo/model workspace; necessary regression tests can go with the PR. Do not delete tests that exist on the target branch, and a slim PR still runs tests. Follow each target repo's contribution requirements, record the regressions and model evaluations actually run, and submit for human review; if the gates do not pass, keep the not-accepted status.
+
+### Reference versions, not proof of passing
+
+All three PRs were open when reviewed, and the first two were marked DO NOT MERGE:
+
+| Reference | Reviewed head SHA |
+| --- | --- |
+| vLLM #54955 | `4b5c627c23e6690b8987100d1cbf78e34ac14bf9` |
+| Megatron #7050 | `327a238239448de6771beea185dc6902a8de3eaa` |

+
+## 9. PRs and cleanup
+
+- Three-repo delivery follows the target branches in §8.
+- The PR description records: minimal purpose, base and patch stack, related existing PRs/why it is not a duplicate, upstream/private PRs, RL-only content, test commands and results, model impact, rollback method, AI assistance and human review requirements.
+- Split a large PR into small independently reviewable PRs and prove equivalence before and after the split with the tree hash; open PRs only from your own fork.
+- Resolve conflicts on the head branch of the PR the user specified; do not open a similarly named new PR to pass the original off as fixed.

+
+## Minimal changes, contribution and delivery
+
+Change the config along the entry script the user specified, so multiple temporary launchers do not drift apart. End with one launch entry that actually runs, with defaults, necessary overrides and image/code pins traceable; exports that exist only in chat are not delivery.

+# Evidence and experiment rules
+
+Rules for what counts as evidence, how experiments are designed and recorded, and when old evidence stops holding. Mechanisms live in the guides.
+
+## 1. Evidence labels
+
+PASS / FAIL / INVALID (did not enter the target path) / VACUOUS (condition had zero hits) / SUPERSEDED / HISTORICAL. These label evidence, not lifecycle states. The tables in [validation.md](../workflow/validation.md) and the [report template](../workflow/report-template.md) have only `pass / fail / inconclusive / not run`. PASS→`pass`, FAIL→`fail`; INVALID and VACUOUS become `inconclusive` with the reason in the notes; SUPERSEDED and HISTORICAL stay out of the current table and live only in the [candidate evidence ledger](#6-candidate-evidence-ledger) and historical reports. One SUPERSEDED piece of evidence makes the gate it covered stale. A successful run, train-inference consistency and a held-out score gain are different conclusions and cannot substitute for each other.
+
+## 2. Evidence that must not be confused
+
+- Enabling `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` is not cross-framework bitwise alignment; the same text is not the same logprob.
+- Zero difference in probability space, zero KL or identical printed numbers do not replace comparing valid logprobs in the original dtype.
+- Replaying fixed inputs is a localization tool; statistics from old trajectories are not an unbiased KL under the current policy.
+- The same function name, generated code or environment variables do not prove the same actual kernel, launch config and shared libraries.
+- Output replacement, forced routing, disabling Graph and bypassing bad packing are valid causal experiments if you state what they change.
+- Similar quality scores are not identical per-problem results; same-problem quality, bitwise logprob and 8K/1K performance are accounted separately. When the acceptance script fails, check the producer receipt first; do not resample or declare a pass automatically.
+- Verify quantization rules on the deployed bytes, not dequantized weights ([precision pitfall P2](../guides/precision-quant.md#p2-verifying-a-rule-with-dequantized-weights-gives-a-false-positive)). QAT/low-precision training only narrows the weight gap; 0 diff comes only from training calling the same kernel as inference; see [How much QAT can shrink the mismatch](../guides/precision-quant.md#4-how-much-mismatch-qat-can-remove).
+- Do not manufacture a pass by changing tokens, weights, model geometry, precision or tolerance. If the comparison baseline really must change, start a new experiment and re-verify quality.
+- Do not carry DS4's EP/MoE config over to dense Qwen; do not manufacture a performance gain by weakening the BI=0 config, locally disguising BI as off, or removing existing correctness patches.
+- Source tests passing is not the final image passing. Development overlay results belong only to their experiment; the delivered image digest, installed source and build artifacts must match the acceptance object, and the evidence chain is rebuilt after repackaging.
+
+## 3. Inferences no longer carried forward
+
+Historical numbers and criteria stay with the run that produced them; a new task does not inherit a past run's model, dataset, topology, performance statistics method or pass status. Lessons from retracted or narrowed claims:
+
+- A number in a summary is not evidence: find the raw numerator and denominator for the same policy/workload/config, or retract the assertion.
+- Execution completion is not numerical acceptance: finished steps, a started job, an existing adapter file or finite nonzero gradients do not show the target class ran or the comparison passed. Record the instantiated class and its import source, and accept non-empty original-dtype token comparison, module VJP against an independent reference, actual update, shutdown and long-term stability separately.
+- Evidence does not transfer across candidates: a source pin, the same Docker tag, an earlier proxy, an experiment stack or a direct operator call does not prove the current candidate, image or compiled module dispatch. Verify branch, dirty patch, wheel, `.so`, dependencies and digest separately, and re-establish entry-gate evidence for the current candidate.
+- A fixed split count or a pass on one path does not cover other batches, prefill/decode, the first round after resume or cross-node communication; each needs its own evidence.
+- When an acceptance wrapper fails, find the failing layer before resampling or rerunning; a control-plane parsing error does not discard sealed numerical evidence.
+
+Each new case records only "contract → minimal counterexample → discriminating experiment → root cause/minimal fix → regression on the original reproducer → scope/source", with the small raw receipt for disputed numbers. Merge status, recommended dependency versions and best-performing config are volatile; look them up in the target repo.
+
+## 4. Experiment contract
+
+### Define the objects of equality first
+
+State the checkpoint/adapter/policy version, tokenizer and chat template, raw token IDs, position IDs, attention/response mask, padding/packing, and the logits processing on both training and inference sides.
+
+For response token `y[t]`, compare `log p(y[t] | prompt, y[:t])`. Make explicit the prediction position of the first response token, whether EOS counts, and the exclusion rules for truncation and padding. Do not align logits rows of different positions.
+
+Distinguish raw logits, raw logprobs, and logprobs after temperature/repetition penalty/top-k/top-p, and record which one the interface returns. The same seed does not guarantee the same scheduling or RNG consumption: freeze the tokens instead of resampling.
+
+### Record these goals separately
+
+| Goal | Valid evidence | Cannot infer |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Single-side repeatability | A/A with the same input and state | Consistency across batches or processes |
+| batch/layout invariance | Same semantic sample identical under different positions, neighbors and packing | Training and inference are the same |
+| prefill/decode parity | Two execution paths with the same forced tokens | backward or the training update is correct |
+| Cross-stack forward parity | Real training forward against a frozen rollout | Full-vocabulary logits match, if only sampled tokens are compared |
+| Effective training loop | Non-degenerate gradients, parameter change, post-update parity | Convergence or long-term stability |
+
+When the user requires bitwise, compare original-dtype bytes and record mismatching/valid token counts; do not reach a pass through a float cast, probability-space rounding or a tolerance loosened afterwards. If the goal is an error budget, fix the metric and threshold in advance and measure each side's own noise; generic numerical alignment need not be forced to bitwise.
+
+A finite logprob is necessary; an empty mask, all-zero placeholders, missed capture, NaN or the wrong weight version cannot pass. A zero may be legitimate; tell it from a placeholder by hook count, score source and a negative control.
+
+### Recipe and coverage record
+
+When building a train-inference recipe, also fix these inputs, recovering missing items from the existing config first:
+
+| Item | What to record |
+| --- | --- |
+| Workload | Training context length, rollout input/output length distribution, concurrency, packing, training token batch |
+| Hardware | GPU architecture/count, GPU memory, interconnect and target TP/CP/EP/PP/DP, trainer and rollout separately |
+| Numerics | master/deployed weight, activation, KV, accumulation and gradient dtype; quantization granularity, scale rule and update method |
+| Scope | Raw sampled logprob or full-vocabulary logits, applicable hardware/software, Graph/cache path |
+| Budget | Throughput, peak GPU memory, quality and gradient criteria, experiment count and stop condition; with an unknown threshold, report the measurement and do not declare a pass |
+
+Record the measured baseline of the current config, then build a strong performance baseline per the main flow, without exhaustive tuning first. Rust Bench 8192/1024, ignore EOS, c=1–64 is a fixed comparison and does not replace the target context and natural-length workload; a user-specified workload governs, with the difference reported.
+
+A proxy records "full-model function → proxy position → test case → uncovered items" and keeps the hidden/head/expert/quantization geometry and layout that affect kernel selection. Reuse existing modules and tests, but after changing model, dtype or parallelism re-check the contract; changing the config does not carry over the old acceptance.
+
+### Environment fingerprint
+
+Keep the code commit, dirty patch hash, untracked runtime files, image digest, GPU architecture, Torch/Triton/CUDA, actual import path, and native `.so` path and hash. Record TP/PP/CP/EP/DP for trainer and rollout, dtype/quantization/scale, kernel backend, and Graph/compile/cache and autotune config.
+
+Read the resolved config and actual modules/libraries inside the worker, not launcher settings. For weights, record content version and update status of derived weights/scales, not just the path. Keep immutable known-good and known-bad artifacts before diagnosing.
+
+### Scope of conclusions
+
+For each result, record model scale, valid sample count, independent token count, lengths and boundaries, process count, GPU/parallel config and number of updates. Four samples repeated into batch32 are still four independent samples; mixed scheduling a small model never triggers cannot cover the full model.
+
+Record machine budget, maximum experiment count and stop condition. GPU or system faults give `inconclusive`; a failed numerical comparison gives `fail`; `pass` for a scope requires every declared acceptance item.
+
+### Experiment discipline
+
+Write these nine rules into the record before comparing two arms; if any is unmet, the conclusion is "pending re-check".
+
+| Rule | How to do it | Mechanism and example |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| One image per recipe | Both arms use the same image and recipe, differing only in the recipe switch; inject changes with an overlay and record the hash | [One recipe, one image](../guides/recipe-and-acceptance.md#one-recipe-one-image-deliver-true-on-policy-and-the-regular-baseline-with-the-bi-switch) |
+| One seed per config | One seed by default; add more only when the user asks for variance, reported separately | Extra seeds spend budget on variance; most problems are systematic |
+| Small-workload iteration | Iterate with small batch, short outputs and few steps; run the recipe default workload only for final acceptance | The default workload allows only one or two iterations a day |
+| Freeze the criterion first and plant an error | Fix comparison window and tolerance in writing before the run; confirm with a known error that it can judge FAIL; never adjust the threshold after a failure | A threshold chosen afterwards can always pass; [paired acceptance](../guides/recipe-and-acceptance.md#paired-acceptance) |
+| No conclusion from a single e2e run | Measure noise first; on the same hardware and image, report the median of multiple pairs and single pairs separately | [Performance and profiling](../guides/performance.md) |
+| Same fabric | Before comparing communication bottlenecks, confirm both arms use the same transport and record the relevant environment variables | [Same-fabric fairness](../guides/debugging-mismatch.md#same-fabric-fairness) |
+| Same-node comparison | Run paired arms sequentially on the same node or node group, with node names recorded | Memory fragmentation, resident processes and interconnect topology differ between nodes |
+| JIT pollution: check `tl_after_bench=0` | After the run, confirm no new compilation after the bench; results with recompilation are void | [Performance and profiling](../guides/performance.md) |
+| Take metrics by key name | Read numbers from raw metrics (jsonl/W&B) by full key name and cite the key in the report; never by column position in log lines | An `actor/grad_norm` column once read as entropy reversed a conclusion |
+
+List confounders before comparing; see [paired acceptance](../guides/recipe-and-acceptance.md#paired-acceptance).
+
+## 5. Execution state
+
+For every comparison, record the actual execution state, and keep results from different execution states as separate evidence.
+
+### Fields that must be recorded
+
+- Resolved Graph mode, capture sizes, whether the step is prefill/decode/mixed, and kernel call evidence; a successful capture does not mean every step uses the same graph, nor numerics identical to eager.
+- Whether the prefix cache hit, and whether it was disabled/isolated during diagnosis; passing with the cache off does not mean the native lifecycle is fixed.
+- Weight lifecycle phase: cold load, sleep/wake, Graph replay, reload in a new process, one row each.
+- Whether chunk boundary state and partial input buffers of stateful layers such as Mamba/SSM are saved.
+
+### Keep separate evidence
+
+Eager, compiled with Graph off, and production Graph each keep their own artifacts; hooks run at capture, not replay, so a capture dump does not represent replay. List separately: diagnostic runtime override vs formal source candidate, Graph vs no-Graph, forward-only vs real `train()`+autograd. A new process passing does not prove the old process's cache/Graph is fixed; two fixes that each pass go through the gate again when stacked. Once CUDA state is corrupted, end that experiment and collect no more numerical evidence from it.
+
+### Where the mechanisms and methods are
+
+| Question | Where to go |
+| --- | --- |
+| Graph capture vs replay, the Graph/eager 2×2 comparison with fixed composition, which bucket the filler falls into | [BI kernel appendix](../guides/bi-kernels.md) (cudagraph row) |
+| prefix cache semantics, Mamba chunk boundary state, bitwise comparison with "cache off as the gold standard" | [rollout-engine](../guides/rollout-engine.md) |
+| Localizing CUDA asynchronous errors | [debugging-mismatch](../guides/debugging-mismatch.md#isolate-the-side-first) |
+
+## 6. Candidate evidence ledger
+
+Goal: keep an old pass from becoming a new pass.
+
+When an experiment changes model scale, quantization dispatch, attention, MoE, Graph or policy weights, create one ledger row per **candidate execution closure**, then decide what to rerun.
+
+### What one row of evidence is bound to
+
+| Field | What to record and check |
+| --- | --- |
+| Object | Original layer numbers and real adjacency, parameter/quantization geometry, tokenizer, checkpoint content, policy version; a proxy's manually spliced boundaries listed separately |
+| Execution on both sides | Trainer/server image digest, source and overlay hashes, actually imported classes and files, resolved config, native/JIT artifacts |
+| Path | `train()`/autograd/whether backward runs, actual dispatch of attention/norm/linear/MoE, compile/Graph/cache, TP/EP/PP layout |
+| Workload | Content digest of prompt/response tokens, valid mask, length distribution, packing, concurrency, reward/advantage and actual accepted sample count |
+| Criterion | Original dtype, finite valid token count, bitwise mismatch, sample count, first difference, and the independent states of gradient/update/normal exit |
+| Artifacts | Inputs, score, worker/rank receipt, command, time, parent version, hash and `pass`/`fail`/`inconclusive`/`not run` |
+
+`policy_manifest_sha256`, the exported `policy_content_id` and the rollout receipt hash answer three separate questions, **manifest version, weight content, run artifact**, and are not comparable with each other. If the exported content ID is the hash of the export receipt, follow the receipt to check shard hashes against the files the server actually loaded; one equal version string is not enough.
+
+### Entry gates from cheap to expensive
+
+1. **Module.** Use a real triggering input and a non-unit scale/real layout; A/A first, then the candidate's forward against an independent reference; for gradients, check dX/dW/other differentiable quantities separately with the same dY. A pass covers only the shapes, arithmetic and VJP tested.
+2. **Minimal real-adjacency proxy.** Cover the actual order of layer types, not just the operator set. With a fixed 8192+1024 tokens, check inference BI/PD first, then per the [dual-path contract](../workflow/validation.md#old-logprob-and-training-forward-dual-path-contract) verify native old-logprob and the grad-enabled actor forward separately; for a fixed-token comparison only, do not add GSM8K/RL to the proxy. Record source closure, actual class, Graph, non-empty valid tokens and original-dtype mismatch. When any item changes, re-examine whether this step still transfers.
+3. **Full-model zero-update.** Generate a real-workload rollout with the full model on the **current** serving candidate, saving tokens and raw scores; the actor replays the same policy and history before the optimizer update. Check the earliest failing sample, then expand to the agreed sample size; if unequal, stop here and narrow the boundary instead of working around it with five-step RL or a quality evaluation.
+4. **Per-version update.** For each θk, compare on-policy first, then check reward/advantage, backward, master parameters and the optimizer step, then sample θk+1; "the last training step exited" is not "the last version's comparison passed".
+5. **Independent acceptance.** Module gradients, whole-model gradient coverage, real RL, quality, performance, clean exit and the final image each get their own result. Numbers from a previous candidate or another execution mode stay as historical comparison and never fill the current candidate's pass cell.
+
+A fixed-weight serving overlay without RL lifecycle operations such as sleep/wake is only a serving screening candidate, even if BI/PD and 8K/1K paired performance pass; once the lifecycle is restored, rerun the affected proxy, zero-update and post-update comparison. Do not splice historical throughput and another candidate's RL pass into one "completed" version.
+

+
+## 7. Failure records
+
+Keep failure records as they are; append new results, with no overwriting, deletion or editing. For W&B, use a separate project per comparison and read back through the API to check no step is missing. For freezing the criterion, planting a known error and "no conclusion from a single e2e run", see [§4 Experiment discipline](#experiment-discipline).

+# Train-inference consistency workflow: C0–C10
+
+Turn a train-inference difference into a repeatable experiment with fixed input and fixed weights, locate the first divergence, fix or optimize, then return to the real training loop. Keep the user's model, precision, parallelism and consistency target. Switches, thresholds, passing scope and implementation paths from historical cases, reference PRs and implementations already in the training framework (such as an existing true-on-policy path) are experience, not defaults for the current model, dataset or hardware; measure their numerics and training-step time before reusing them.
+
+Forward consistency, backward conformance to the gradient contract, training quality and performance are accepted separately; none replaces another. User config comes first. Recover missing information from the source and resolved config, and ask only for what cannot be recovered and affects the approach. Choose the low-precision recipe by hardware and existing paths, not by a default precision, model or framework. Changing the model or precision requires rechecking coverage and acceptance evidence.

+Work in one directory per task, with state changes in an event log and artifacts carrying provenance sidecars. +
+## Run the cheapest failure criterion first
+
+1. host metadata / shape arithmetic: minimal counterexample of a pure function and boundary parameterization.
+2. Single operator: same input, real dtype/layout, non-finite detection, repeat / cross-process / Graph.
+3. frozen batch replay: the original failing A/C and A/A, full valid-token comparison.
+4. engine: batch composition, prefill/decode, chunk boundaries, cache/Graph, actual parallelism scope.
+5. Real training: non-degenerate reward/advantage, finite non-zero gradients, optimizer step, parameter change, frozen-token alignment after the update.

+
+## RL delivery gates
+
+Training and inference use **the same immutable image digest and the same Python/Torch and runtime dependencies**. They may run on separate nodes and processes, but two environments inside one image cannot be used to dodge compatibility. Complete at least two real updates through the target RL framework's actual entry point and verify each round: original-dtype logprob 0 diff before the update, an actual parameter update, and 0 diff for the new policy after it. Saved rollouts, offline replay, separate images and cold start are diagnostics only. This is a delivery agreement, not a technical claim about all RL systems.
+
+Deliver one vLLM PR, one Megatron PR, one verl PR and one unified image, targeting `vllm-project/vllm:main`, `NVIDIA/Megatron-LM:dev` and `verl-project/verl:main`. Non-observability changes in verl should be limited to the recipe and the image script where possible. Follow [from clean PR to delivery](../practices/code-and-delivery.md#step-10-from-clean-prs-to-verifiable-delivery): check the target branch and full diff, pin cross-repository commits, build the image from clean source, and fill in the [delivery manifest](report-template.md#delivery-manifest).

+
+- **Baseline track**: C1's BI=0 tuning, backend combinations and multi-round performance evidence. Do not sacrifice default performance for consistency in advance; after reasonable tuning, freeze the candidate and wait for human audit.

+- Share the model/precision/hardware/image contract; isolate code, environment and artifacts; keep consistency patches out of BI=0. While the baseline is not final, mark the scope consistency covers and re-verify after config changes.
+- Do not add nodes beyond the budget. On a single node, GPU experiments time-share; during a formal benchmark, run no GPU, heavy CPU or I/O work from the other track. The final performance gap is accepted against the human-confirmed strong baseline with full consistency evidence.

+## Numerical contracts and shared forward
+
+### Check the arithmetic that actually executes
+
+The same formula does not guarantee the same floating-point result. Check accumulation dtype, cast position, FMA, reduction tree, chunking/split-K, approximate activations, quantization scale/rounding, epilogue and the input dtype of the final logprob. The same source can also produce different execution configs through autotune, compile specialization or a different GPU.
+
+A shared kernel still needs its caller, arguments, layout and compile boundary checked; a direct call and a torch.compile fused path may differ. If needed, keep the same forward behind an existing opaque custom-op boundary; do not introduce unproven arithmetic rewrites to imitate the output.
+
+Quantization execution checks (scale taken from the actual runner, quantization dispatch, quantizer outside the `nn.Module` tree, training vs deployment quantization grid) are in the [precision, quantization and QAT guide](../guides/precision-quant.md#training-side-numerics), the grid in [P8](../guides/precision-quant.md#p8-training-grid-differs-from-the-deployment-grid); format and scale records are in [conversion chain §1](../guides/precision-quant.md#1-four-stages).
+
+First check that the semantics exist on both sides. When a feature is inside the kernel on one side and external or missing on the other, the difference does not go away with precision settings. Run a two-layer minimal comparison per model feature (attention sink, RoPE variant, final norm, etc.), enabling one at a time. In the external MiMo case SWA alone gave 0 and SWA+sink gave `3.906e-03`, because only one side's kernel included the sink.
+
+### Discrete decisions come before last-bit error
+
+After router/indexer logits, also compare the selected set, the order and the tie-break. Top-K with the same set in a different order still changes downstream gather/reduction. A deterministic tie-break defines the index order for equal scores and keeps the invalid/padding index contract.
+
+For MoE, also fix or verify dispatch, expert capacity, grouped GEMM geometry, quantization and combine. Do not hide a router difference by forcing expert indices; forced routing only isolates the downstream.
+
+The top-k/top-p truncation set is also a discrete decision: a last-bit logit difference moves tokens near the cutoff in or out of the set, and the normalization denominator of the processed logprob jumps with it. Compare the candidate set before processed logprob. MiMo-V2.6 replays the candidate set together with R3 in production: rollout records a fixed-shape, full-vocabulary bitmap (avoiding host sync and truncation), and training renormalizes within the set. If the contract adopts this replay, state in the report that it masks the set difference, and count the set flip rate separately.
+
+### Test shape and process boundaries
+
+For the same victim, construct batch1 / multiple neighbors, different physical positions, lengths on both sides of a boundary, cross-process autotune, prefill/decode and Graph/eager. Different launches when only M changes are not a numerical difference; measure the output. Finding no difference covers only the shapes tested.
+
+SSM chunk recurrence and per-token recurrence can be two legal but different rounding paths. Unifying them requires matching the chunk grid, boundary state precision and gate order, not just a deterministic switch.
+
+For history-dependent operators, a single token's scan/conv input and output can make an upstream history difference look like an error in that operator. First find the first differing token at each layer over the **full prompt batch**, then capture norm, projection, conv, scan, gate and output projection in order at that layer. A single-position probe only narrows candidates; it does not prove the first cause. A plain Python hook in a compiled graph may hold stale warmup data; verify capture freshness with a predictable sentinel such as embedding/residual, and if needed use the custom-op boundary that actually executes and a separate buffer.
+
+### Boundary between shared forward and backward
+
+With a shared inference forward + native differentiable VJP, verify separately: forward parity, a finite gradient for every trainable parameter, and gradient comparison under a cotangent representable in the same dtype. Operator-level VJP verification does not prove the whole-model gradient is bitwise equal to the original training implementation.
+
+Do not detach the inference output and use it as a trainable substitute. A finite gradient does not mean effective learning; also check that advantage/reward is not degenerate, the gradient is non-zero, and parameters and optimizer state are updated.
+
+### Changing the arithmetic baseline
+
+If you deliberately change both sides' arithmetic baseline to align them, keep the old baseline, build a new frozen rollout, state that "old outputs are not guaranteed to stay bitwise unchanged", and run model quality and performance regressions. Success numbers from the old baseline do not carry over to the new implementation.

+# Train–inference consistency report
+
+## Outcome and scope
+
+State pass/fail/inconclusive for the requested scope. Record model/layers, independent samples, valid tokens, dtype, topology, Graph/cache paths, update count and untested conditions.
+
+Link the human-approved acceptance checklist: required vs out-of-scope checks, recipe revision, two-update stop condition, quality/resume coverage and target-repository submission requirements. Out-of-scope checks are unverified, not passed; finishing the short run does not complete missing required checks.
+
+## Immutable experiment
+
+Record source commits and dirty patch hashes, loaded libraries, image digest, GPU, checkpoint/policy identity, input bundle digest, score semantics, resolved config, commands, resource budget and artifacts.
+
+Separate source, installed wheel, loaded native libraries and JIT specializations. State whether the measured runtime and the final delivered image are identical; if not, name the missing verification instead of inheriting the result.
+
+For recipe work, record training context, rollout length distribution, concurrency, packing/token batch, hardware/interconnect and master/deployment/activation/KV/accumulation/gradient dtypes, plus quantization granularity, scale/update rules and the quality/throughput/memory budgets defined before testing. Unknown budgets stay unaccepted even when measurements exist.
+
+## Delivery manifest
+
+For the three-PR / one-image delivery, fill this from the final clean build, not development overlays. Use full SHAs and immutable image identity; mark missing evidence as not run.
+
+| Deliverable | Review / source identity | Build or acceptance evidence |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| vLLM PR | URL; target owner/branch/base SHA; head SHA | Build command and wheel/native/JIT inputs |
+| Megatron PR | URL; target owner/branch/base SHA; head SHA | Installed model / primitive / adapter identity |
+| verl PR | URL; target owner/branch/base SHA; head SHA | Recipe and image build script paths |
+| Unified image | Base and final platform digests; dependency pins | Build log; actual trainer and rollout worker imports/libraries; no development source mounts |

+
+Each PR is complete against the agreed base, not stacked on an unmerged feature branch; cross-repository dependency pins are expected. Every required runtime file outside the PRs must be a pinned existing dependency; an uncommitted production patch is a delivery gap.
