+| Proxy inference ↔ actual grad-enabled actor forward | | | |
+| Backward / SFT / RL, if in proxy scope | | | |
+| Upgrade to full-model BI work | | | |
+
+For each cross-stack row, follow the [dual-path contract](validation.md#old-logprob-and-training-forward-dual-path-contract): model geometry, frozen policy/checkpoint identity, source/image digest, dtype, topology, model/grad modes, output requires_grad, actual backends, raw logprob mismatch count and first mismatch. Keep native no-grad scoring semantics; its pass does not prove grad-enabled forward parity. Capture scores before updates and loss transforms.
+
+| Gate | Command / artifact | Result and count | Scope limitation |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Original failing replay | | | |
+| Operator / metadata regression | | | |
+| Engine and production layouts | | | |
+| Independent module VJP and one optimizer update | | | |
+| Controlled proxy SFT (A/B/C paths) | | | |
+| Real backward/update | | | |
+| θ0 / θ1 / θ2 parity | | | |
+| First post-checkpoint-resume export / parity | | | |
+| Model quality | | | |
+| Clean shutdown / sustained run | | | |
+| Final immutable image, without development overlays | | | |
+
+For two-update RL, keep a receipt per policy θ0, θ1, θ2: input/mask identity, valid token count, original-byte mismatches, actual trainer-forward execution and update norm/count. Record both forward-path results at matching frozen policy versions. Worker exit is checked at final shutdown, not at each policy transition.
+
+## SFT controls and quality (when training is in scope)
+
+Separate SFT-A (production), SFT-B (same visible forward at the same snapshot plus an independent surrogate) and SFT-C (verified native training); these labels are independent of replay packing variants. Link same-checkpoint/same-batch A/B gradients and optimizer deltas; once trajectories diverge, later forward values are not assumed identical. A/C differences include forward/quantization changes.
+
+Record initial master and optimizer state, data/order, labels/masks, packing, effective-token normalization, batch/accumulation, learning-rate schedule, clipping, precision/loss scaling, RNG/dropout/recompute and intentional differences. Keep raw train, held-out and fixed-probe loss, gradient norm, update RMS, clipping/nonfinite/skipped-step counts, throughput and baseline/seed variation when available. Use one optimizer-step or effective-token axis; report predefined windows/thresholds, missing controls and whether evidence is only a short smoke run.
+
+## Performance
+
+Record matched work, warm/cold timing, node pool and paired order, repetitions, latency/throughput, kernel/rollout/full-step results and numerical receipts. Separate measured improvements, rejected candidates and estimates.
+
+For 8K/1K acceptance, link the [approved aggregation protocol](../guides/recipe-and-acceptance.md#pairing-and-computation): formula, repetitions, per-concurrency thresholds and invalid-leg replacement rules. Include all raw pairs, exclusions with reasons and the approved aggregate per c; median paired loss and loss from median throughputs are different statistics. Other phase timings are diagnostics, not gates.
+
+Where relevant, include training time, peak memory, launch count vs token batch, CPU gaps and repeated quantization/allocation. Separate early feasibility profiles from final full-model optimization; normal autoregressive decoding is not evidence of an avoidable per-token prefill/training loop.
+
+State whether this is a BI-only causal comparison or each side's best valid stack, and list all differing flags/backends. Include prompt count vs expanded requests, actual input/output lengths, completed output tokens, wall-time denominator and whether the run is fixed-length synthetic or natural-EOS. Do not sum overlapping GPU ranges or percentages from separate ablations.
+
+## Evidence corrections and retention
+
+List superseded claims with the correcting artifact and reason. Record which original failure bundles, checkpoints and small receipts are retained, their storage budget/location, and any missing eval steps. Never fill a curve with a different policy lineage.
+
+## Remaining work
+
+List concrete gaps and the smallest next experiment. State whether production hooks/config were restored. Keep raw evidence; do not upgrade historical or partial results into current completion.
+
+## Experiment record (YAML)
+
+```yaml
+# Train-inference consistency replay experiment record: each variant changes only one variable, everything else is fixed.
+purpose: "frozen-policy old-logprob replay"
+target: "bitwise selected-token raw logprob"
+rollout: "/absolute/path/to/frozen-rollout"      # original framework batch, not exported scores
+checkpoint: "content id + pre-update recovery path"
+environment: "image digest, source+patch hashes, libraries, GPU"
+topology:
+  trainer: "TP/PP/CP/EP/DP"
+  rollout: "TP/PP/CP/EP/DP"
+state: "RNG, mutable buffers, Graph/cache and reset policy"
+budget: {max_runs: 3, timeout_seconds: 600}
+variants:
+  - {name: A, change: "none (A/A baseline)", cmd: "", output: "", exit: null, result: ""}
+  - {name: B, change: "none (A/A repeat)", cmd: "", output: "", exit: null, result: ""}
+  - {name: C, change: "packing reversed", cmd: "", output: "", exit: null, result: ""}
+```

+# Tiered regression and completion criteria
+
+## Full-model entry gate: pass proxy train-inference forward first
+
+When backends, compile paths or delivery images have changed, check against the [candidate evidence ledger](../practices/evidence-and-experiments.md#6-candidate-evidence-ledger) whether old results still apply. A passing old candidate is history only and does not fill the current candidate's entry gate cells.
+
+Before full-model correctness or training experiments, provide the evidence below. Missing or not executed counts as not passed; repeated full-model launches are no substitute. Proxy inference-internal BI/PD and proxy training forward↔inference logprob comparison are two independent results: the former passing does not mean the latter passes.
+
+| Gate | Minimal evidence |
+| --- | --- |
+| Proxy coverage | Inventory of operator types, necessary adjacent-layer interactions, quantization geometry, state and parallel paths; uncovered items stated |
+| Inference BI/PD | Batch, prefill/decode and mixed-scheduling comparison on the proxy with fixed weights and tokens; proves only consistency inside inference |
+| Training forward↔inference | Same proxy, same policy weights, fixed tokens: verify native old-logprob recomputation and the grad-enabled actor forward used in training separately, each against the target production inference path; keep evidence per the dual-path contract below |
+| Backward and quality | [Independent module gradient comparison](../guides/backward-validation.md#layer-1-module-level-vjp-comparison) with reference implementation, tolerances and raw results; controlled SFT per task scope, or an explicit statement that quality is not covered |
+| Real RL update | At least two effective updates, θ0/θ1/θ2 same-policy comparison, actual parameter change, normal exit; sequence below |
+| Performance feasibility | launch/sync/memory overhead on real shapes and the proxy profile, ruling out bottlenecks such as per-token launches in batchable prefill/training; the target Graph path works |
+
+This is an escalation gate, not the completion criterion: two-step RL does not prove convergence, and the proxy does not prove full depth, capacity, long context or cross-node correctness. On the full model, extend coverage one item at a time. Inference-only tasks apply only the relevant gates, state that training is not accepted, and add no training work.
+
+Before escalating, record per gate in the [report template](report-template.md#verification): `pass`/`fail`/`inconclusive`/`not run`, command, artifact path and the bound model geometry, weights, source/image, precision and parallelism. Accept only current-candidate evidence. For training forward↔inference, the bitwise target requires original-dtype mismatch of valid tokens to be 0; tasks with an agreed error budget use the predefined standard and cannot use it to report a bitwise failure as a pass. An unexecuted training forward, an empty mask, or passing only single-operator or inference BI/PD tests must not release to the full model. Keep the first failing sample on the proxy for layer-by-layer localization, and after the fix rerun the original failing case and the affected matrix.
+
+### old-logprob and training forward dual-path contract
+
+- **Native old-logprob recomputation:** follow the framework's actual path and its `no_grad`/`forward_only` semantics; do not force autograd on for acceptance. Its result proves only that this scoring path matches rollout.
+- **Actual training forward:** with the same frozen θ, token history and valid mask, run the grad-enabled actor branch training actually uses, capture logprob before the loss transform, and compare with rollout independently. Keep the target packing, recompute, operators and parallelism; do not substitute a diagnostic forward. Passing does not replace the later independent backward validation.
+- Record per path: model mode, grad mode, output `requires_grad`, operator class / backend / source hash, original dtype, non-empty valid token count and mismatch. Diagnostics (substitute attention/MoE, Graph off) prove only that path; `forward_only` alone is not grounds for rejection, and native old-logprob passing does not prove the grad-enabled branch.
+- The comparison happens before the corresponding policy update, for both proxy and full-model θ0 entry. If the formal recipe has several minibatch updates per round, do not require 0 diff between the updated actor and the old-θ rollout, and do not modify the algorithm to manufacture equality; record the real parameter version and compare only within one version.
+
+When an adapter / overlay is injected dynamically, the receipt must also record the actual object's class, source file and key config and assert that the target callsite was hit. A script directory placed before the overlay in `PYTHONPATH` can silently load an old adapter; a 0 diff from such a run cannot vouch for the new candidate.
+
+If the user limits the minimal proxy to fixed-token logprob comparison (or forward only), do not require GSM8K, SFT or two-step RL; mark those gates `not run`, not passed. Scale up as agreed only after the proxy train-inference forward passes. Before any multi-step full-model RL, first complete a zero-update same-policy logprob comparison with **full-model θ0 real workload, real training mode, target production inference mode**, then the necessary gradient validation and effective-update checks. A fixed 8K/1K proxy pass does not replace the full-model variable-length workload. When full-model θ0 fails, stop optimizer updates, keep the failing trajectory and shrink to the first divergence. This scope adjustment does not waive the proxy forward gate.
+
+### Limited exceptions that allow going to the full model early
+
+- Establishing the BI=0 performance/quality baseline of the full target model is not approval for full-model BI debugging or training.
+- When a fault depends on real depth, capacity, cross-layer state or cross-node topology and cannot be reproduced on a semantics-preserving proxy, targeted full-model diagnosis is allowed. Before the experiment, write down why the proxy is insufficient, the hypotheses to distinguish, the minimal scale and the stop condition.
+- Scaling up does not scale up resource permissions: no extra GPUs, no stopping other jobs, no bypassing the model/runner scope the user set.
+
+### Faster iteration and fallback on failure
+
+Judge each change's impact first: minimal counterexample, single operator or fixed replay, then the relevant proxy gates, then the staged full model; do not repeat all ten steps per commit. Changes to shared arithmetic or gradients regress the affected forward/backward; final delivery still runs the full agreed acceptance.
+
+On a full-model failure, first save the input before the first divergence, the weight version, metadata, cache/routing and necessary RNG state, and extract a module or few-layer reproducer. Iterate on it only after confirming the fault survives shrinking. If the fault disappears, a passing shrunk test is not a fix, and the full-model reproduction is kept.
+
+Fixed rollout / module inputs may be cached and replayed in an isolated resident process, bound to fingerprints of weights, input, config and necessary state; a new implementation still reruns the comparison. Each scale-up states the existing evidence and the open question the new scale answers.
+
+If a candidate fix changes the sampling trajectory or EOS stop point, save the new token history and replay training old logprob on it with the same weight version. The old trajectory remains a fixed-input diagnostic; comparing new inference against the old response length is not an end-to-end pass. List evidence separately for a diagnostic runtime override, a formal source candidate, Graph/no-Graph, forward-only and real `train()`+autograd. An isolation package may be used for localization; final acceptance returns to the delivered code and the default target execution mode.
+
+## Start from the cheapest failure criterion
+
+1. host metadata/shape arithmetic: minimal counterexample of a pure function and boundary parameterization; if needed, exhaustively check equivalence before and after the fix.
+2. Single operator: same input, real dtype/layout, non-finite detection, repeat/cross-process and Graph.
+3. frozen batch replay: the original failing A/C and A/A, full valid-token comparison; UID mapping passes.
+4. engine: batch composition, prefill/decode, chunk boundaries, cache/Graph, actual parallelism scope.
+5. Real training (when in scope): non-degenerate reward/advantage, finite and meaningful non-zero gradients, optimizer step, actual parameter change, frozen-token alignment after the update.
+6. Production acceptance: full model, agreed multiple steps, update/restore lifecycle, quality evaluation and paired performance.
+
+Not every task runs every tier. Report the tiers completed; when the user asks only for diagnosis, do not start full training. Extend existing test suites first; do not replace behavior tests with assertions on source strings.
+
+## Preventing false greens
+
+- Zero valid tokens, comparison not executed, missing rank/sample: invalid experiment.
+- All-zero score, mask all false, the same sample repeated: check the producer and coverage; a passing comparison is not enough.
+- probability/KL/logPPL is zero: still check the original logprob bytes.
+- Zero gradient or identical rewards: maybe no effective update; check advantage, update count and parameter difference.
+- Small model / short output passes: confirm the full model's mixed-step and long-context trigger conditions.
+- A shrunk proxy's error magnitude is not the full-model baseline: in the external MiMo case the 12-layer proxy was `1.866e-12` and full-depth real weights were `1.143e-02`. The proxy only verifies the execution path.
+- In-training mismatch metric is 0: confirm the micro-batch really ran the trainer forward. The framework may skip the forward for a zero-advantage batch and return 0, a trivial match; count only reports with non-zero advantage.
+- A success marker written before the process was killed: separate a completed numerical experiment from normal exit / long-term stability.
+- probs_diff is 0 but many sibling samples within a group are identical: a sampling diversity defect, independent of the consistency metric. Count distinct rollout samples per group; the mechanism and fix are in [rollout-engine §1](../guides/rollout-engine.md#1-sampling-seed-collision).
+- The launcher shows `COMPLETED 0:0`: read the recipe's own exit code. When tests report passed, check the skipped count; GPU cases may be skipped wholesale by a marker or environment gate.
+
+## Unified measurement basis and matrix for forward consistency
+
+Fix policy, token history, position, mask and tensor semantics, and record per item the original dtype/shape, valid token count (greater than 0), non-finite count, bitwise mismatch count, maximum absolute difference and first failing position. A dtype difference is a contract inconsistency first; do not convert and then claim a bitwise pass. After aligning semantics, compare contiguous tensor bytes that preserve the bit pattern or an equal-width integer view; floating-point `==` does not distinguish positive and negative zero. NaN/Inf in a valid logprob is a failure even with identical bytes. Sampled-token comparison does not extrapolate to the full vocabulary.
+
+Keep cases and artifacts per item for the target execution scope, and list unsupported / not run items:
+
+| Dimension | Comparison under fixed semantics |
+| --- | --- |
+| A/A | Repeated execution with the same weights, input and state; in a separate process if needed |
+| BI | Single request, different batch sizes, companion requests, permutation/position and packing |
+| PD | Full prefill, chunked prefill and step-by-step decode on the same history, covering mixed scheduling |
+| Length and branches | Real lengths, chunk/causal boundaries, and cases that trigger sparse selection, MoE and special modules; not only random tokens |
+| Execution state | Target Graph capture/replay, cache reuse/reset and the actual parallel layout |
+
+The bitwise target requires mismatch=0; error-budget tasks report against the predefined standard and are never recorded as a bitwise pass. Gradient tolerances are defined independently, see [module VJP](../guides/backward-validation.md#layer-1-module-level-vjp-comparison) and [SFT control](#proxy-sft-three-way-control).
+
+## Two-step RL sequence
+
+This sequence is the lower bound for entry; "container started / training script exited 0" is not a pass.
+
+When the task includes the full train-inference loop, complete at least this sequence; every actor recomputation uses the same policy and token history as its rollout:
+
+```text
+θ0 → rollout0 → actor(θ0) recompute and compare
+   → backward0 / optimizer update → θ1
+θ1 → rollout1 → actor(θ1) recompute and compare
+   → backward1 / optimizer update → θ2
+θ2 → rollout2 → actor(θ2) recompute and compare
+```
+
+The θ2 comparison needs no third optimizer update. To compare outputs across policies, use the same frozen token history; do not rely on sampling happening to match.
+
+For each stage save the policy content identifier, token/mask, non-empty valid comparison count and raw byte comparison result; for each update save finite loss/gradient, coverage of parameters that should have gradients, master update norm and optimizer step.
+
+For a bitwise task the θ0, θ1 and θ2 comparisons must all have mismatch=0, with two effective updates and a normal exit actually completed. Skipped updates, both sides reading an old cache, an empty mask or comparing only probability summaries are not allowed.
+
+A small master update may not cross a quantization bucket, so deployment bytes need not change every step. Judge an update by master update norm and optimizer step, not by step count or byte change.
+
+## Proxy SFT three-way control
+
+The three paths, controlled variables, recorded items and localization order are in [Backward validation layer 3](../guides/backward-validation.md#layer-3-proxy-sft-three-arm-comparison). If the module gradient comparison fails, fix the implementation before starting SFT.
+
+## Performance and model quality
+
+When forward arithmetic, precision, scorer or inference path changes, rerun the same quality evaluation within the human-reviewed scope and the target repository's requirements. Record model/data, problem count, prompt format, generation settings, statistical variation and unfinished parts; mark out-of-round items unverified, and add no SFT or long runs. A loss decrease or two-step reward change does not prove no quality regression.
+
+Micro benchmarks, fixed-token parity, generation quality, normal exit and multi-step stability are separate. A run with four non-zero updates and 139,260 bitwise-equal tokens that ended in a DataLoader error supports four-step alignment, not clean shutdown or 50-step stability.
+
+The full model covers the reviewed scope (real depth / weights, target context, concurrency, packing, parallelism/hardware, cache/Graph) and reruns affected correctness gates; proxy curves do not extrapolate to full-model quality. Final performance is accepted on 8K/1K per the [paired statistics protocol](../guides/recipe-and-acceptance.md#pairing-and-computation); training and full-step times may be listed as diagnostics and add no performance gate. Scope and stop condition of the two-step short run are in the [general two-step acceptance agreement](#general-two-step-acceptance-agreement).
+
+## Failure classification and delivery
+
+Use `pass`, `fail`, `inconclusive` with a reason. Keep source/patch/image/bundle hashes, commands, per-item counts, earliest difference, excluded hypotheses, and before/after results on the original reproducer. Cleaned-up code needs re-verification or explicit behavior-equivalence evidence; old tests do not vouch for new code.
+
+Passed items stand despite unfinished ones, but the final conclusion is limited in scope. Use the [report template](report-template.md). Formal upstream contributions also follow the target repository's duplicate check, human line-by-line review, tests and AI assistance disclosure; historical cases do not mean the review was done on the author's behalf.
+
+If the delivery includes an image, the gate object is the final immutable artifact, not a development image plus a source mount. Verify the closure per [runtime provenance](../guides/environment-provenance.md); accept save per [01 §3.2](../guides/checkpoint-resume.md#32-reproduce-and-discriminate), load per [§4](../guides/checkpoint-resume.md#4-load-enough-capacity-does-not-mean-enough-for-the-transient-peak), and the first resume per [§6](../guides/checkpoint-resume.md#6-how-to-prove-resume-is-correct). Passing environment checks proves only the preconditions for running, not GPU numerics or performance.
+
+## Recipe review materials and two-step acceptance agreement
+
+The integration point is in [training-side model support](../guides/training-forward.md); only process agreements are here.
+
+### Recipe and PR delivery contract
+
+Locate the existing integration layer in the selected version first. Megatron's `experimental/lite/examples/verl/verl_mlite/` provides the verl engine adapter; an external integration package installs normally into the unified image, and removing the runtime overlay does not require reimplementing the engine in verl. Check the actual engine registration, model factory, batch conversion, loss normalization and optimizer path, and list reusable interfaces and specific gaps.
+
+- **verl PR** contains by default the model's DAPO recipe and the unified image Dockerfile. Public interface changes beyond these two: submit the gap and plan first, implement after human review; necessary regression tests may stay.
+- **Megatron PR** contains the model, operators and necessary support in the existing `verl_mlite` integration layer; do not move generic code that does not belong in Megatron there just to keep the verl PR at two files.
+- **vLLM PR** contains the necessary inference-side model, kernel, state and weight loading changes.
+- Per the [general delivery target](../practices/code-and-delivery.md#8-three-repo-delivery-from-experimental-implementation-to-three-prs-and-one-image), submit complete PRs to the three main repositories, including the required model adaptation and not stacked on another unmerged feature PR; pin cross-repository dependency versions and state the build order. Consistency uses mLite and the training baseline uses the existing verl recipe's default MCore path (see [the workflow](README.md#gate-table)); do not merge them into one training scheme.
+
+### DAPO reference and review materials
+
+[verl #7688](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7688), at reviewed version `640c5f0a317307e99636924804c40624242fa19b`, uses Megatron's integration package through `model_engine=mlite` and `pkg://verl_mlite.config`, so the verl diff needs only the recipe and the Dockerfile. Follow its real `verl.trainer.main_ppo` execution chain; do not assume its config keys, DeepSeek precision/topology, mounts or overlay fit the current model.
+
+The reference case's model, data and evaluation set are not defaults. Choose training data / reward by target model and human agreement, and keep the training set distinct from the quality evaluation set. Finish config resolution and the necessary proxy smoke, then submit for human review:
+
+- Executable launch script, unified image digest, commit of each repository and full resolved config.
+- Parameter differences from the reference recipe with reasons: data/reward, prompt/response length, rollout count, batch/microbatch, parallelism, quantization / KV precision, optimizer.
+- Proxy check results, known uncovered items, and the acceptance scope of the full-model zero update and the two real updates.
+
+Formal full-model E2E starts after a human confirms a specific recipe version and the proxy entry passes. Workload or numerical/update changes are reviewed again; path and log changes that leave input and execution semantics unchanged are only recorded. This gate does not block already authorized builds or proxy development.
+
+### General two-step acceptance agreement
+
+- **Freeze versions first.** Record the heads of the three delivery PRs, the unified image digest and the full recipe config. Changes that affect results require a version update and the related verification; old artifacts cannot be reused for acceptance.
+- **Review the recipe first** (materials above). Confirming process or scope does not approve an unsubmitted recipe. The review checklist also marks which quality, restore and long-run checks are required or out of scope for this round, and the evidence the target repository requires; out of scope does not mean passed, and the short run ending does not hide missing required items.
+- **Run two effective updates by default.** Use the formal recipe and shorten only the execution length to two steps; do not downgrade data, sequence length, rollout count, batch, optimizer, algorithm, parallelism or backend. If the stop step count drives the learning-rate schedule, keep the formal recipe's learning-rate/warmup semantics for the first two steps instead of compressing the full schedule into two; the implementation is reviewed with the recipe.
+- **Keep the existing correctness gates.** After the proxy real training forward passes, run the full-model [two-step RL sequence](#two-step-rl-sequence) with actual parameter updates; a fixed-weight replay does not count instead.
+- **Performance is accepted only on 8K/1K.** On the frozen version, use Rust Bench at 8192 input / 1024 output, ignore EOS, c=1/8/32/64, against the human-confirmed BI=0 baseline and performance budget. Training forward, backward and full RL step times may be recorded but add no performance gate.
+- After the two updates, the θ2 comparison and the agreed 8K/1K performance pass, stop the short run and report. Overall acceptance is still judged item by item against the review checklist; if a required item is missing, state that it is not complete. Do not extend to 100 steps, add an MCore long-run comparison or new quality gates, and do not extrapolate the two-step result to long-run training quality.
+
+### E2E comparison target
+
+Run the [two-step RL sequence](#two-step-rl-sequence) through the real trainer entry point. 0 diff means equal original-dtype logprob for the same weight version, token history and valid mask; θ0 and θ1 outputs may differ. Verify the actual master update each round (not step count or byte change). Disk replay is a localization tool and does not replace acceptance through the real trainer entry point.
+
+Finally re-verify with the image built from the delivery PRs and the reviewed recipe. Record standalone engine smoke, old image numerical results and historical performance separately; they do not replace full evidence from this execution entry point.

@@ -0,0 +1,218 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Tests for the LoRA-aware FlashInfer TRTLLM MXFP4 experts
+(`TrtLlmMxfp4LoRAExperts`) against a float64 reference."""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from tests.kernels.moe.utils import make_dummy_moe_config
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.activation import MoEActivation
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.config import mxfp4_w4a16_moe_quant_config
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.experts.trtllm_lora_moe import (
+    TrtLlmMxfp4LoRAExperts,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.oracle.mxfp4 import (
+    Mxfp4MoeBackend,
+    _requested_kernel_cls,
+    backend_to_kernel_cls,
+    convert_weight_to_mxfp4_moe_kernel_format,
+)
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.utils.flashinfer import has_flashinfer_trtllm_fused_moe
+from vllm.utils.torch_utils import set_random_seed
+
+# FlashInfer's TRTLLM MoE LoRA kernels only run on SM100-family GPUs.
+pytestmark = [
+    pytest.mark.skipif(
+        not current_platform.is_device_capability_family(100)
+        or not has_flashinfer_trtllm_fused_moe(),
+        reason="Requires an SM100-family GPU and FlashInfer TRTLLM fused MoE",
+    ),
+    pytest.mark.skip_global_cleanup,
+]
+
+E, N, K, T, TOPK = 16, 256, 512, 33, 4
+E2M1 = [0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6]
+
+
+def _dequant_mxfp4(weight: torch.Tensor, scale: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """(E, R, K/2) packed nibbles + (E, R, K/32) e8m0 scales -> (E, R, K) f64."""
+    nibbles = torch.stack([weight & 0xF, weight >> 4], dim=-1).flatten(-2).long()
+    magnitude = torch.tensor(E2M1, dtype=torch.float64, device=weight.device)
+    values = magnitude[nibbles & 7] * torch.where(nibbles >> 3 == 1, -1.0, 1.0)
+    block_scale = torch.pow(2.0, scale.double() - 127.0)
+    return values * block_scale.repeat_interleave(32, dim=-1)
+
+
+def _make_experts(has_bias: bool, activation=MoEActivation.SILU):
+    w13 = torch.randint(0, 256, (E, 2 * N, K // 2), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
+    w2 = torch.randint(0, 256, (E, K, N // 2), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
+    s13 = torch.randint(118, 122, (E, 2 * N, K // 32), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
+    s2 = torch.randint(118, 122, (E, K, N // 32), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
+    b13 = torch.randn(E, 2 * N, device="cuda") / 4 if has_bias else None
+    b2 = torch.randn(E, K, device="cuda") / 4 if has_bias else None
+    k13, k2, ks13, ks2, kb13, kb2 = convert_weight_to_mxfp4_moe_kernel_format(
+        Mxfp4MoeBackend.FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_BF16,
+        None,
+        w13.clone(),
+        w2.clone(),
+        s13.clone(),
+        s2.clone(),
+        None if b13 is None else b13.clone(),
+        None if b2 is None else b2.clone(),
+        _cache_permute_indices={},
+    )
+    config = make_dummy_moe_config(
+        num_experts=E,
+        experts_per_token=TOPK,
+        hidden_dim=K,
+        intermediate_size=N,
+        activation=activation,
+    )
+    quant_config = mxfp4_w4a16_moe_quant_config(ks13, ks2, kb13, kb2)
+    experts = TrtLlmMxfp4LoRAExperts(config, quant_config)
+    reference = (_dequant_mxfp4(w13, s13), _dequant_mxfp4(w2, s2), b13, b2)
+    return experts, (k13, k2), reference
+
+
+def _make_inputs():
+    x = torch.randn(T, K, device="cuda").to(torch.bfloat16)
+    ids = torch.stack([torch.randperm(E, device="cuda")[:TOPK] for _ in range(T)])
+    weights = torch.rand(T, TOPK, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32) + 0.1
+    return x, ids.to(torch.int32), weights
+
+
+def _reference(reference, x, ids, weights, gate_delta=None, up_delta=None):
+    """Float64 MoE; the checkpoint w13 layout is [gate | up]."""
+    w13, w2, b13, b2 = reference
+    ids = ids.long()
+    h = torch.einsum("tk,tjnk->tjn", x.double(), w13[ids])
+    if b13 is not None:
+        h = h + b13.double()[ids]
+    gate, up = h[..., :N], h[..., N:]
+    if gate_delta is not None:
+        gate, up = gate + gate_delta.double(), up + up_delta.double()
+    act = torch.nn.functional.silu(gate) * up
+    out = torch.einsum("tjn,tjkn->tjk", act, w2[ids])
+    if b2 is not None:
+        out = out + b2.double()[ids]
+    return act, (out * weights.double()[..., None]).sum(1)
+
+
+def _run_lora_path(experts, kernel_weights, x, ids, weights, delta):
+    """`delta` is (T, TOPK, 2I) in the [up | gate] order of apply_w13_lora."""
+    lora_context = SimpleNamespace(w13_num_slices=2)
+    gemm2, expert_weights, idx_map, act_permuted = experts.invoke_routed_moe(
+        hidden_states=x,
+        w1=kernel_weights[0],
+        w2=kernel_weights[1],
+        topk_ids_and_weights=(ids, weights),
+        gemm1_lora_delta=experts.prepare_gemm1_lora_delta(delta, lora_context, ids),
+        global_num_experts=E,
+        a1q_scale=None,
+        output=torch.empty(T, K, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda"),
+    )
+    assert act_permuted.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+    act = experts._unpermute_activation(act_permuted, idx_map, T, TOPK, N)
+    output = torch.empty(T, K, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    no_w2_delta = torch.zeros(T, TOPK, K, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    experts._finalize_with_w2_lora(
+        output, gemm2, expert_weights, idx_map, no_w2_delta, T, TOPK
+    )
+    return act.view(T, TOPK, N), output
+
+
+def _rel_err(actual: torch.Tensor, expected: torch.Tensor) -> float:
+    actual, expected = actual.double(), expected.double()
+    return float((actual - expected).norm() / expected.norm())
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("has_bias", [False, True])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_gemm1_lora_delta_matches_reference(has_bias: bool):
+    set_random_seed(0)
+    experts, kernel_weights, reference = _make_experts(has_bias)
+    x, ids, weights = _make_inputs()
+    gate_delta = (torch.randn(T, TOPK, N, device="cuda") / 2).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    up_delta = (torch.randn(T, TOPK, N, device="cuda") / 2).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    ref_act, ref_out = _reference(reference, x, ids, weights, gate_delta, up_delta)
+    _, ref_base_out = _reference(reference, x, ids, weights)
+    # The delta has to matter for the layout check below to mean anything.
+    assert _rel_err(ref_out, ref_base_out) > 0.3
+
+    delta = torch.cat([up_delta, gate_delta], dim=-1)
+    act, out = _run_lora_path(experts, kernel_weights, x, ids, weights, delta)
+    assert _rel_err(act, ref_act) < 0.02
+    assert _rel_err(out, ref_out) < 0.02
+
+    swapped = torch.cat([gate_delta, up_delta], dim=-1)
+    _, out = _run_lora_path(experts, kernel_weights, x, ids, weights, swapped)
+    assert _rel_err(out, ref_out) > 0.3
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("has_bias", [False, True])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_zero_delta_matches_base_path(has_bias: bool):
+    set_random_seed(0)
+    experts, kernel_weights, reference = _make_experts(has_bias)
+    x, ids, weights = _make_inputs()
+    base = torch.empty(T, K, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    experts.invoke_routed_moe(
+        hidden_states=x,
+        w1=kernel_weights[0],
+        w2=kernel_weights[1],
+        topk_ids_and_weights=(ids, weights),
+        gemm1_lora_delta=None,
+        global_num_experts=E,
+        a1q_scale=None,
+        output=base,
+    )
+    _, ref_out = _reference(reference, x, ids, weights)
+    assert _rel_err(base, ref_out) < 0.02
+
+    zero = torch.zeros(T, TOPK, 2 * N, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    _, out = _run_lora_path(experts, kernel_weights, x, ids, weights, zero)
+    assert _rel_err(out, base) < 0.02
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("w13_num_slices", [1, 2])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("activation", [MoEActivation.SILU, MoEActivation.SWIGLUOAI])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_prepare_gemm1_lora_delta_layout(activation, w13_num_slices: int):
+    set_random_seed(0)
+    experts, _, _ = _make_experts(False, activation)
+    ids = _make_inputs()[1]
+    gate = torch.randn(T, TOPK, N, device="cuda").to(torch.bfloat16)
+    up = torch.randn(T, TOPK, N, device="cuda").to(torch.bfloat16)
+    if w13_num_slices == 2:
+        # What apply_w13_lora(swap_w13_slices=True) writes for per-expert LoRA.
+        pair, halves = (up, gate), (up, gate)
+    else:
+        # A fused (3D) adapter follows the checkpoint w13 row order.
+        pair, halves = (gate, up), (gate, up)
+    if activation == MoEActivation.SWIGLUOAI:
+        delta = torch.stack(pair, dim=-1).flatten(-2)
+    else:
+        delta = torch.cat(halves, dim=-1)
+

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""The DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 VL wrappers stream the language model's weights to it
+as one contiguous group."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+from torch import nn
+
+from vllm.model_executor.models.utils import WeightsMapper
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_cuda(), reason="CUDA implementations"
+)
+
+
+class _FakeFinalizingLanguageModel(nn.Module):
+    finalizes_weights_during_load = True
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        self.tensor_a = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(1))
+        self.tensor_c = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(1))
+        self.load_calls = 0
+        self.finalized_values: list[tuple[float, float]] = []
+
+    def load_weights(self, weights) -> set[str]:
+        self.load_calls += 1
+        loaded = set()
+        for name, value in weights:
+            getattr(self, name).data.copy_(value)
+            loaded.add(name)
+        self.finalized_values.append((self.tensor_a.item(), self.tensor_c.item()))
+        return loaded
+
+
+def _v4_wrapper():
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v4.common.vl_model import (
+        DeepseekV4ForConditionalGeneration,
+    )
+
+    return DeepseekV4ForConditionalGeneration
+
+
+def _v41_wrapper():
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.nvidia.vl_model import DeepseekV41ForCausalLM
+
+    return DeepseekV41ForCausalLM
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("wrapper", [_v4_wrapper, _v41_wrapper], ids=["v4", "v41"])
+def test_load_weights_streams_language_model_group(wrapper) -> None:
+    model = object.__new__(wrapper())
+    nn.Module.__init__(model)
+    model.language_model = _FakeFinalizingLanguageModel()
+    model.vision = nn.Module()
+    model.vision.tensor_b = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(1))
+    model.hf_to_vllm_mapper = WeightsMapper()
+
+    def interleaved_weights():
+        yield "language_model.tensor_a", torch.tensor([1.0])
+        # Loaded before the stream is drained, not after.
+        assert model.language_model.tensor_a.item() == 1.0
+        # Splits the language model's weights unless the wrapper regroups them.
+        yield "vision.tensor_b", torch.tensor([2.0])
+        yield "language_model.tensor_c", torch.tensor([3.0])
+
+    loaded = model.load_weights(interleaved_weights())
+
+    assert loaded == {
+        "language_model.tensor_a",
+        "vision.tensor_b",
+        "language_model.tensor_c",
+    }
+    assert model.language_model.load_calls == 1
+    assert model.language_model.finalized_values == [(1.0, 3.0)]
+    assert model.vision.tensor_b.item() == 2.0

+def stream_language_model_first(
+    weights: Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]],
+) -> Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]:
+    """Yield ``language_model.*`` weights as they arrive, then the rest.
+
+    Keeps the language model's weights in one contiguous group without
+    materializing the stream. Deferred weights are cloned so they do not keep
+    the loader's per-shard storage alive until the end of the load.
+    """
+    rest = []
+    for name, tensor in weights:
+        if name.startswith("language_model."):
+            yield name, tensor
+        else:
+            rest.append((name, tensor.clone()))
+    yield from rest

+# vLLM model recipes
+
+This directory holds the deployment recipes for models served by vLLM, one
+YAML per model at `models/<hf_org>/<hf_repo>.yaml`. The path mirrors the
+Hugging Face ID, so `models/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B.yaml` renders at
+[recipes.vllm.ai/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B](https://recipes.vllm.ai/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B).
+
+The site, the command builder, and the JSON API are built by
+[vllm-project/recipes](https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes). That
+repository owns the schema and the shared vocabulary (hardware profiles,
+serving strategies, KV-offload deployments) and pins this directory to a
+commit. Omni (image, video, audio) recipes stay in vllm-project/recipes for
+now (moving to vllm-omni), and Ascend NPU content is inline in these recipes
+(moving to vllm-ascend overlays).
+
+## Editing a recipe
+
+Start a new recipe from
+[`templates/recipe.yaml`](https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/blob/main/templates/recipe.yaml).
+Fields are defined in
+[SCHEMA.md](https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/blob/main/SCHEMA.md) and
+checked against [`recipe.schema.json`](https://recipes.vllm.ai/recipe.schema.json)
+on every build; an unknown or misspelled key is an error. For completion and
+inline errors in YAML-aware editors, start the file with
+`# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://recipes.vllm.ai/recipe.schema.json`.
+
+Follow the recipes repository's
+[add-recipe skill](https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/blob/main/.agents/skills/add-recipe/SKILL.md)
+for the schema and the validation steps. To validate a change exactly as this
+repository's `Recipes` PR check does, run from a checkout of
+`vllm-project/recipes`:
+
+```bash
+node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir ~/vllm/recipes
+```
+
+To preview the site with your changes, add a gitignored `sources.local.yaml`
+to that checkout with `overrides: { vllm: ~/vllm/recipes }` and run `pnpm dev`.
+This works once vllm-project/recipes reads this directory as its `vllm`
+source (vllm-project/recipes#1095).

+  slug: "seed-oss-36b"
+  provider: "Seed (ByteDance)"
+  description: "ByteDance Seed-OSS 36B dense model with unique 'thinking budget' control and 512K context support"

+
+guide: |
+  ## Overview
+
+  Seed-OSS-36B is a dense language model from ByteDance Seed with a unique **thinking
+  budget** feature for controlled reasoning, and up to 512K context. Users can choose
+  tensor-parallel (low latency) or data-parallel (high throughput).
+
+  ## Prerequisites
+
+  - Hardware: 8x GPU recommended (TP=8); also runs on consumer hardware like RTX 3090
+  - vLLM >= 0.11.0 (support may require main branch)
+  - Latest transformers for compatibility
+
+  ### Install vLLM (NVIDIA)
+
+  ```bash
+  uv venv
+  source .venv/bin/activate
+  uv pip install -U vllm --torch-backend auto
+  uv pip install git+https://github.com/huggingface/transformers.git@56d68c6706ee052b445e1e476056ed92ac5eb383
+  ```
+
+  ### Install vLLM (AMD ROCm)
+
+  ```bash
+  uv pip install vllm --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/rocm/
+  ```
+
+  ## Launch commands
+
+  NVIDIA:
+
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve ByteDance-Seed/Seed-OSS-36B-Instruct \
+    --host localhost --port 8000 \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
+    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
+    --tool-call-parser seed_oss
+  ```
+
+  AMD:
+
+  ```bash
+  export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
+  vllm serve ByteDance-Seed/Seed-OSS-36B-Instruct \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
+    --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser seed_oss \
+    --trust-remote-code
+  ```
+
+  Tuning:
+  - `--max-model-len=65536` works well; max is 512K.
+  - `--max-num-batched-tokens=32768` for prompt-heavy; reduce to 8K–16K for latency.
+  - `--gpu-memory-utilization=0.95` to maximize KV cache.
+
+  ## Thinking Budget
+
+  Control the model's chain-of-thought length via `chat_template_kwargs`. Recommended
+  values are multiples of 512 (512, 1K, 2K, 4K, 8K, 16K). Use `0` for direct answers.
+
+  ```python
+  from openai import OpenAI
+
+  client = OpenAI(api_key="EMPTY", base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1")
+  model = client.models.list().data[0].id
+
+  response = client.chat.completions.create(
+      model=model,
+      messages=[
+          {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant"},
+          {"role": "user", "content": "Janet's ducks lay 16 eggs per day..."},
+      ],
+      extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"thinking_budget": 512}},
+  )
+  print(response.choices[0].message.content)
+  ```
+
+  curl:
+
+  ```bash
+  curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
+    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
+    -d '{
+      "model": "ByteDance-Seed/Seed-OSS-36B-Instruct",
+      "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Explain quantum computing"}],
+      "chat_template_kwargs": {"thinking_budget": 512}
+    }'
+  ```
+
+  The model emits `<seed:think>` blocks with `<seed:cot_budget_reflect>` markers that
+  report token usage against the budget.
+
+  ## Benchmarking
+
+  ```bash
+  vllm bench serve \
+    --backend vllm --model ByteDance-Seed/Seed-OSS-36B-Instruct \
+    --endpoint /v1/completions --host localhost --port 8000 \
+    --dataset-name random --random-input 800 --random-output 100 \
+    --request-rate 2 --num-prompt 100
+  ```
+
+  ## References
+
+  - [Seed-OSS-36B-Instruct on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/ByteDance-Seed/Seed-OSS-36B-Instruct)

+guide: |
+  ## Overview
+
+  [DiffusionGemma 26B-A4B](https://huggingface.co/google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it) is a block-diffusion language model built on Gemma 4's MoE backbone. Instead of generating tokens one at a time (autoregressive), it generates blocks of 256 tokens simultaneously via iterative denoising over a fixed canvas — trading higher time-to-first-token for significantly higher per-request generation throughput.
+
+  ### Key Architecture Features
+  - **Block Diffusion**: Generates tokens in 256-token canvas blocks via iterative denoising (up to 48 steps per block).
+  - **MoE Backbone**: Same Gemma 4 architecture — 128 fine-grained experts with top-8 routing, 26B total / 4B active parameters.
+  - **Entropy-Bound Sampling**: Uses an entropy-based sampler (`diffusion_sampler: entropy_bound`, `entropy_bound: 0.1`) for the denoising process.
+  - **Multimodal**: Supports text + images via the Gemma 4 vision encoder.
+  - **Thinking Mode**: Supports structured reasoning via `<|channel>thought\n...<channel|>` delimiters.
+  - **Function Calling**: Supports Gemma 4's tool-call protocol (works best in thinking mode).
+
+  ### Important Deployment Notes
+
+  DiffusionGemma requires several specific flags that differ from standard Gemma 4:
+
+  | Flag | Why |
+  |------|-----|
+  | `--max-num-seqs 4` | The diffusion state buffers (`self_conditioning_probs`) pre-allocate `max_seqs × canvas_length × vocab_size` tensors. With Gemma's 262K vocab and canvas_length=256, higher values cause OOM. |
+  | `--generation-config vllm` | The checkpoint's `generation_config.json` sets `max_tokens: 256`, which would override per-request limits. This flag ignores it. |
+  | `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85` | Leaves headroom for activation memory during denoising. |
+  | `--hf-overrides '{"diffusion_sampler":"entropy_bound","diffusion_entropy_bound":0.1}'` | Configures the entropy-bound denoising sampler. |
+  | `--diffusion-config '{"canvas_length": 256}'` | Sets the canvas block size for generation. |
+
+  ## Prerequisites
+
+  DiffusionGemma requires a vLLM build with diffusion model support, available in the
+  Gemma docker image:
+
+  ```bash
+  docker pull vllm/vllm-openai:gemma
+  ```
+
+  ## Deployment
+
+  ### Single GPU (H100/H200, BF16)
+
+  ```bash
+  docker run -itd --name diffusiongemma \
+      --ipc=host --network host --gpus all \
+      -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \
+      vllm/vllm-openai:gemma \
+          --model google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it \
+          --max-model-len 262144 \
+          --max-num-seqs 4 \
+          --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
+          --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
+  ```
+
+  ### Intel Xeon 6 (CPU, BF16)
+
+  DiffusionGemma runs on Intel Xeon 6 CPUs using vLLM's CPU backend with AMX BF16 acceleration.
+  The generated example uses TP=1. Adjust `--tensor-parallel-size` based on the
+  detected NUMA topology and deployment requirements.
+
+  ```bash
+  docker run \
+    --privileged --ipc=host -p 8000:8000 \
+    -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \
+    vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:latest-x86_64 google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it \
+    --max-num-seqs 4 \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
+    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
+    --tool-call-parser gemma4 \
+    --chat-template examples/tool_chat_template_gemma4.jinja \
+    --reasoning-parser gemma4
+  ```
+
+
+  ### Intel XPU (B60 / B70, BF16)
+
+  Validated on 4x Intel Arc Pro B60 / B70 (B60 24 GB, B70 32 GB per card)
+  with the official vLLM XPU image `vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:latest`. `--enforce-eager`
+  and `--attention-backend TRITON_ATTN` are required on this backend. Select Arc Pro
+  B60/B70 in the hardware picker above for the exact command.
+
+  ### Full-Featured Server (text + image + thinking + tools)
+
+  ```bash
+  docker run -itd --name diffusiongemma \
+      --ipc=host --network host --gpus all \
+      -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \
+      vllm/vllm-openai:gemma \
+          --model google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it \
+          --max-model-len 262144 \
+          --max-num-seqs 4 \
+          --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
+          --mm-processor-kwargs '{"max_soft_tokens": 1120}' \
+          --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 7}' \
+          --enable-auto-tool-choice \
+          --tool-call-parser gemma4 \
+          --reasoning-parser gemma4 \
+          --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
+  ```
+
+  ### Jev-Style Structured Decisions (Nightly)
+
+  vLLM's structured-read support for DiffusionGemma can answer yes/no, multiple-choice,
+  and scored questions with a confidence value. The example server seeds a canvas with
+  the response template, leaves only the answer slots noisy, and reads a probability
+  distribution from every slot after one denoising step. It exposes the Jev-compatible
+  `/v1/systemone` endpoint; this is an example server rather than a standard vLLM endpoint.
+
+  Use the pinned nightly image that contains the merged structured-read support:
+
+  ```bash
+  docker run -d --name dgemma \
+      --gpus '"device=0"' \
+      --ipc=host \
+      -p 8000:8000 \
+      -p 8011:8011 \
+      -v "$HOME/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface" \
+      vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-e9757321527ca1ecd514c07c1418dd2c53da3d19 \
+      google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it \
+      --served-model-name dgemma \
+      --diffusion-config '{"canvas_length":64}' \
+      --max-logprobs 32 \
+      --enable-prefix-caching
+  ```
+
+  Wait for the vLLM server to become healthy, then start the example server in the same
+  container:
+
+  ```bash
+  until curl -fsS localhost:8000/health >/dev/null; do sleep 2; done
+
+  docker exec -d dgemma \
+      python /vllm-workspace/examples/features/structured_diffusion/structured_server.py \
+      --upstream http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
+      --tokenizer google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it \
+      --canvas 64
+  ```
+
+  After the example server becomes healthy, send a Jev-style decision request:
+
+  ```bash
+  until curl -fsS localhost:8011/health >/dev/null; do sleep 2; done
+
+  curl -sS localhost:8011/v1/systemone \
+      -H 'content-type: application/json' \
+      -d '{
+        "model": "jev-latest",
+        "state": {"ticket": "Everything is down, demo at noon."},
+        "questions": {
+          "urgent": {
+            "type": "noul",
+            "instructions": "Needs a reply within the hour?"
+          }
+        }
+      }'
+  ```
+
+  ## Client Usage
+
+  ### Text Generation
+
+  ```python
+  from openai import OpenAI
+
+  client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1", api_key="EMPTY")
+  response = client.chat.completions.create(
+      model="google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it",
+      messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Write a poem about the ocean."}],
+      max_tokens=512,
+      temperature=0.7,
+  )
+  print(response.choices[0].message.content)
+  ```
+
+  ### Offline Inference
+
+  ```python
+  from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
+  from transformers import AutoTokenizer
+
+  model_path = "google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it"
+  tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_path)
+
+  llm = LLM(
+      model=model_path,
+      max_num_seqs=4,
+      gpu_memory_utilization=0.85,
+      hf_overrides={
+          "diffusion_sampler": "entropy_bound",
+          "diffusion_entropy_bound": 0.1,
+      },
+      diffusion_config={"canvas_length": 256},
+  )
+
+  messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "Explain quantum computing in simple terms."}]
+  prompt = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True)
+  outputs = llm.generate(prompt, SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=1024))
+
+  print(outputs[0].outputs[0].text)
+  ```
+
+  ### Thinking Mode
+
+  Launch the server with `--reasoning-parser gemma4`, then enable per-request:
+
+  ```python
+  response = client.chat.completions.create(
+      model="google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it",
+      messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "What is the derivative of x^3 * ln(x)?"}],
+      max_tokens=32768,
+      extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": True}},
+  )
+  ```
+
+  ## Performance Characteristics
+
+  Compared to the autoregressive Gemma 4 26B-A4B baseline (single H100, concurrency=1, SPEED-Bench):
+
+  | Metric | Gemma 4 26B-A4B (baseline) | DiffusionGemma 26B-A4B |
+  |--------|---------------------------|------------------------|
+  | Output TPS | 199 tok/s | 375 tok/s (**1.9×**) |
+  | E2E Request Time (mean) | 2.87s | 0.88s (**3.3× faster**) |
+  | TTFT (mean) | 53ms | 489ms (higher due to canvas denoising setup) |
+  | Per-request Gen TPS (mean) | 205 tok/s | 1,282 tok/s (**6.2×**) |
+
+  The diffusion model trades higher time-to-first-token for significantly higher generation throughput. It generates fewer total tokens per prompt on average (shorter outputs) but completes requests much faster.
+
+  ## Known Limitations
+
+  - **TTFT**: ~10× higher than autoregressive baseline — the model must denoise an entire canvas block before emitting the first token.
+  - **`--max-num-seqs`**: Must be kept low (≤4) due to the large diffusion state tensors. Higher values cause CUDA OOM.
+  - **Audio**: Not supported — the diffusion checkpoints do not include an audio encoder.
+  - **Function Calling**: Works best in thinking mode. Non-thinking mode may answer directly instead of emitting tool calls.
+
+  ## References
+
+  - [Model card](https://huggingface.co/google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it)
+  - [vLLM structured-read support for DiffusionGemma](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57250)
+  - [djev-run Cloud Run deployment](https://github.com/taeold/djev-run)
+  - [Gemma 4 26B-A4B (autoregressive baseline)](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it)
+  - [Gemma docs](https://ai.google.dev/gemma/docs)

+guide: |
+  ## Overview
+
+  [Gemma 4](https://ai.google.dev/gemma/docs) is Google's most capable open model family, featuring a unified multimodal architecture that natively processes text, images, and audio. The **12B Unified** model is *encoder-free*: instead of dedicated vision/audio encoders, it projects raw image patches and audio waveforms directly into the decoder's embedding space through lightweight linear layers, so every modality flows into a single decoder-only transformer. Gemma 4 models support structured thinking/reasoning, function calling with a custom tool-use protocol, and dynamic vision resolution — all available through vLLM's OpenAI-compatible API.
+
+  ### Key Features
+  - **Encoder-free multimodality**: Text, image, and audio inputs handled by a single decoder-only transformer — no separate encoders to load, reducing multimodal latency.
+  - **Dual Attention**: Alternating sliding-window (local, 1024 tokens) and global attention; the final layer is always global, with unified Keys/Values and Proportional RoPE on global layers for long-context efficiency.
+  - **Thinking Mode**: Structured reasoning via `<|channel>thought\n...<channel|>` delimiters.
+  - **Function Calling**: Custom tool-call protocol with dedicated special tokens.
+  - **Native System Prompt Support**: First-class `system` role.
+
+  ### Supported Variants
+
+  Dense:
+  - `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` (effective 2B)
+  - `google/gemma-4-E4B-it` (effective 4B)
+  - `google/gemma-4-12B-it` (11.95B, encoder-free)
+  - `google/gemma-4-31B-it` (31B)
+
+  MoE:
+  - `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` (26B total / 4B active)
+
+  > **Context length**: this recipe pins `context_length` to the value in `config.json` (`max_position_embeddings = 131072`, i.e. 128K). The Gemma 4 model card markets the 12B at up to 256K — raise `--max-model-len` only if your vLLM build accepts it.
+
+  TPU support is provided through [vLLM TPU](https://github.com/vllm-project/tpu-inference) with recipes for [Trillium](https://github.com/AI-Hypercomputer/tpu-recipes/tree/main/inference/trillium/vLLM/Gemma4) and [Ironwood](https://github.com/AI-Hypercomputer/tpu-recipes/blob/main/inference/ironwood/vLLM/Gemma4/).
+
+  > **Nightly required**: support for the encoder-free 12B Unified model landed in [vllm-project/vllm#44429](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44429) and has not yet shipped in a stable release. Use the pinned Docker image (recommended) or a nightly pip wheel.
+
+  ## Prerequisites
+
+  ### Docker (recommended)
+  ```bash
+  docker pull vllm/vllm-openai:gemma4-unified            # NVIDIA (CUDA 13; append -cu129 for CUDA 12.9 hosts)
+  docker pull vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:latest                # Intel XPU (B60 / B70)
+  ```
+  TPU images are published separately by [vllm-project/tpu-inference](https://github.com/vllm-project/tpu-inference); see the Trillium / Ironwood tpu-recipes below for the pinned tag.
+
+  ### pip (nightly, NVIDIA CUDA)
+  ```bash

+
+  ## Deployment Configurations
+
+  ### Quick Start (Single GPU, BF16)
+  The 12B fits comfortably on a single 40 GB+ GPU.

+  ### Docker (Cloud TPU — Trillium / Ironwood)
+  TPU uses the separate `vllm/vllm-tpu` image (no pip wheel). Pull the tag specified by the upstream [Trillium](https://github.com/AI-Hypercomputer/tpu-recipes/tree/main/inference/trillium/vLLM/Gemma4) or [Ironwood](https://github.com/AI-Hypercomputer/tpu-recipes/blob/main/inference/ironwood/vLLM/Gemma4/) recipe, then run:
+  ```bash
+  docker run -itd --name gemma4-tpu \
+    --privileged --network host --shm-size 16G \
+    -v /dev/shm:/dev/shm -e HF_TOKEN=$HF_TOKEN \
+    vllm/vllm-tpu:latest \
+      --model google/gemma-4-12B-it \
+      --max-model-len 16384 \
+      --disable_chunked_mm_input \
+      --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
+  ```
+
+  ## Client Usage
+
+  ### Text Generation
+  ```python
+  from openai import OpenAI
+  client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1", api_key="EMPTY")
+  response = client.chat.completions.create(
+      model="google/gemma-4-12B-it",
+      messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Write a poem about the ocean."}],
+      max_tokens=512, temperature=0.7,
+  )
+  print(response.choices[0].message.content)
+  ```
+
+  ### Image Understanding
+  ```python
+  response = client.chat.completions.create(
+      model="google/gemma-4-12B-it",
+      messages=[{"role": "user", "content": [
+          {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3a/Cat03.jpg/1200px-Cat03.jpg"}},
+          {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this image in detail."},
+      ]}],
+      max_tokens=1024,
+  )
+  ```
+
+  ### Audio
+  Requires `uv pip install "vllm[audio]"`.
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve google/gemma-4-12B-it \
+    --max-model-len 8192 \
+    --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 4, "audio": 1}'
+  ```
+
+  ### Thinking Mode
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve google/gemma-4-12B-it \
+    --max-model-len 16384 \
+    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
+    --reasoning-parser gemma4 \
+    --tool-call-parser gemma4 \
+    --chat-template examples/tool_chat_template_gemma4.jinja
+  ```
+  Enable thinking per-request via `extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": True}}`, or default-on with `--default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": true}'`.
+
+  ### Structured Outputs
+  vLLM guided decoding constrains output to a JSON schema. Include semantic instructions in the system prompt — the model does not see schema descriptions.
+
+  ## Configuration Tips
+
+  - Set `--max-model-len` to match your workload.
+  - `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.90–0.95` maximizes KV cache.
+  - Image-only workloads: pass `--limit-mm-per-prompt.audio 0`.
+  - Text-only workloads: pass `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 0, "audio": 0}'` to skip MM profiling.
+  - `--async-scheduling` improves throughput.
+  - FP8 KV cache (`--kv-cache-dtype fp8`) saves ~50% KV memory.
+
+  ## Speculative Decoding (MTP)
+
+  Enable the **Spec Decoding** feature toggle (above) or add `--speculative-config` manually to use MTP drafting with the [assistant model](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-12B-it-assistant). Recommended `num_speculative_tokens`: 4–8 for this model.
+
+  > **Note:** MTP speculative decoding for Gemma 4 requires the nightly build — the pinned `vllm/vllm-openai:gemma4-unified` image or a nightly pip wheel. The standard `:latest` stable tag does not include this feature.
+
+  ## References
+
+  - [Model card](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-12B-it)
+  - [vLLM support PR (#44429)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44429)
+  - [Assistant (MTP draft) model](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-12B-it-assistant)
+  - [Gemma docs](https://ai.google.dev/gemma/docs)
+  - [vLLM Gemma 4 tool-call template](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/examples/tool_chat_template_gemma4.jinja)
+  - [TPU recipes: Trillium](https://github.com/AI-Hypercomputer/tpu-recipes/tree/main/inference/trillium/vLLM/Gemma4)
+  - [TPU recipes: Ironwood](https://github.com/AI-Hypercomputer/tpu-recipes/blob/main/inference/ironwood/vLLM/Gemma4/)

+guide: |
+  ## Overview
+
+  [Gemma 4 26B-A4B](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it) is the Mixture-of-Experts member of Google's Gemma 4 family — 26B total parameters with only 4B active per token via 128 fine-grained experts and top-8 routing. It supports text + images natively, structured thinking, function calling, and dynamic vision resolution.
+
+  Intel Xeon 6 CPU support remains verified. Benchmark-specific TP/DP, CPU binding,
+  sequence limits, and repro-only timeouts remain deployment choices.
+
+  ### Key Features
+  - **MoE**: 128 fine-grained experts with top-8 routing and custom GELU-activated FFN.
+  - **Multimodal**: Text + images natively (video via custom frame-extraction pipeline). Audio is only supported on the smaller E2B/E4B variants.
+  - **Dual Attention**: Alternating sliding-window (local) and global attention with different head dimensions.
+  - **Thinking Mode**: Structured reasoning via `<|channel>thought\n...<channel|>` delimiters.
+  - **Function Calling**: Custom tool-call protocol with dedicated special tokens.
+  - **Dynamic Vision Resolution**: Per-request configurable vision token budget (70, 140, 280, 560, 1120 tokens).
+
+  TPU support is provided through [vLLM TPU](https://github.com/vllm-project/tpu-inference) with recipes for [Trillium](https://github.com/AI-Hypercomputer/tpu-recipes/tree/main/inference/trillium/vLLM/Gemma4) and [Ironwood](https://github.com/AI-Hypercomputer/tpu-recipes/blob/main/inference/ironwood/vLLM/Gemma4/).
+
+  ## Prerequisites
+
+  - Hardware: Intel Xeon 6/Xeon 5 CPUs
+  - vLLM >= 0.25.0
+
+  ### pip (NVIDIA CUDA)
+  ```bash
+  uv venv
+  source .venv/bin/activate
+  uv pip install -U vllm --pre \
+    --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/nightly/cu129 \
+    --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu129 \
+    --index-strategy unsafe-best-match
+  ```
+
+  ### pip (AMD ROCm: MI300X, MI325X, MI350X, MI355X)
+  Requires Python 3.12, ROCm 7.2.1, glibc >= 2.35 (Ubuntu 22.04+).
+  ```bash
+  uv venv --python 3.12
+  source .venv/bin/activate
+  uv pip install vllm --pre \
+    --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/rocm/nightly/rocm721 --upgrade
+  ```
+
+  ### pip (Intel Xeon 6 CPUs)
+  For Intel and AMD x86 CPUs, follow the [CPU pre-built wheels](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/getting_started/installation/cpu/#pre-built-wheels) installation instructions.
+
+  ### Docker
+  ```bash
+  docker pull vllm/vllm-openai:gemma4-0505-cu129  # NVIDIA Hopper (H100/H200, CUDA 12.9)
+  docker pull vllm/vllm-openai:gemma4-0505-cu130  # NVIDIA Blackwell (B200/B300, CUDA 13.0)
+  docker pull vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:latest   # AMD
+  docker pull vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:latest-x86_64 # For Intel Xeon 6
+  docker pull vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:latest # Intel XPU (B60 / B70)
+  ```
+  TPU images are published separately by [vllm-project/tpu-inference](https://github.com/vllm-project/tpu-inference); see the Trillium / Ironwood tpu-recipes below for the pinned tag.
+
+  ## Deployment Configurations
+
+  ### 26B MoE on 1x A100/H100 (BF16)
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it \
+    --max-model-len 32768 \
+    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90
+  ```
+
+  ### Full-Featured Server Launch
+  Enables text, image, thinking, and tool calling:
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it \
+    --max-model-len 16384 \
+    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
+    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
+    --reasoning-parser gemma4 \
+    --tool-call-parser gemma4 \
+    --chat-template examples/tool_chat_template_gemma4.jinja \
+    --limit-mm-per-prompt.image 4 \
+    --async-scheduling \
+    --host 0.0.0.0 \
+    --port 8000
+  ```
+
+  ### Docker (NVIDIA)
+  ```bash
+  docker run -itd --name gemma4-moe \
+    --ipc=host --network host --shm-size 16G --gpus all \
+    -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \
+    vllm/vllm-openai:gemma4-0505-cu129 \
+      --model google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it \
+      --max-model-len 32768 \
+      --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
+      --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
+  ```
+  Swap `vllm/vllm-openai:gemma4-0505-cu129` for `vllm/vllm-openai:gemma4-0505-cu130` on Blackwell (B200/B300).
+
+  ### Docker (AMD MI300X/MI325X/MI350X/MI355X)
+  ```bash
+  docker run -itd --name gemma4-rocm \
+    --ipc=host --network=host --privileged \
+    --cap-add=CAP_SYS_ADMIN --device=/dev/kfd --device=/dev/dri \
+    --group-add=video --cap-add=SYS_PTRACE \
+    --security-opt=seccomp=unconfined --shm-size 16G \
+    -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \
+    vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:latest \
+      --model google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it \
+      --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
+  ```
+
+  ### Docker (Cloud TPU — Trillium / Ironwood)
+  TPU uses the separate `vllm/vllm-tpu` image (no pip wheel). Pull the tag specified by the upstream [Trillium](https://github.com/AI-Hypercomputer/tpu-recipes/tree/main/inference/trillium/vLLM/Gemma4) or [Ironwood](https://github.com/AI-Hypercomputer/tpu-recipes/blob/main/inference/ironwood/vLLM/Gemma4/) recipe, then run:
+  ```bash
+  docker run -itd --name gemma4-tpu \
+    --privileged --network host --shm-size 16G \
+    -v /dev/shm:/dev/shm -e HF_TOKEN=$HF_TOKEN \
+    vllm/vllm-tpu:latest \
+      --model google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it \
+      --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
+      --max-model-len 16384 \
+      --disable_chunked_mm_input \
+      --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
+  ```
+  Trillium requires a 4-chip slice minimum; Ironwood runs on a single chip.
+
+  ### Intel Xeon 6 Deployment via Docker
+
+  Launch the x86 CPU vLLM Docker container for `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it`:
+
+  ```bash
+  docker run \
+    --privileged --ipc=host -p 8000:8000 \
+    -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \
+    vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:latest-x86_64 google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
+    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
+    --tool-call-parser gemma4 \
+    --chat-template examples/tool_chat_template_gemma4.jinja \
+    --reasoning-parser gemma4
+  ```
+
+  For additional Intel Xeon 6 deployment details, see the Intel Software Catalog entries for [Gemma 4 26B-A4B IT](https://aiswcatalog.intel.com/models/google-gemma-4-26b-a4b-it).
+
+  The following settings are intentionally not prescribed as portable CPU model
+  defaults because they depend on the workload, hardware, or runtime environment:
+
+  - `--max-num-batched-tokens`: scheduler/throughput tuning.
+  - `--max-num-seqs`: concurrency and scheduler-capacity tuning.
+  - `--gpu-memory-utilization`: platform memory-budget tuning.
+  - `--no-enable-prefix-caching`: workload/benchmark cache-policy tuning.
+  - `VLLM_ENGINE_ITERATION_TIMEOUT_S`: operational runtime timeout.
+
+  These settings may still appear in validated hardware-specific overrides. Tune
+  them at deployment time based on platform resources, workload shape, and
+  latency/throughput goals.
+
+  ### Docker (Intel XPU B60 / B70, TP=4, Full-Featured)
+
+  Validated on 4x Intel Arc Pro B60 / B70 with the official vLLM XPU image.
+
+  ```bash
+  docker run --device /dev/dri \
+    -v /dev/dri/by-path:/dev/dri/by-path --shm-size=16g \
+    --privileged --ipc=host -p 8000:8000 \
+    -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \
+    vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:latest \
+    google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it \
+    --enforce-eager \
+    --attention-backend flash_attn \
+    --host 0.0.0.0 \
+    --port 8000 \
+    --trust-remote-code \
+    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
+    --reasoning-parser gemma4 \
+    --tool-call-parser gemma4 \
+    --chat-template examples/tool_chat_template_gemma4.jinja \
+    --limit-mm-per-prompt.image 4 \
+    --async-scheduling \
+    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
+    --no-enable-prefix-caching \
+    --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
+    --max-model-len 5120 \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 4
+  ```
+
+  ## Client Usage
+
+  ### Text Generation
+  ```python
+  from openai import OpenAI
+  client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1", api_key="EMPTY")
+  response = client.chat.completions.create(
+      model="google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it",
+      messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Write a poem about the ocean."}],
+      max_tokens=512, temperature=0.7,
+  )
+  print(response.choices[0].message.content)
+  ```
+
+  ### Image Understanding
+  ```python
+  response = client.chat.completions.create(
+      model="google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it",
+      messages=[{"role": "user", "content": [
+          {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3a/Cat03.jpg/1200px-Cat03.jpg"}},
+          {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this image in detail."},
+      ]}],
+      max_tokens=1024,
+  )
+  ```
+
+  ### Thinking Mode
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it \
+    --max-model-len 16384 \
+    --reasoning-parser gemma4 \
+    --tool-call-parser gemma4 \
+    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
+    --chat-template examples/tool_chat_template_gemma4.jinja
+  ```
+  Enable per-request via `extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": True}}`.
+
+  ### Dynamic Vision Resolution
+  Supported values: 70, 140, 280 (default), 560, 1120 tokens/image.
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it \
+    --mm-processor-kwargs '{"max_soft_tokens": 560}'
+  ```
+
+  ## Configuration Tips
+
+  - Set `--max-model-len` to match your workload.
+  - `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.90-0.95` maximizes KV cache.
+  - Text-only workloads: `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 0, "audio": 0}'`.
+  - `--async-scheduling` improves throughput.
+  - FP8 KV cache (`--kv-cache-dtype fp8`) saves ~50% KV memory.
+  - For MoE, TEP (tensor-expert parallelism) and DEP (data-expert parallelism) strategies scale better than pure TP at large node counts.
+
+  ## Quantized Variants
+
+  Three pre-quantized checkpoints are available:
+
+  - [`RedHatAI/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-FP8-dynamic`](https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-FP8-dynamic) — FP8 (E4M3) weights with dynamic per-token activation quantization; runs on Hopper and Blackwell.
+  - [`RedHatAI/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-NVFP4`](https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-NVFP4) — NVFP4 (4-bit) weights; requires Blackwell (B200/B300).
+  - [`nvidia/Gemma-4-26B-A4B-NVFP4`](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Gemma-4-26B-A4B-NVFP4) — NVIDIA ModelOpt NVFP4 (4-bit) weights; this is the checkpoint validated on the single-GPU Blackwell desktops below.
+
+  Pick them from the **Variant** dropdown above, or pass the repo id directly to `vllm serve`.
+
+  ### NVFP4 on the Blackwell desktops
+
+  [`nvidia/Gemma-4-26B-A4B-NVFP4`](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Gemma-4-26B-A4B-NVFP4)
+  has been run end to end on DGX Spark (GB10), DGX Station (GB300) and RTX PRO
+  6000, in each case on one GPU at TP1 with MTP drafting against
+  [`google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-assistant`](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-assistant).
+
+  Select the **NVIDIA NVFP4** variant, enable **Spec Decoding**, and switch the
+  hardware pill — memory utilization, batch size, prefill scheduling and the
+  drafter's MoE backend all differ per box and are encoded per hardware, so the
+  generated command is the tested one. Highlights:
+
+  - **DGX Spark (GB10)** — 128 GB shared with the CPU, so `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.8`
+    and an 8-way batch. Serve from `eugr/spark-vllm:nightly-20260704`: vLLM 0.24
+    and the generic nightly both fail on this checkpoint, so the pip tab is
+    hidden on this hardware.
+  - **DGX Station (GB300)** — 252 GB on one GPU, so `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.92`
+    with chunked prefill and a 64-way batch.
+  - **RTX PRO 6000** — 96 GB, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.92` and an 8-way batch.
+
+  All three run the full 262,144-token context, above the 131,072 in
+  `config.json`, and pass `"moe_backend":"triton"` in `--speculative-config`
+  because the drafter's default fused MoE path is not built in these images.
+
+  The GB300 and RTX PRO 6000 runs used an internal NVIDIA nightly vLLM build.
+  As noted under Speculative Decoding below, Gemma 4 MTP has not landed in a
+  stable release, so the default `vllm/vllm-openai:latest` tag will not serve
+  these commands with Spec Decoding enabled — use a nightly wheel or a nightly
+  image on those two boxes.
+
+  ## Throughput vs Latency
+
+  | Goal | TP | `--max-num-seqs` | Notes |
+  |------|----|------------------|-------|
+  | Max throughput | 1-2 | 256-512 | Best tok/s per GPU |
+  | Min latency   | 4-8 | 8-16   | Best TTFT/TPOT |
+  | Balanced      | 2   | 128    | Mixed workloads |
+
+  ## Speculative Decoding (MTP)
+
+  Enable the **Spec Decoding** feature toggle (above) or add `--speculative-config` manually to use MTP drafting with the [assistant model](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-assistant). Recommended `num_speculative_tokens`: 4 for this model. See the [Gemma 4 usage guide](../../Google/Gemma4) for details and benchmarks.

Install via the nightly wheel (`uv pip install -U vllm --pre --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/nightly/cu129 …`) or use the `vllm/vllm-openai:gemma4-0505-cu129` / `vllm/vllm-openai:gemma4-0505-cu130` images above; the standard `:latest` stable tag does not include this feature.

+guide: |
+  ## Overview
+
+  [Gemma 4](https://ai.google.dev/gemma/docs) is Google's most capable open model family, featuring a unified multimodal architecture that natively processes text, images, and audio. Gemma 4 models support structured thinking/reasoning, function calling with a custom tool-use protocol, and dynamic vision resolution — all available through vLLM's OpenAI-compatible API.
+
+  ### Key Features
+  - **Multimodal**: Text + images natively (video via custom frame-extraction pipeline). The smaller E2B and E4B models also support audio.
+  - **MoE variant**: 128 fine-grained experts with top-8 routing and custom GELU-activated FFN (Gemma 4 26B-A4B).
+  - **Dual Attention**: Alternating sliding-window (local) and global attention with different head dimensions.
+  - **Thinking Mode**: Structured reasoning via `<|channel>thought\n...<channel|>` delimiters.
+  - **Function Calling**: Custom tool-call protocol with dedicated special tokens.
+  - **Dynamic Vision Resolution**: Per-request configurable vision token budget (70, 140, 280, 560, 1120 tokens).
+
+  ### Supported Variants
+
+  Dense:
+  - `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` (effective 2B)
+  - `google/gemma-4-E4B-it` (effective 4B)
+  - `google/gemma-4-31B-it` (31B)
+
+  MoE:
+  - `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` (26B total / 4B active)
+
+  TPU support is provided through [vLLM TPU](https://github.com/vllm-project/tpu-inference) with recipes for [Trillium](https://github.com/AI-Hypercomputer/tpu-recipes/tree/main/inference/trillium/vLLM/Gemma4) and [Ironwood](https://github.com/AI-Hypercomputer/tpu-recipes/blob/main/inference/ironwood/vLLM/Gemma4/).
+
+  ## Prerequisites
+
+  ### pip (NVIDIA CUDA)
+  ```bash
+  uv venv
+  source .venv/bin/activate
+  uv pip install -U vllm --pre \
+    --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/nightly/cu129 \
+    --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu129 \
+    --index-strategy unsafe-best-match
+  ```
+
+  ### pip (AMD ROCm: MI300X, MI325X, MI350X, MI355X)
+  Requires Python 3.12, ROCm 7.2.1, glibc >= 2.35 (Ubuntu 22.04+).
+  ```bash
+  uv venv --python 3.12
+  source .venv/bin/activate
+  uv pip install vllm --pre \
+    --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/rocm/nightly/rocm721 --upgrade
+  ```
+
+  ### Docker
+  ```bash
+  docker pull vllm/vllm-openai:gemma4-0505-cu129  # NVIDIA Hopper (H100/H200, CUDA 12.9)
+  docker pull vllm/vllm-openai:gemma4-0505-cu130  # NVIDIA Blackwell (B200/B300, CUDA 13.0)
+  docker pull vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:latest   # AMD
+  docker pull vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:latest # Intel XPU (B60 / B70)
+  ```
+  TPU images are published separately by [vllm-project/tpu-inference](https://github.com/vllm-project/tpu-inference); see the Trillium / Ironwood tpu-recipes below for the pinned tag.
+
+  ## Deployment Configurations
+
+  ### Quick Start (Single GPU)
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve google/gemma-4-E4B-it \
+    --max-model-len <n_of_tokens>   # up to 131072
+  ```
+
+  ### 31B Dense on 2xA100/H100 (TP=2, BF16)
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve google/gemma-4-31B-it \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
+    --max-model-len 32768 \
+    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90
+  ```
+
+  ### 26B MoE on 1xA100/H100 (BF16)
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it \
+    --max-model-len 32768 \
+    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90
+  ```
+
+  ### Full-Featured Server Launch
+  Enables text, image, audio, thinking, and tool calling:
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve google/gemma-4-31B-it \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
+    --max-model-len 16384 \
+    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
+    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
+    --reasoning-parser gemma4 \
+    --tool-call-parser gemma4 \

+
+  ### Docker (NVIDIA)

+  docker run -itd --name gemma4 \
+    --ipc=host --network host --shm-size 16G --gpus all \
+    -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \
