+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Widen the dummy weight init for the MoRIIO dummy-weight P/D test.
+
+The dummy loader fills float weights in +-1e-3, which keeps every activation so
+small that outputs barely depend on the input, so a wrong KV prefix would go
+unnoticed. The P/D test names ``WideDummyWeights`` as each server's
+``--worker-extension-cls``. Workers import it before they load the model, which
+re-registers the ``dummy`` load format in every worker process with a loader
+that fills 16/32-bit float weights in +-``MORIIO_DUMMY_WEIGHT_RANGE``; 8-bit
+weights and scales keep the default init. The format keeps the name ``dummy``
+so every config path that special-cases dummy weights still applies.
+
+The test process itself never imports this module.
+"""
+
+import os
+
+import torch
+from torch import nn
+
+from vllm.config import ModelConfig
+from vllm.model_executor.model_loader import register_model_loader
+from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.dummy_loader import DummyModelLoader
+from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload.layerwise import get_layerwise_info
+from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload.utils import get_layer_tensors
+from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_utils import (
+    initialize_single_dummy_weight,
+)
+
+_RANGE = float(os.environ["MORIIO_DUMMY_WEIGHT_RANGE"])
+
+
+@register_model_loader("dummy")
+class WideDummyModelLoader(DummyModelLoader):
+    def load_weights(self, model: nn.Module, model_config: ModelConfig) -> None:
+        # DummyModelLoader.load_weights with a wider init for 16/32-bit floats.
+        for layer in model.modules():
+            info = get_layerwise_info(layer)
+            if info.can_load():
+                self._process_online_quant_layer(layer, info)
+                continue
+            for name, tensor in get_layer_tensors(layer).items():
+                if name in layer._non_persistent_buffers_set:
+                    continue
+                if tensor.is_floating_point() and torch.finfo(tensor.dtype).bits >= 16:
+                    initialize_single_dummy_weight(
+                        tensor, low=-_RANGE, high=_RANGE, name=name
+                    )
+                else:
+                    initialize_single_dummy_weight(tensor, name=name)
+
+
+class WideDummyWeights:
+    """Worker extension that only exists to import this module in workers."""

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Single-node MoRIIO WRITE P/D checks on dummy weights.
+
+Each case serves a real model architecture with ``--load-format dummy``, widened
+by ``moriio_wide_dummy`` (see ``DUMMY_WEIGHT_RANGE``): the
+config keeps the real hidden size, head geometry, MLA ranks and recurrent-state
+shapes, so the connector registers and transfers exactly the production cache
+layout, but the layer stack is cut to a few layers that still contain every
+cache-group kind and the MoE is cut to a handful of experts. Dummy weights are
+seeded, so the prefill, decode and reference servers hold identical weights.
+Cases marked ``HMA_off`` run every server with
+``--disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager``, so all layers, sliding-window ones
+included, share a single cache group.
+
+Prefill runs on one GPU, decode on another, and MoRI moves the KV over xGMI.
+Either way decode computes the last prompt token itself. For hybrid models
+prefill computes only the first ``n - 1`` tokens and transfers the KV and the
+recurrent state after them. For attention-only models prefill computes and
+transfers all ``n``, and decode's scheduler, seeing the whole prompt cached,
+recomputes the last token. A direct serve splits the same prompt the same way
+when the first ``n - 1`` tokens end on a chunk boundary that both servers share,
+so the prompts are chosen to make that happen: one is a single chunk plus one
+token, the others are a whole number of hybrid cache blocks plus one token
+(prefix caching ends chunks on block boundaries) or, for attention-only models,
+a whole number of chunks plus one token. With the split matched, a correct
+transfer reproduces the direct serve's first-token log-probabilities exactly,
+so the comparison needs no noise allowance. The
+servers compile with Inductor's deterministic mode, since otherwise each one
+benchmarks its own reduction launch configs and separately started servers
+can drift apart by a few bf16 logit steps. Guards:
+
+* decode must report an external prefix-cache hit for every transferred token
+  of every prompt, so the match is not a local recompute;
+* changing the first half of a prompt must move the direct serve's log-probs by
+  at least ``MIN_CONTEXT_EFFECT``, so a wrong prefix would be visible;
+* ``test_corrupted_prefill_state_is_detected`` makes prefill compute its KV with
+  a different norm epsilon (same shapes, different values) and requires every
+  prompt to fail the comparison.
+"""
+
+import atexit
+import contextlib
+import json
+import os
+import random
+import shutil
+import signal
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import time
+from collections.abc import Callable, Iterator
+from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+import pytest
+import requests
+
+from tests.utils import RemoteOpenAIServer
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.utils.network_utils import get_open_port
+
+_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4]
+_PROXY = (
+    _ROOT / "examples/disaggregated/disaggregated_serving/moriio_toy_proxy_server.py"
+)
+
+# Max allowed difference between centered first-token log-probabilities of the
+# P/D and direct outputs, over the direct serve's top-k tokens. The split is
+# matched, so correct transfers produce identical logits; this only absorbs the
+# fp32 rounding of the log-softmax (~1e-7), far below one bf16 logit step.
+TOLERANCE = float(os.getenv("MORIIO_DUMMY_E2E_TOL", "1e-5"))
+# Several bf16 steps of the logits at DUMMY_WEIGHT_RANGE.
+MIN_CONTEXT_EFFECT = 0.05
+# Half-width of the uniform dummy init for 16/32-bit float weights, applied in
+# every server worker by moriio_wide_dummy.py. The loader default (1e-3) shrinks
+# every activation so far that a context change moves the first-token log-probs
+# by ~1e-4; at 0.1 it moves them by >0.1 and a corrupted prefill changes the
+# top-k set entirely.
+DUMMY_WEIGHT_RANGE = 0.1
+_WIDE_DUMMY_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+TOP_K = 20
+MAX_TOKENS = 4
+MAX_MODEL_LEN = 4096
+
+# Prefill token budget of every server. Prompts longer than it are chunked, so
+# the final-chunk save path runs; the short prompt fills exactly one chunk.
+PREFILL_CHUNK = 299
+SHORT_PROMPT_LEN = PREFILL_CHUNK + 1
+# Hybrid blocks per aligned prompt, before the trailing token.
+ALIGNED_BLOCKS = (1, 2)
+# Prefill chunks per long attention-only prompt, before the trailing token.
+ALIGNED_CHUNKS = (2, 4)
+
+
+def _mori_available() -> bool:
+    try:
+        import mori.io  # noqa: F401
+    except ImportError:
+        return False
+    return True
+
+
+pytestmark = [
+    pytest.mark.skipif(
+        not current_platform.is_rocm() or not _mori_available(),
+        reason="MoRIIO P/D needs ROCm and MoRI",
+    ),
+    pytest.mark.skipif(
+        current_platform.is_rocm() and current_platform.device_count() < 2,
+        reason="needs one GPU for prefill and one for decode",
+    ),
+]
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Model architectures
+
+
+def _kimi_linear_overrides(cfg) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    # 3 KDA layers then 1 MLA layer; layer 0 stays dense (first_k_dense_replace).
+    linear = dict(cfg.linear_attn_config)
+    linear["kda_layers"] = [1, 2, 3]
+    linear["full_attn_layers"] = [4]
+    groups = max(1, cfg.num_expert_group)
+    return {
+        "num_hidden_layers": 4,
+        "linear_attn_config": linear,
+        "num_experts": 2 * groups,
+        "num_experts_per_token": 2,
+        "topk_group": min(cfg.topk_group, groups),
+    }
+
+
+def _qwen3_5_moe_overrides(cfg) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    # 3 Gated DeltaNet layers then 1 full-attention layer.
+    return {
+        "text_config": {
+            "num_hidden_layers": 4,
+            "layer_types": ["linear_attention"] * 3 + ["full_attention"],
+            "num_experts": 4,
+            "num_experts_per_tok": 2,
+        }
+    }
+
+
+def _qwen3_dense_overrides(cfg) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    # Attention-only: decode gets the KV for the whole prompt.
+    return {"num_hidden_layers": 4}
+
+
+def _deepseek_v3_overrides(cfg) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    # MLA attention-only: layer 0 dense, layer 1 MoE, no MTP layer.
+    return {
+        "num_hidden_layers": 2,
+        "first_k_dense_replace": 1,
+        "n_routed_experts": 8,
+        "num_experts_per_tok": 2,
+        "n_group": 1,
+        "topk_group": 1,
+        "num_nextn_predict_layers": 0,
+    }
+
+
+def _gemma3_overrides(cfg) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    # Five sliding-window layers then one global layer, as in the real
+    # 5:1 pattern. Without the hybrid KV cache manager vLLM gives the sliding
+    # layers full-attention cache specs, so all six share one group.
+    return {
+        "num_hidden_layers": 6,
+        "layer_types": ["sliding_attention"] * 5 + ["full_attention"],
+    }
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ArchCase:
+    model: str
+    overrides: Callable[[Any], dict[str, Any]]
+    # Norm-epsilon override that perturbs every computed KV/state value
+    # without changing a single shape. Used by the corruption control.
+    corrupt_overrides: dict[str, Any]
+    env: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
+    args: tuple[str, ...] = ()
+    # Has recurrent-state (mamba-style) layers, so prefill stops at n - 1.
+    hybrid: bool = True
+
+
+ARCHS: dict[str, ArchCase] = {
+    "kimi_linear": ArchCase(
+        model="moonshotai/Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct",
+        overrides=_kimi_linear_overrides,
+        corrupt_overrides={"rms_norm_eps": 1.0},
+        env={"VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER": "1"},
+        args=("--trust-remote-code", "--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype", "float32"),
+    ),
+    "qwen3_5_moe": ArchCase(
+        model="Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B",
+        overrides=_qwen3_5_moe_overrides,
+        corrupt_overrides={"text_config": {"rms_norm_eps": 1.0}},
+        # AITER's GDN conv-update kernel rejects the DS conv-state layout that
+        # MoRIIO's recurrent-state transfer requires.
+        env={"VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER": "0"},
+        args=("--language-model-only",),
+    ),
+    "qwen3_dense": ArchCase(
+        model="Qwen/Qwen3-32B",
+        overrides=_qwen3_dense_overrides,
+        corrupt_overrides={"rms_norm_eps": 1.0},
+        env={"VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER": "0"},
+        hybrid=False,
+    ),
+    "deepseek_v3": ArchCase(
+        model="deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3",
+        overrides=_deepseek_v3_overrides,
+        corrupt_overrides={"rms_norm_eps": 1.0},
+        env={"VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER": "1"},
+        hybrid=False,
+    ),
+    # Text-only Gemma 3. The multimodal Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration takes
+    # the inputs_embeds path on KV consumers (enable_mm_embeds is forced on
+    # there) and computes differently from a direct serve without any transfer.
+    "gemma3": ArchCase(
+        model="google/gemma-3-1b-it",
+        overrides=_gemma3_overrides,
+        corrupt_overrides={"rms_norm_eps": 1.0},
+        env={"VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER": "0"},
+        hybrid=False,
+    ),
+}
+
+
+def _arch_overrides(arch: ArchCase) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    from vllm.transformers_utils.config import get_config
+
+    return arch.overrides(get_config(arch.model, trust_remote_code=True))
+
+
+def _merge(base: dict[str, Any], extra: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    merged = dict(base)
+    for key, value in extra.items():
+        if isinstance(value, dict) and isinstance(merged.get(key), dict):
+            merged[key] = _merge(merged[key], value)
+        else:
+            merged[key] = value
+    return merged
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Serving
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Case:
+    arch: str
+    attention_backend: str
+    prefill_graph: str
+    decode_graph: str
+    # Run every server of the case without the hybrid KV cache manager.
+    hma_off: bool = False
+
+    @property
+    def extra_args(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
+        return ("--disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager",) if self.hma_off else ()
+
+    @property
+    def id(self) -> str:
+        return (
+            f"{self.arch}-{self.attention_backend}-"
+            f"P_{self.prefill_graph}-D_{self.decode_graph}"
+            + ("-HMA_off" if self.hma_off else "")
+        )
+
+
+_DEFAULT = "FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"
+CASES = [
+    # Kimi-Linear: KDA + MLA groups.
+    Case("kimi_linear", "ROCM_AITER_MLA", _DEFAULT, _DEFAULT),
+    Case("kimi_linear", "ROCM_AITER_MLA", "NONE", "NONE"),
+    Case("kimi_linear", "ROCM_AITER_MLA", "PIECEWISE", "PIECEWISE"),
+    Case("kimi_linear", "ROCM_AITER_MLA", _DEFAULT, "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"),
+    Case("kimi_linear", "TRITON_MLA", _DEFAULT, _DEFAULT),
+    # Qwen3.5: Gated DeltaNet + full-attention groups.
+    Case("qwen3_5_moe", "TRITON_ATTN", _DEFAULT, _DEFAULT),
+    Case("qwen3_5_moe", "TRITON_ATTN", "NONE", "NONE"),
+    Case("qwen3_5_moe", "TRITON_ATTN", "PIECEWISE", "PIECEWISE"),
+    Case("qwen3_5_moe", "TRITON_ATTN", _DEFAULT, "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"),
+    # ROCM_ATTN keeps a (2, num_blocks, ...) KV layout and opts out of KV
+    # connectors, so the second ROCm attention backend is the unified one.
+    Case("qwen3_5_moe", "ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN", _DEFAULT, _DEFAULT),
+    # Attention-only: prefill transfers the whole prompt.
+    Case("qwen3_dense", "TRITON_ATTN", _DEFAULT, _DEFAULT),
+    Case("qwen3_dense", "ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN", _DEFAULT, _DEFAULT),
+    # Without the hybrid KV cache manager: one cache group per model.
+    Case("qwen3_dense", "TRITON_ATTN", _DEFAULT, _DEFAULT, hma_off=True),
+    Case("deepseek_v3", "ROCM_AITER_MLA", _DEFAULT, _DEFAULT, hma_off=True),
+    Case("gemma3", "TRITON_ATTN", _DEFAULT, _DEFAULT, hma_off=True),
+]
+
+
+def _graph_args(mode: str) -> list[str]:
+    if mode == "NONE":
+        return ["--enforce-eager"]
+    # Inductor otherwise picks reduction launch configs by timing them, so each
+    # separately compiled server may sum in a different order and drift by a
+    # few bf16 logit steps; deterministic mode fixes the choice.
+    config = {
+        "cudagraph_mode": mode,
+        "inductor_compile_config": {"deterministic": True},
+    }
+    return ["--compilation-config", json.dumps(config)]
+
+
+def _visible_devices() -> tuple[str, list[str]]:
+    selectors = ("HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES", "ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES", "CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES")
+    selector = next((k for k in selectors if k in os.environ), selectors[0])
+    visible = os.getenv(selector)
+    devices = (
+        visible.split(",")
+        if visible
+        else [str(i) for i in range(current_platform.device_count())]
+    )
+    return selector, devices
+
+
+def _device_env(selector: str, device: str) -> dict[str, str]:
+    # vLLM mirrors HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES into CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES at import, so
+    # the test process carries both; pin every selector or the server refuses
+    # the mismatch. ROCR narrows the set first, so HIP/CUDA then index into it.
+    env = {selector: device}
+    for key in ("HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES", "CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"):
+        if key != selector:
+            env[key] = "0" if selector == "ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES" else device
+    return env
+
+
+# KV consumers force enable_mm_embeds on, which moves multimodal-capable models
+# (Qwen3.5) from input_ids to inputs_embeds, but the AOT compile-cache key does
+# not cover it, so a consumer can load a producer's graph and crash in
+# profile_run. Keep each role's compile cache apart until
+# vllm-project/vllm#54642 lands (vllm-project/vllm#50891).
+_CACHE_ROOT = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="moriio_dummy_e2e_cache_"))
+atexit.register(shutil.rmtree, _CACHE_ROOT, ignore_errors=True)
+
+
+def _server(
+    arch: ArchCase,
+    overrides: dict[str, Any],
+    backend: str,
+    graph: str,
+    device: str,
+    selector: str,
+    *,
+    port: int | None = None,
+    extra_args: tuple[str, ...] = (),
+    kv_transfer_config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
+) -> RemoteOpenAIServer:
+    port = port or get_open_port()
+    args = [
+        *arch.args,
+        *extra_args,
+        "--port",
+        str(port),
+        "--load-format",
+        "dummy",
+        "--worker-extension-cls",
+        "moriio_wide_dummy.WideDummyWeights",
+        "--hf-overrides",
+        json.dumps(overrides),
+        "--dtype",
+        "bfloat16",
+        "--attention-backend",
+        backend,
+        "--max-model-len",
+        str(MAX_MODEL_LEN),
+        "--max-num-batched-tokens",
+        str(PREFILL_CHUNK),
+        "--max-num-seqs",
+        "16",
+        "--kv-cache-memory-bytes",
+        str(2 * 1024**3),
+        "--gpu-memory-utilization",
+        "0.5",
+        "--enable-prefix-caching",
+        *_graph_args(graph),
+    ]
+    role = "direct"
+    if kv_transfer_config is not None:
+        args += ["--kv-transfer-config", json.dumps(kv_transfer_config)]
+        role = kv_transfer_config["kv_role"]
+    env = {
+        "PATH": str(Path(sys.executable).parent) + os.pathsep + os.environ["PATH"],
+        **_device_env(selector, device),
+        "VLLM_HOST_IP": "127.0.0.1",
+        "VLLM_PORT": str(get_open_port()),
+        "VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD": "spawn",
+        "VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT": "DS",
+        "VLLM_CACHE_ROOT": str(_CACHE_ROOT / role),
+        # Only this directory, so the source tree cannot shadow installed vllm.
+        "PYTHONPATH": os.pathsep.join(
+            filter(None, [str(_WIDE_DUMMY_DIR), os.environ.get("PYTHONPATH")])
+        ),
+        "MORIIO_DUMMY_WEIGHT_RANGE": str(DUMMY_WEIGHT_RANGE),
+        **arch.env,
+    }
+    return RemoteOpenAIServer(
+        arch.model, args, env_dict=env, auto_port=False, max_wait_seconds=900
+    )
+
+
+def _moriio_config(role: str, http_port: int, ping_port: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    return {
+        "kv_connector": "MoRIIOConnector",
+        "kv_role": role,
+        "kv_connector_extra_config": {
+            "backend": "xgmi",
+            "read_mode": False,
+            "host_ip": "127.0.0.1",
+            "proxy_ip": "127.0.0.1",
+            "proxy_ping_port": str(ping_port),
+            "http_port": str(http_port),
+            "handshake_port": str(get_open_port()),
+            "notify_port": str(get_open_port()),
+        },
+    }
+
+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def _proxy(ping_port: int) -> Iterator[str]:
+    # Free ports for both sockets, so cases from parallel shards on one host
+    # do not collide.
+    port = get_open_port()
+    process = subprocess.Popen(
+        [
+            sys.executable,
+            str(_PROXY),
+            "--port",
+            str(port),
+            "--service-discovery-port",
+            str(ping_port),
+        ],
+        start_new_session=True,
+    )
+    try:
+        deadline = time.monotonic() + 60
+        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
+            assert process.poll() is None, "MoRIIO proxy exited during startup"
+            try:
+                requests.get(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/", timeout=1)
+                break
+            except requests.ConnectionError:
+                time.sleep(0.2)
+        else:
+            raise TimeoutError("MoRIIO proxy did not start")
+        yield f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"
+    finally:
+        if process.poll() is None:
+            os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGTERM)
+            try:
+                process.wait(timeout=10)
+            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+                os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
+                process.wait(timeout=10)
+
+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def _pd_pair(
+    arch: ArchCase,
+    prefill_overrides: dict[str, Any],
+    decode_overrides: dict[str, Any],
+    case: Case,
+) -> Iterator[tuple[str, RemoteOpenAIServer]]:
+    selector, devices = _visible_devices()
+    assert len(devices) >= 2, "needs one GPU for prefill and one for decode"
+    prefill_port, decode_port, ping_port = (get_open_port() for _ in range(3))
+    with _proxy(ping_port) as proxy_url, contextlib.ExitStack() as stack:
+        servers: list[RemoteOpenAIServer] = []
+        stack.callback(RemoteOpenAIServer.shutdown_many, servers)
+        with ThreadPoolExecutor(2) as pool:
+            futures = [
+                pool.submit(
+                    _server,
+                    arch,
+                    prefill_overrides,
+                    case.attention_backend,
+                    case.prefill_graph,
+                    devices[0],
+                    selector,
+                    port=prefill_port,
+                    extra_args=case.extra_args,
+                    kv_transfer_config=_moriio_config(
+                        "kv_producer", prefill_port, ping_port
+                    ),
+                ),
+                pool.submit(
+                    _server,
+                    arch,
+                    decode_overrides,
+                    case.attention_backend,
+                    case.decode_graph,
+                    devices[1],
+                    selector,
+                    port=decode_port,
+                    extra_args=case.extra_args,
+                    kv_transfer_config=_moriio_config(
+                        "kv_consumer", decode_port, ping_port
+                    ),
+                ),
+            ]
+            for future in futures:
+                servers.append(future.result())
+        _wait_for_registration(proxy_url, arch.model)
+        yield proxy_url, servers[1]
+
+
+def _wait_for_registration(proxy_url: str, model: str) -> None:
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + 120
+    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
+        # The proxy hands decode max_tokens - 1 (prefill emits the first
+        # token), so the probe needs at least 2 for decode to accept it.
+        try:
+            response = requests.post(
+                f"{proxy_url}/v1/completions",
+                json={"model": model, "prompt": [1000, 1001], "max_tokens": 2},
+                timeout=300,
+            )
+            # The proxy streams the decode body, so a decode-side error can
+            # surface as a truncated response rather than a status code.
+            if response.status_code == 200 and response.json()["choices"]:
+                return
+        except requests.RequestException:
+            pass
+        time.sleep(1)
+    raise TimeoutError("prefill/decode never registered with the MoRIIO proxy")
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Measurement
+
+
+def _metric(server: RemoteOpenAIServer, name: str) -> list[Any]:
+    from prometheus_client.parser import text_string_to_metric_families
+
+    response = requests.get(server.url_for("metrics"), timeout=10)
+    response.raise_for_status()
+    return [
+        sample
+        for family in text_string_to_metric_families(response.text)
+        for sample in family.samples
+        if sample.name == name
+    ]
+
+
+def _block_size(server: RemoteOpenAIServer) -> int:
+    # Hybrid models pad the attention block to the recurrent-state page, so the
+    # effective size is only known once the server has started.
+    sizes = {
+        int(sample.labels["block_size"])
+        for sample in _metric(server, "vllm:cache_config_info")
+    }
+    assert len(sizes) == 1, f"expected one cache block size, got {sizes}"
+    return sizes.pop()
+
+
+def _prompt_lengths(arch: ArchCase, server: RemoteOpenAIServer) -> list[int]:
+    # Hybrid chunks end on cache-block boundaries; attention-only chunks end on
+    # the prefill budget, so the last token is computed on its own either way.
+    if arch.hybrid:
+        unit, counts = _block_size(server), ALIGNED_BLOCKS
+    else:
+        unit, counts = PREFILL_CHUNK, ALIGNED_CHUNKS
+    aligned = [
+        k * unit + 1 for k in counts if k * unit + 1 + MAX_TOKENS <= MAX_MODEL_LEN
+    ]
+    assert aligned, f"alignment unit {unit} leaves no aligned prompt"
+    return [SHORT_PROMPT_LEN, *aligned]
+
+
+def _prompts(lengths: list[int]) -> list[list[int]]:
+    rng = random.Random(0)
+    return [[rng.randrange(1000, 30000) for _ in range(n)] for n in lengths]
+
+
+def _first_step(url: str, model: str, prompt: list[int]) -> dict[str, float]:
+    response = requests.post(
+        f"{url}/v1/completions",
+        json={
+            "model": model,
+            "prompt": prompt,
+            "max_tokens": MAX_TOKENS,
+            "temperature": 0,
+            "logprobs": TOP_K,
+            "return_tokens_as_token_ids": True,
+        },
+        timeout=600,
+    )
+    response.raise_for_status()
+    top = response.json()["choices"][0]["logprobs"]["top_logprobs"]
+    assert top, "server returned no logprobs"
+    return top[0]
+
+
+def _distance(ref: dict[str, float], got: dict[str, float]) -> float:
+    """Max difference of centered log-probs over the shared top-k tokens.
+
+    Centering removes the log-sum-exp offset, leaving the logit differences the
+    KV actually determines.
+    """
+    common = sorted(ref.keys() & got.keys())
+    if len(common) < len(ref) // 2:
+        return float("inf")
+    ref_mean = sum(ref[t] for t in common) / len(common)
+    got_mean = sum(got[t] for t in common) / len(common)
+    return max(abs((ref[t] - ref_mean) - (got[t] - got_mean)) for t in common)
+
+
+def _external_hits(server: RemoteOpenAIServer) -> float:
+    samples = _metric(server, "vllm:external_prefix_cache_hits_total")
+    return sum(sample.value for sample in samples)
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Reference:
+    prompts: list[list[int]]
+    logprobs: list[dict[str, float]]
+    hybrid: bool
+
+    @property
+    def expected_external_hits(self) -> int:
+        # Hybrid prefill stops one token short; attention-only prefill hands
+        # decode the whole prompt.
+        return sum(len(p) - int(self.hybrid) for p in self.prompts)
+
+
+def _reference(arch: ArchCase, overrides: dict[str, Any], case: Case) -> Reference:
+    """Direct serve; also checks that the comparison can see a wrong prefix."""
+    selector, devices = _visible_devices()
+    # Prefill graphs run the chunks and the decode-only last step runs the same
+    # captured graph in every decode mode used here, so the prefill mode
+    # reproduces both halves of the P/D computation.
+    with _server(
+        arch,
+        overrides,
+        case.attention_backend,
+        case.prefill_graph,
+        devices[0],
+        selector,
+        extra_args=case.extra_args,
+    ) as server:
+        url = server.url_root
+        lengths = _prompt_lengths(arch, server)
+        prompts = _prompts(lengths)
+        refs = [_first_step(url, arch.model, p) for p in prompts]
+        # Same tail, different early context: the comparison has to see it.
+        for prompt, ref in zip(prompts, refs):
+            altered = [t + 1 for t in prompt[: len(prompt) // 2]]
+            altered += prompt[len(prompt) // 2 :]
+            moved = _distance(ref, _first_step(url, arch.model, altered))
+            print(f"[sensitivity] len={len(prompt)} context-change distance={moved}")
+            assert moved >= MIN_CONTEXT_EFFECT, (
+                f"first-token log-probs barely depend on the context (moved "
+                f"{moved:.4g} for len {len(prompt)}); a wrong prefix would go "
+                "unnoticed"
+            )
+        # Determinism of the reference itself (served from its prefix cache).
+        again = _first_step(url, arch.model, prompts[-1])
+        print(f"[noise] repeat distance={_distance(refs[-1], again)}")
+    return Reference(prompts, refs, arch.hybrid)
+
+
+def _pd_distances(
+    arch: ArchCase,
+    prefill_overrides: dict[str, Any],
+    decode_overrides: dict[str, Any],
+    case: Case,
+    ref: Reference,
+) -> tuple[list[float], float]:
+    with _pd_pair(arch, prefill_overrides, decode_overrides, case) as (
+        proxy_url,
+        decode,
+    ):
+        hits_before = _external_hits(decode)
+        distances = [
+            _distance(expected, _first_step(proxy_url, arch.model, prompt))
+            for prompt, expected in zip(ref.prompts, ref.logprobs)
+        ]
+        hits = _external_hits(decode) - hits_before
+    lengths = [len(p) for p in ref.prompts]
+    print(f"[pd] {case.id} lens={lengths} distances={distances} external_hits={hits}")
+    return distances, hits
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Tests
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("case", CASES, ids=lambda c: c.id)
+def test_write_matches_direct_serve(case: Case):
+    arch = ARCHS[case.arch]
+    overrides = _arch_overrides(arch)
+    ref = _reference(arch, overrides, case)
+    distances, hits = _pd_distances(arch, overrides, overrides, case, ref)
+
+    # Every transferred token of every prompt must come from prefill.
+    assert hits == ref.expected_external_hits, (
+        f"decode reported {hits} external prefix-cache hits, expected "
+        f"{ref.expected_external_hits}; it did not use all the transferred KV"
+    )
+    lengths = [len(p) for p in ref.prompts]
+    bad = {n: d for n, d in zip(lengths, distances) if not d <= TOLERANCE}
+    assert not bad, f"P/D first-token log-probs differ from direct serve: {bad}"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("arch_name", sorted(ARCHS))
+def test_corrupted_prefill_state_is_detected(arch_name: str):
+    """Negative control: KV computed with different values must fail."""
+    arch = ARCHS[arch_name]
+    default = next(c for c in CASES if c.arch == arch_name)
+    case = Case(
+        arch_name, default.attention_backend, _DEFAULT, _DEFAULT, default.hma_off
+    )
+    overrides = _arch_overrides(arch)
+    ref = _reference(arch, overrides, case)
+    corrupted = _merge(overrides, arch.corrupt_overrides)
+    distances, hits = _pd_distances(arch, corrupted, overrides, case, ref)
+
+    assert hits == ref.expected_external_hits, (
+        "decode did not use the transferred KV; the control proves nothing"
+    )
+    assert all(d > TOLERANCE for d in distances), (
+        f"P/D outputs with wrongly computed prefill KV still matched the "
+        f"reference (distances {distances}); the comparison cannot detect "
+        "transfer corruption"
+    )

 }
 ```
 
+## Explicit pool sizing for `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`
+
+`SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` accepts an optional `num_cpu_blocks` in
+`kv_connector_extra_config`. The scheduler and every worker use this exact
+number of offload blocks instead of automatic sizing from
+`cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank` or `cpu_bytes_to_use / world_size`.
+Use the same positive integer on all ranks, chosen
+to fit the smallest per-worker capacity. This supports pipeline stages with
+different KV cache sizes without adding a collective during initialization.
+
+```json
+{
+  "kv_connector": "SimpleCPUOffloadConnector",
+  "kv_role": "kv_both",
+  "kv_connector_extra_config": {
+    "cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank": 1073741824,
+    "num_cpu_blocks": 64,
+    "lazy_offload": false
+  }
+}
+```
+
+The example count must be adjusted for the model, KV layout, and parallelism.
+The configured byte budget remains an upper bound: startup fails if the
+requested count exceeds a worker's capacity. For the `disk` backend the count
+selects disk slots and is checked against `disk_capacity_bytes`. Omitting
+`num_cpu_blocks` preserves automatic per-worker sizing. This option applies
+to `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`, separately from `OffloadingConnector` above.
+
 ## Further Reading
 
 - [vLLM blog: KV Offloading Connector](https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-01-08-kv-offloading-connector) — motivation, architecture (DMA-based async transfer), and benchmarks (TTFT and throughput).

@@ -76,6 +76,10 @@ for span in completion.weight_versions:
 
 The offsets cover the whole output, so with streamed delta outputs, collect the tokens before slicing. `/inference/v1/generate` returns the same list on each choice; see [Tokens In <> Tokens Out API](../serving/online_serving/token_in_token_out.md#weight-versions).
 
+`/v1/completions` and `/v1/chat/completions` return it on each choice when the request sets `return_weight_versions: true`. The offsets count the choice's output tokens, which `return_token_ids` returns as `token_ids`, and a streamed choice gets the list on its last chunk.
+
+An aborted request returns spans over its partial output. If you resubmit that output as part of a new prompt, the new request's spans start again at 0, so shift them by the number of tokens already generated before joining the two lists.
+
 ## Example
 
 The [async RLHF example](../../examples/rl/rlhf_async_new_apis.py) demonstrates this pattern with `vllm.AsyncLLMEngine`, NCCL weight transfer, and mid-flight pause/resume with validation.

+This backend depends on the `nccl-extensions` Python package (and its `nccl4py` dependency), which vLLM does not install. Install both against a compatible NCCL 2.30.5 or newer runtime. The backend creates its data-plane communicator through `nccl4py` and passes that communicator directly to `nccl.m2n`.
 
 The backend imports the runtime lazily, so vLLM is unaffected unless you select it.
 
 ## How It Works
 
-1. The trainer ranks and all inference workers join **one** NCCL communicator via `StatelessProcessGroup`. Trainer ranks occupy `[0, T)` and workers `[T, T + N)` — m2n meshes are contiguous rank intervals, which is exactly what vLLM's existing `rank_offset` convention produces.
-2. At the init handshake the trainer ships the full transfer plan: both meshes — one per side, shared by every parameter — then each parameter's name, dtype, shape and placement. The workers resolve the matching **destination placements** and publish them back over the shared group; the meshes themselves are declared, not negotiated.
+1. A `StatelessProcessGroup` exchanges metadata and the NCCL unique ID. The trainer ranks and all inference workers then create **one** `nccl.core.Communicator`: trainer ranks occupy `[0, T)` and workers `[T, T + N)`. The communicator is passed directly to each M2N collective.
+2. At the init handshake the trainer ships the full transfer plan: the session-wide destination mesh, then each parameter's name, dtype, shape, source mesh, and source placements. The workers resolve the matching **destination placements** and publish them over the data-plane communicator; the meshes themselves are declared, not negotiated.
 3. Each round, both sides issue one `reshard` per parameter in the same order. Every rank in the communicator participates in every reshard, so — as with the NCCL engine — the worker must be inside `update_weights` while the trainer sends. The trainer engine handles that concurrency itself.
 
 ### Destination resolution

Every rank in the communicator must be inside the same reshard, so `update_weights` has to be in flight while the trainer sends; the engine runs it on a helper thread so the trainer loop does not have to open-code that.

+Trainers with a custom producer (a Megatron export, MoE re-fusing) subclass
+`M2NWeightSource` and supply layouts explicitly. A source may yield any
+nccl4py-compatible CUDA buffer: a torch tensor, a CUDA Array Interface object,
+or a raw device pointer. vLLM keeps buffer owners alive through stream
+completion, using allocator stream tracking when the buffer provides it.
+Sources must provide buffers on the communicator's current device; nccl4py

-- A directly-resharded parameter spreads over `tp_size` destination shards, so each one is fed by fewer source shards. A parameter on the fallback path is replicated, i.e. a single destination shard fed by every source shard, so a trainer that **sharded** its parameters is still limited to 16 ranks whenever any parameter falls back — which fused parameters always do. A replicated trainer is unaffected.

+)

+WIDTH = 4  # Kimi-K3 short_conv_kernel_size
+STATE_LEN = WIDTH - 1
+HEAD_DIM = 128
+LOCAL_HEADS = 4  # per-TP-rank heads; projection = 512, packed dim = 1536
+
+
+def _fused_fn():
+    gdn = pytest.importorskip("aiter.ops.triton.gated_delta_net")
+    return gdn.causal_conv1d_split_qkv_triton_tile_fn
+
+
+def _make_inputs(seqlens, has_initial_state, seed=0, device="cuda"):
+    torch.manual_seed(seed)
+    proj = HEAD_DIM * LOCAL_HEADS
+    dim = 3 * proj
+    total = sum(seqlens)
+    n_seqs = len(seqlens)
+    # Token-major activations, as produced by the in_proj GEMM.
+    mixed_qkv = torch.randn(total, dim, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device)
+    weight = torch.randn(dim, WIDTH, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device) * 0.3
+    # More cache lines than sequences, assigned in a shuffled order. Line 0 is
+    # vLLM's null block (NULL_BLOCK_ID), which causal_conv1d_fn skips, so real
+    # sequences never map to it.
+    n_lines = n_seqs + 2
+    conv_state = torch.randn(
+        n_lines, dim, STATE_LEN, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device
+    )
+    cache_indices = (torch.randperm(n_lines - 1, device=device)[:n_seqs] + 1).to(
+        torch.int32
+    )
+    query_start_loc = torch.tensor(
+        [0] + list(torch.tensor(seqlens).cumsum(0).tolist()),
+        dtype=torch.int32,
+        device=device,
+    )
+    has_initial = torch.full(
+        (n_seqs,), has_initial_state, dtype=torch.bool, device=device
+    )
+    return mixed_qkv, weight, conv_state, cache_indices, query_start_loc, has_initial
+
+
+def _reference(
+    mixed_qkv, weight, conv_state, cache_indices, query_start_loc, has_initial
+):
+    """fp32 per-sequence depthwise causal conv + SiLU.
+
+    Returns (out[T, dim], new_conv_state).
+    """
+    x = mixed_qkv.float().t()  # (dim, T)
+    w = weight.float()
+    dim = x.shape[0]
+    out = torch.empty_like(x)
+    new_state = conv_state.float().clone()
+    qsl = query_start_loc.tolist()
+    for s in range(len(qsl) - 1):
+        start, end = qsl[s], qsl[s + 1]
+        ci = int(cache_indices[s])
+        xs = x[:, start:end]
+        if bool(has_initial[s]):
+            xin = torch.cat([conv_state[ci].float(), xs], dim=1)
+        else:
+            xin = F.pad(xs, (STATE_LEN, 0))
+        y = F.conv1d(xin.unsqueeze(0), w.unsqueeze(1), None, groups=dim)[0]
+        out[:, start:end] = F.silu(y)
+        new_state[ci] = xin[:, -STATE_LEN:]
+    return out.t(), new_state
+
+
+def _three_launch(
+    mixed_qkv, weight, conv_state, cache_indices, query_start_loc, has_initial
+):
+    """The pre-fusion KDA prefill path: one causal_conv1d_fn per projection."""
+    proj = mixed_qkv.shape[1] // 3
+    outs = []
+    for x, state, w in zip(
+        mixed_qkv.split(proj, dim=-1),
+        conv_state.split(proj, dim=-2),
+        weight.split(proj, dim=0),
+    ):

+            causal_conv1d_fn(
+                x.transpose(0, 1),
+                w,
+                None,
+                activation="silu",
+                conv_states=state,
+                has_initial_state=has_initial,
+                cache_indices=cache_indices,
+                query_start_loc=query_start_loc,
+            ).transpose(0, 1)
+        )
+    return outs
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "seqlens", [[1024], [8, 1, 300], [64, 64, 64], [513, 64, 1, 1200]]
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("has_initial_state", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("block_m", [8, 128])
+def test_fused_split_qkv_conv1d_matches_reference(seqlens, has_initial_state, block_m):
+    fused_fn = _fused_fn()
+    mixed_qkv, weight, conv_state, cache_indices, qsl, has_initial = _make_inputs(
+        seqlens, has_initial_state
+    )
+    proj = mixed_qkv.shape[1] // 3
+
+    ref_out, ref_state = _reference(
+        mixed_qkv, weight, conv_state, cache_indices, qsl, has_initial
+    )
+
+    state_3 = conv_state.clone()
+    q3, k3, v3 = _three_launch(
+        mixed_qkv, weight, state_3, cache_indices, qsl, has_initial
+    )
+
+    state_f = conv_state.clone()
+    # Exactly the call made by KimiK3DeltaAttention._forward.
+    qf, kf, vf = fused_fn(
+        mixed_qkv.transpose(0, 1),
+        weight,
+        None,
+        state_f,
+        qsl,
+        proj,
+        proj,
+        cache_indices=cache_indices,
+        has_initial_state=has_initial,
+        activation="silu",
+        block_m=block_m,
+        metadata=None,
+        preserve_input_dtype=True,
+    )
+
+    fused = torch.cat([qf, kf, vf], dim=-1)
+    assert fused.shape == mixed_qkv.shape and fused.dtype == mixed_qkv.dtype
+    assert all(t.is_contiguous() for t in (qf, kf, vf))
+
+    tol = dict(atol=2e-2, rtol=2e-2)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(fused.float(), ref_out, **tol)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(fused, torch.cat([q3, k3, v3], dim=-1), **tol)

+    # conv_state writeback: assigned lines updated, the others untouched.
+    torch.testing.assert_close(state_f.float(), ref_state, **tol)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(state_f, state_3, **tol)
+    untouched = torch.ones(conv_state.shape[0], dtype=torch.bool, device="cuda")
+    untouched[cache_indices.long()] = False
+    assert untouched[NULL_BLOCK_ID]
+    assert torch.equal(state_f[untouched], conv_state[untouched])

+def _make_vllm_config(supports_grouping: bool = False) -> MagicMock:
+    """Create a minimal mock VllmConfig for builder resolution tests.
+
+    ``supports_grouping`` selects whether the resolved model class declares
+    ``SupportsKVCacheGrouping`` (exposing a ``get_kv_cache_groups`` classmethod).
+    """
+    cfg = MagicMock()
+    cfg.model_config.supports_kv_cache_grouping = supports_grouping
+    cfg.attention_config.hisparse_config = None
+    if supports_grouping:

+            _GroupedModel,
+            "arch",
+        )
+    return cfg
+

+CUSTOM_PATH = "tests.v1.core.test_kv_cache_config_builder.CustomBuilder"

+class CustomBuilder(DefaultKVCacheConfigBuilder):

+    @classmethod

+        return []

+    @classmethod

+        from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import KVCacheGroupSpec

+        return [KVCacheGroupSpec(["a"], kv_cache_spec["a"])]

+
+from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+from vllm.utils.import_utils import resolve_obj_by_qualname

+        KVCacheSpec,
+    )

+class KVCacheConfigBuilder(ABC):
+    """Interface for platform KV cache placement.
+
+    .. note::
+        This interface is experimental and subject to change. The exact hooks
+        and the ``num_blocks`` contract may evolve before it stabilizes.
+
+    Subclasses normally inherit from ``DefaultKVCacheConfigBuilder`` and
+    override only the hooks they need. The cross-worker planning flow
+    (:func:`vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_planning.get_kv_cache_configs`) is Core-owned;
+    this builder supplies the placement decisions: how layers are split into
+    groups and how a group list is materialized into tensors for a given block
+    count. Grouping coordination lives in ``DefaultKVCacheConfigBuilder`` (a
+    model implementing :class:`~vllm.model_executor.models.interfaces.
+    SupportsKVCacheGrouping` owns its grouping there); a platform that replaces
+    the builder fully owns its own grouping.
+    """
+
+    @abstractmethod
+    def get_kv_cache_groups(
+        self,
+        vllm_config: "VllmConfig",
+        kv_cache_spec: dict[str, "KVCacheSpec"],
+    ) -> list["KVCacheGroupSpec"]:
+        """Split the given layers into KV cache groups.
+
+        Planning passes all workers' layers; profiling passes one worker's.
+        Core rejects a result that does not put each layer in exactly one group.
+
+        The default builder honors a model's
+        :class:`~vllm.model_executor.models.interfaces.SupportsKVCacheGrouping`
+        declaration here before falling back to the default grouping; a
+        platform-specific builder decides its own grouping.
+        """
+        raise NotImplementedError
+
+    @abstractmethod
+    def get_kv_cache_config_from_groups(
+        self,
+        vllm_config: "VllmConfig",
+        kv_cache_groups: list["KVCacheGroupSpec"],
+        num_blocks: int,
+    ) -> "KVCacheConfig":
+        """Materialize the groups for exactly ``num_blocks`` blocks.
+
+        Each device backing's size is ``bytes_per_block * num_blocks``. All
+        device tensors share one backing allocation unless the builder
+        overrides ``_get_pool_bytes_per_block``. Host-resident tensors, such as
+        HiSparse source storage, are excluded from the device byte accounting
+        and sized independently.
+        """
+        raise NotImplementedError
+
+    def _get_pool_bytes_per_block(
+        self,
+        vllm_config: "VllmConfig",
+        kv_cache_groups: list["KVCacheGroupSpec"],
+    ) -> int | None:
+        """Return the device bytes one block ID consumes, or ``None``.
+
+        Private and transitional; expected to go away with worker-driven
+        allocation (RFC #42449). With ``None`` (the default), Core derives the
+        value from a one-block placement with one device backing. Override it
+        only for placements with several device allocations.
+        """
+        return None
+
+
+def get_kv_cache_config_builder(
+    vllm_config: "VllmConfig",
+) -> KVCacheConfigBuilder:
+    """Resolve the builder selected by the current platform.
+
+    Resolution priority is owned by the platform hook
+    (:meth:`vllm.platforms.interface.Platform.get_kv_cache_config_builder_cls`).
+    Builders are stateless (every method takes ``vllm_config``), so a fresh
+    instance is returned per call and engines with different configs in the
+    same process always get the correct builder.
+    """
+    from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+    builder_cls = resolve_obj_by_qualname(
+        current_platform.get_kv_cache_config_builder_cls(vllm_config)
+    )
+    return builder_cls()

@@ -201,6 +201,30 @@ checkpoint's output format.
 !!! note
     With `tool_choice="auto"`, structural-tag constraints require both `VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=true` (the default) and at least one tool with `strict: true`, or a server-side floor set via `--tool-strict-level`. When these conditions are met and the selected parser supports structural tags, vLLM constrains the tool-call envelope and pins the argument schema of each tool that sets `strict: true` (or of every tool under `--tool-strict-level parameter`). Otherwise, vLLM extracts tool calls from raw text, so arguments may occasionally be malformed or violate the function's parameter schema.
 
+### Beam Models (`beam`)
+
+Beam checkpoints describe their output format with `response_template` metadata, so the `beam` parser reads it like the `hf` parser does:
+
+```bash
+vllm serve <model> \
+    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
+    --tool-call-parser beam \
+    --reasoning-parser beam
+```
+
+Unlike `hf`, the `beam` parser also constrains its output. For strict tools, required or named tool choice, and structured outputs, it derives a
+structural-tag grammar from the template. The grammar follows the template's tool call format, pins the arguments of strict tools when their
+encoding can be derived, allows a single call with `parallel_tool_calls=false`, and frames a structured output as the answer. Raw string arguments
+keep the `format` or `pattern` of their schema, as XGrammar keeps them in JSON strings, unless a match could end the value early. With
+`tool_choice="none"`, the grammar allows only reasoning and an answer, so a model that still sees the tools in its prompt cannot call them. When no
+grammar can be derived, required and named tool choice are rejected, and strict tools under `tool_choice="auto"` are left unconstrained with a
+warning.
+
+It also constrains the output of requests without strict tools, forced tool choice, or structured outputs to the template's format: tool calls with
+free arguments or an answer, or just the rest of an answer the prompt already opened. This always-on grammar needs the `xgrammar` structured
+outputs backend, the default, and is disabled with `VLLM_BEAM_ALWAYS_CONSTRAIN_OUTPUT=0`. From the message start, every `beam` grammar opens with
+reasoning that holds visible text, unless `enable_thinking` is false.
+
 ### Hermes Models (`hermes`)
 
 All Nous Research Hermes-series models newer than Hermes 2 Pro should be supported.

+use std::sync::Arc;
+
+use serde_json::{Value, json};
+use vllm_tokenizer::test_utils::TestTokenizer;
+use vllm_tokenizer::{DecodedText, Tokenizer as _};
+use xgrammar_structural_tag::ToolChoice;
+use xgrammar_structural_tag::format::Format;
+
+use super::{BeamUnifiedParser, HfPosition, build_output_grammar, other_names};
+use crate::output_grammar::test_utils::outline;

+use crate::tool::Tool;
+use crate::unified::{ResponseTemplate, UnifiedParser, UnifiedParserEvent, UnifiedParserOutput};
+
+/// The `tag_pattern` of the checkpoint of [`template`].
+const TAG_PATTERN: &str =
+    r#"<rfl:parameter name="(?P<key>[^"]+)">\n(?P<value>.*?)\n</rfl:parameter>"#;
+/// [`TAG_PATTERN`], but a value may also end where the next parameter opens.
+const LENIENT_TAG_PATTERN: &str = r#"<rfl:parameter name="(?P<key>[^"]+)">\n(?P<value>.*?)\n(?:</rfl:parameter>|(?=<rfl:parameter name="))"#;
+
+/// The Beam-1.0 `response_template`, with `tag_pattern`.
+fn template(tag_pattern: &str) -> Arc<ResponseTemplate> {
+    template_with(tag_pattern, json!("<|end|><|start|>assistant"))
+}
+
+/// [`template`] with `thinking_close` as the reasoning closer.
+fn template_with(tag_pattern: &str, thinking_close: Value) -> Arc<ResponseTemplate> {
+    let template = json!({
+        "defaults": {"role": "assistant"},
+        "start_anchor_pattern": r"<\|start\|>assistant",
+        "fields": {
+            "thinking": {
+                "open": "<|channel|>analysis<|message|>",
+                "close": thinking_close,
+                "content": "text"
+            },
+            "content": {
+                "open": "<|channel|>final<|message|>",
+                "close": ["<|return|>", "<|end|>", "<|call|>"],
+                "content": "text"
+            },
+            "tool_calls": {
+                "open_pattern": r" to=(?P<name>[^\s<]+)<\|channel\|>analysis <\|constrain\|>xml<\|message\|>",
+                "close": ["<|end|><|start|>assistant", "<|call|>"],
+                "repeats": true,
+                "content": "xml-inline",
+                "content_args": {
+                    "tag_pattern": tag_pattern,
+                    "value_parser": {"name": "text", "args": {"strip": false}}
+                },
+                "transform": {
+                    "type": "function",
+                    "function": {"name": "{name}", "arguments": "{content}"}
+                }
+            }
+        }
+    });
+    Arc::new(ResponseTemplate::from_json(&template).unwrap())
+}
+
+fn tools() -> Vec<Tool> {
+    vec![
+        Tool {
+            name: "get_weather".to_string(),
+            description: None,
+            parameters: json!({
+                "type": "object",
+                "properties": {
+                    "location": {"type": "string"},
+                    "days": {"type": "integer"},
+                    "unit": {"enum": ["c", "f"]}
+                },
+                "required": ["location"],
+                "additionalProperties": false
+            }),
+            strict: Some(true),
+            defer_loading: None,
+        },
+        Tool {
+            name: "get_time".to_string(),
+            description: None,
+            parameters: json!({
+                "type": "object",
+                "properties": {"zone": {"type": "string"}}
+            }),
+            strict: None,
+            defer_loading: None,
+        },
+    ]
+}
+
+/// A parser initialized from `prompt`, the rendered conversation.
+fn parser(prompt: &str) -> BeamUnifiedParser {
+    parser_with(TAG_PATTERN, prompt)
+}
+
+fn parser_with(tag_pattern: &str, prompt: &str) -> BeamUnifiedParser {
+    let tokenizer = Arc::new(TestTokenizer::new());
+    let prompt_ids = tokenizer.encode(prompt, false).unwrap();
+    let mut parser = BeamUnifiedParser::new(template(tag_pattern), &tools(), tokenizer);
+    parser.initialize(&prompt_ids).unwrap();
+    parser
+}
+
+const PROMPT: &str = "<|start|>user<|message|>Weather in Paris?<|end|><|start|>assistant";
+
+fn grammar(position: HfPosition, tool_choice: ToolChoice, parallel: bool) -> Option<String> {
+    grammar_with(position, &tools(), tool_choice, parallel, false, false)
+}
+
+fn grammar_with(
+    position: HfPosition,
+    tools: &[Tool],
+    tool_choice: ToolChoice,
+    parallel: bool,
+    always_constrain: bool,
+    lenient: bool,
+) -> Option<String> {
+    let ctx = OutputGrammarContext {
+        tools,
+        tool_choice: &tool_choice,
+        tool_strict_level: ToolStrictLevel::Auto,
+        parallel_tool_calls: parallel,
+        answer: None,

+    grammar_in(position, &ctx, always_constrain, lenient)
+}
+
+fn grammar_in(

+    let grammar = build_output_grammar(

+        always_constrain,
+        lenient,
+        template(TAG_PATTERN).reasoning_closers(),
+    )
+    .unwrap()?;
+    assert_eq!(grammar.coverage, GrammarCoverage::FromTokenZero);
+    Some(outline(&grammar.format))

+fn constrained_grammar(
+    position: HfPosition,
+    tool_choice: ToolChoice,
+    answer: Format,
+    always_constrain: bool,
+) -> Option<String> {
+    let tools = tools();
+    let ctx = OutputGrammarContext {
+        tools: &tools,
+        tool_choice: &tool_choice,
+        tool_strict_level: ToolStrictLevel::Auto,
+        parallel_tool_calls: true,
+        answer: Some(&answer),
+    };
+    grammar_in(position, &ctx, always_constrain, false)
+}

+    assert_eq!(
+        position("<|channel|>analysis<|message|>Let me"),

+    // The reasoning closer ends with the anchor, so the next message starts.

+/// Parse `output` after the prompt under `tag_pattern`, returning the calls as
+/// `(name, arguments)`.
+fn calls(tag_pattern: &str, output: &str) -> Vec<(String, Value)> {
+    let mut parser = parser_with(tag_pattern, PROMPT);
+    let mut events = UnifiedParserOutput::default();
+    parser.parse_into(DecodedText::unattributed(output), &mut events).unwrap();
+    events.append(parser.finish().unwrap());
+    let mut calls: Vec<(String, String)> = Vec::new();
+    for event in events.events {
+        if let UnifiedParserEvent::ToolCall(delta) = event {
+            if let Some(name) = delta.name {
+                calls.push((name, String::new()));
+            }
+            calls.last_mut().unwrap().1.push_str(&delta.arguments);
+        }
+    }
+    calls
+        .into_iter()
+        .map(|(name, arguments)| (name, serde_json::from_str(&arguments).unwrap()))
+        .collect()
+}

+def _named_tool(request: ChatCompletionRequest | ResponsesRequest) -> str:
+    choice = request.tool_choice
+    if isinstance(choice, ToolChoiceFunction):
+        return choice.name
+    return cast(ChatCompletionNamedToolChoiceParam, choice).function.name
+
+
+def _starts_message(template: ResponseTemplate, prefix: str) -> bool:
+    """Whether output after `prefix` starts the assistant message."""
+    ends = [match.end() for match in template.start_anchor_re.finditer(prefix)]
+    return bool(ends) and ends[-1] == len(prefix)
+
+
+def _open_field(template: ResponseTemplate, prefix: str) -> str | None:
+    """The field that `prefix` leaves open with its explicit opener, if any."""
+    field = None
+    for event in ResponseParser(template, prefix=prefix).initial_events:
+        if event["type"] == "region_open" and event["end"] > event["start"]:
+            field = event["field"]
+        elif event["type"] in {"region_close", "region_malformed"}:
+            field = None
+    return field
+
+
+class BeamReasoningParser(ResponseTemplateReasoningParser):
+    """Selects `BeamParser` as the reasoning parser."""
+
+    @classmethod
+    def unified_parser_cls(cls) -> type[ResponseTemplateParser]:
+        return BeamParser
+
+    @property

+        if literal := super().reasoning_start_str:
+            return literal
+        thinking = self.response_template.fields.get(THINKING_FIELD)
+        if thinking is None:
+            return None
+        openers = _openers(thinking, message_start_anchors(self.response_template))
+        if not openers:
+            return None
+        # Budget tracking needs one marker for both a prompt continuation
+        # and a complete assistant message in the checkpoint's pattern.
+        marker = min(openers, key=len)
+        return marker if all(opener.endswith(marker) for opener in openers) else None
+
+

+    """Selects `BeamParser` as the tool parser."""
+
+    @classmethod
+    def unified_parser_cls(cls) -> type[ResponseTemplateParser]:
+        return BeamParser
+
+
+class BeamParser(ResponseTemplateParser):
+    """Parse Beam output with the checkpoint's `response_template` metadata,
+    and constrain it with a grammar derived from that template."""
+
+    reasoning_parser_cls = BeamReasoningParser
+    tool_parser_cls = BeamToolParser

+    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs) -> None:

+        # reasoning, unless the request turns thinking off.

+            chat_template_kwargs.get("enable_thinking", True)

+    def _template_tag(

+        fields = self.response_template.fields
+        named = _is_named_tool_choice(request)

+            self._tool_parser is not None
+            and bool(request.tools)

+        forced = tools_enabled and (request.tool_choice == "required" or named)

+        # model from calling them.
+        tools_forbidden = (
+            bool(request.tools)
+            and request.tool_choice == "none"
+            and TOOL_FIELD in fields

+            strict_level = self.tool_strict_level
+            if strict_level is None:
+                strict_level = self._tool_parser.default_tool_strict_level
+            constrained_tools = resolve_tool_strictness(
+                request.tools or [], request.tool_choice, strict_level
+            )
+        output = request.extract_structured_outputs()
+        if forced and output is not None:
+            logger.warning_once(
+                "structured outputs are ignored because tool_choice forces tool call."
+            )
+            output = None
+        answer = fields.get(CONTENT_FIELD)
+        if output is not None and (
+            output.structural_tag is not None
+            or answer is None
+            or answer.open_re is None
+            or not _xgrammar_supports(output)
+        ):
+            if constrained_tools is not None:
+                logger.warning_once(
+                    "response_template parsing cannot enforce strict tools "
+                    "alongside this structured output."
+                )
+            return None
+        # Without a tool or structured output constraint, the output still
+        # follows the template.
+        always_constrain = envs.VLLM_BEAM_ALWAYS_CONSTRAIN_OUTPUT and not forced
+        if (
+            constrained_tools is None
+            and output is None
+            and not tools_forbidden
+            and not always_constrain
+        ):
+            return None
+
+        # Inside an open answer, only the always-on grammar applies, finishing a
+        # free answer. Inside open reasoning, the grammar needs the reasoning
+        # gate to defer it to the reasoning's end.
+        open_field = _open_field(self.response_template, self._prefix)
+        reasoning_gated = (
+            self._reasoning_parser is not None and request.include_reasoning
+        )
+        tag = None
+        if open_field == CONTENT_FIELD:
+            if always_constrain and output is None:
+                tag = answer_rest_structural_tag(fields[CONTENT_FIELD])
+        elif open_field != THINKING_FIELD or reasoning_gated:
+            functions = []
+            if tools_enabled:
+                tools = _as_tool_dicts(constrained_tools or request.tools)
+                functions = [tool.get("function", tool) for tool in tools]
+            if named:
+                name = _named_tool(request)
+                functions = [f for f in functions if f.get("name") == name]
+            answer_format = (
+                None if output is None else structured_outputs_to_format(output)
+            )
+            try:
+                tag = tool_call_structural_tag(
+                    fields.get(TOOL_FIELD),
+                    functions,
+                    parallel_tool_calls=(
+                        not named and request.parallel_tool_calls is not False
+                    ),
+                    thinking=fields.get(THINKING_FIELD),
+                    answer=None if forced else answer,
+                    answer_format=(
+                        None if answer_format is None else answer_format.model_dump()
+                    ),
+                    message_start=(
+                        message_start_anchors(self.response_template)
+                        if message_start
+                        else None
+                    ),
+                    requires_reasoning=self._requires_reasoning,
+                    # Beam drifts from schemas the grammar does not enforce,
+                    # and also writes arguments sorted by name.
+                    sorted_arguments=True,
+                    strict_arguments=True,
+                )
+            except ValueError as exc:
+                raise VLLMValidationError(str(exc), parameter="tools") from exc
+        if tag is None and forced:
+            kind = "named" if named else "required"
+            raise VLLMValidationError(
+                f"response_template parsing cannot guarantee {kind} tool choice "
+                "for this request",
+                parameter="tool_choice",
+            )
+        if tag is None and constrained_tools is not None:
+            logger.warning_once(
+                "response_template parsing cannot enforce strict tools for this "
+                "request."
+            )
+        return tag

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""ROCm Kimi-K3 KDA metadata under adaptive verification.
+
+Adaptive verification splits the draft budget evenly on the host, then trims
+each verify request on device. The KDA spec path must therefore plan from the
+device offsets, never from host lengths that merely look uniform.
+"""
+
+import torch
+
+from tests.v1.attention.utils import (
+    BatchSpec,
+    create_common_attn_metadata,
+    create_vllm_config,
+)
+from vllm.config import SpeculativeConfig
+from vllm.config.compilation import CUDAGraphMode
+from vllm.models.kimi_k3.amd.kda_metadata import (
+    KimiK3ROCmKDABackend,
+    KimiK3ROCmKDAMetadataBuilder,
+)
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import MambaSpec
+
+BLOCK_SIZE = 16
+DEVICE = torch.device("cpu")
+NUM_SPEC = 3
+
+
+def _config(adaptive: bool):
+    vllm_config = create_vllm_config(
+        model_name="Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B",
+        block_size=BLOCK_SIZE,
+    )
+    vllm_config.compilation_config.cudagraph_mode = CUDAGraphMode.FULL_AND_PIECEWISE
+    vllm_config.speculative_config = SpeculativeConfig(
+        method="ngram",
+        num_speculative_tokens=NUM_SPEC,
+        enable_adaptive_verification=adaptive,
+    )
+    vllm_config.cache_config.mamba_cache_mode = "none"
+    return vllm_config
+
+
+def _spec() -> MambaSpec:
+    return MambaSpec(
+        block_size=BLOCK_SIZE,
+        shapes=((16, 64),),
+        dtypes=(torch.float16,),
+        num_speculative_blocks=NUM_SPEC,
+    )
+
+
+def _builder(adaptive: bool) -> KimiK3ROCmKDAMetadataBuilder:
+    return KimiK3ROCmKDAMetadataBuilder(
+        kv_cache_spec=_spec(),
+        layer_names=["layer.0"],
+        vllm_config=_config(adaptive),
+        device=DEVICE,
+    )
+
+
+def _trimmed_verify_batch(builder: KimiK3ROCmKDAMetadataBuilder):
+    """Host sees [3, 3]; the device was trimmed to [4, 2] (same total)."""
+    batch = BatchSpec(seq_lens=[64, 64], query_lens=[4, 2])
+    common = create_common_attn_metadata(
+        batch, BLOCK_SIZE, DEVICE, arange_block_indices=True
+    )
+    common = common.replace(
+        query_start_loc_cpu=torch.tensor([0, 3, 6], dtype=torch.int32)
+    )
+    accepted = torch.ones(2, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
+    num_decode_draft_tokens_cpu = torch.tensor([NUM_SPEC, NUM_SPEC], dtype=torch.int32)
+    return builder.build(0, common, accepted, num_decode_draft_tokens_cpu)
+
+
+def test_adaptive_verification_plans_from_device_offsets():
+    """Equal host lengths would select the fixed-length recurrent kernel,
+    which places sequence i at i * L and ignores the device cu_seqlens."""
+    assert KimiK3ROCmKDABackend.supports_device_cpu_query_lens_mismatch()
+    bound = KimiK3ROCmKDAMetadataBuilder.get_varlen_cudagraph_max_query_len
+    assert bound(_config(adaptive=True), _spec()) == NUM_SPEC + 1
+    assert bound(_config(adaptive=False), _spec()) is None
+
+    meta = _trimmed_verify_batch(_builder(adaptive=True))
+    assert meta.num_spec_decodes == 2
+    assert meta.uniform_spec_sequence_length is None
+    assert torch.equal(
+        meta.spec_query_start_loc.cpu(), torch.tensor([0, 4, 6], dtype=torch.int32)
+    )
+    # Without adaptive verification the host lengths are exact and kept.
+    meta = _trimmed_verify_batch(_builder(adaptive=False))
+    assert meta.uniform_spec_sequence_length == 3
